# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

## Current owner priorities — product index, reusable shipping knowledge, progressive disclosure (2026-10-12)

The owner has reviewed the updated website and still finds it very cluttered. The home page must become an overview index of products, with the comparison workflow on a dedicated product page. The owner also expects obvious browser-visible shipping rules, such as Pucks free shipping above ₪100, to be found systematically and actually used by the site. These priorities replace the earlier instruction to repeat the initial shipping investigation first in every fresh iteration. The first Pucks/CoffeeMan/Coffee4U browser investigation is already evidenced in iterations 3-67 through 3-72. Use that evidence; fresh browser work should address a specific missing, contradictory or stale condition. Do not spend whole iterations reproducing unchanged amounts while the requested product/UI work waits.

Shurik implements all code, assets, tests and documentation. The overseer only changes this brief and reviews results. Keep the Canton Zürich design direction, Inter, palette and Crema e Gusto-only active scope below.

### 1. Make the home page a product overview index

- The canonical home route must show a clean product index, not the full vendor comparison board. Render its cards from the active catalog. Today that means **one real card: Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**. Design the structure to support additional products later, but do not add or reactivate Oro, Rossa, Suerte, other product lines, fabricated offerings or placeholder cards. Crema e Gusto blend variants and multipacks stay separate inside its comparison.
- Each product card links to a real, directly loadable product-detail URL. The home page needs only product identity, a concise useful summary and a clear way to open the comparison. If a summary price is shown, its quantity, destination, freshness and conditional nature must be understandable; do not mix different cart sizes or variants into a misleading "from" price.
- The product page identifies the coffee and provides the quantity/locality/variant/delivery controls and offers. Provide a clear "All products" way back. Preserve shareable selection state and handle existing product/query links, including retired-line fallbacks, without losing quantity, locality or variant. Keep existing read-only APIs and deterministic refresh behavior working.
- The home title is "Attention shoppers" without a period. The product-detail heading should name the product, e.g. "Lavazza Crema e Gusto", with compact site branding. Do not reproduce a giant branding hero or comparison explanation on both pages.

### 2. Generalize browser shipping research and deterministic shipping policies

- Reuse the real Chrome/ChromeDriver helper, but build a reusable research workflow with vendor-specific navigation recipes and a common evidence output. It must navigate the product/cart/estimator, select the actual delivery method, set whole-pack quantities and permitted locality/postcode, wait for recalculation, and compare displayed item subtotal, shipping and final total. A subtotal displayed before choosing a method is not a delivered quote: the Pucks cart only adds its ₪30 after the delivery card is selected.
- Research a meaningful cart matrix per SKU/variant/pack/service/destination: normal quantities plus below/above a displayed free-shipping threshold. Capture the threshold language, exclusions, minimum order, fees, delivery methods, locality restrictions, any discount and the exact blocker if a quote requires personal details. Keep the anonymous-cart/locality permission and the no-order/payment/login/account/street-address/bot-bypass restrictions below. Sanitize all URLs and output so cart/session/cookie/token values never enter public records.
- Introduce a common, validated shipping-evidence/policy representation and evaluator used by every adapter/quote: distinguish published rules, observed conditional cart quotes and unknown/inconsistent rules. Preserve service, eligible product/SKU/variant/pack, quantity or weight/subtotal scope, destination scope, currency, amount or threshold rule, source, observed/review time and certainty. Per-vendor recipes may differ; common policy interpretation, arithmetic, evidence storage and validation should be shared. Do not keep accumulating unrelated hard-coded adapter strings as the only shipping model.
- Pucks is the concrete acceptance case: the rendered estimator established **₪30 home delivery and free shipping above the stated ₪100 item subtotal**, including 2 × 250 g = ₪60 + ₪30 = ₪90 and 4 × 250 g = ₪120 with free delivery to Tel Aviv / 6100000. Apply the rule to eligible current offers and show the free-shipping condition in the appropriate delivery details. Preserve the threshold comparison/exclusions actually established by the vendor; do not silently turn "above" into "at least" without checking the boundary semantics. Coverage remains qualified beyond the destinations tested.
- CoffeeMan demonstrates why a single global threshold is insufficient: the ₪240 eight-pack cart still charged ₪20 while some single-pack/two-four-pack carts showed free shipping; the small single/four-pack carts showed a ₪15 distribution-center alternative. Store conditional evidence at its actual scope, and keep unverified rules unresolved. Do not infer a nationwide/free-over-X rule from one cart or flatten variant/pack distinctions. Scoped discounts and alternatives must not silently change the ranked courier amount beyond their verified applicability.
- **Fix the known-knowledge/old-store gap.** The latest recorded production probes still had old shipping unknowns even after the policies were established and deployed. Implement a safe versioned policy resolution/enrichment or migration so newly validated shipping knowledge can apply to matching persisted offers promptly, without waiting hours for the next item refresh. Choose the mechanism within the existing Worker architecture; keep it deterministic, bounded and compatible with stored data. Preserve the item's actual price/stock observation time and shipping evidence's own time; applying a newer shipping rule must not claim a fresh vendor price/stock check or advance lastRefreshAt. Do not fabricate an item price, force a Cloudflare refresh through admin tools, or turn a policy into an unconditional coverage guarantee. Test an old persisted Pucks offer with unknown shipping gaining the evidenced rule after a policy update.
- The public Worker must continue to work without the coding loop or a browser open. It should consume validated policy data and bounded public sources; browser research is development/research tooling, not an LLM/browser session triggered by visitor traffic. Document how policy evidence is rechecked or becomes stale, and keep unresolved shipping explicit.

### 3. Use substantial progressive disclosure on the product page

The goal is a short decision flow, not merely smaller versions of every existing paragraph.

- Default view: compact product identity/selection, an easy quantity and locality change, and the best eligible offer with vendor, accurate purchased pack/grams, item subtotal, **named delivery method and charge**, delivered total, stock and a short necessary conditional/unknown/stale warning. On 390 × 844, the actual money values and method must be visible in the initial viewport; a card whose top edge begins at y=829 does not satisfy this. Achieve this by prioritizing content, not tiny text or hiding essential uncertainty.
- Use a clear "Compare other offers" disclosure or a compact comparison preview. Other blend variants remain discoverable through a concise affordance, including the unstated-variant Coffee4U listing; do not silently merge it into Classico. Keep relevant controls accessible, with secondary configuration in a clearly labelled section/drawer when useful.
- Delivery alternatives, pickup locations/fees, free-shipping conditions, detailed coverage and terms belong under "Delivery options" / "Offer details". Self-pickup stays separate from delivered ranking and should be collapsed by default rather than three always-expanded repeated rows. Show a brief coverage qualification beside a conditional total, with the full prose inside details.
- Price history, parser/source provenance, FX, refresh diagnostics and detailed timestamps are secondary disclosures. Retain concise visible stale/failure/unknown warnings when they change a shopping decision. Hide empty "missing information" sections and remove repeated teaching copy, duplicate headings, repeated product restrictions and the same caveat printed several times.
- Use the Canton Zürich native disclosure/accordion/service patterns and the selected blue/soft-blue scheme. Keep semantic stock/uncertainty colors and text labels, keyboard/focus behavior, RTL handling and readable type. Opening one useful detail must not require reading through unrelated diagnostics.
- Fix the independently observed pickup-name regression: the saved after-1440/after-390 screenshots and passing QA output contained **"[object HTMLSpanElement]"** instead of the vendor. Current renderPickupSection passes bidi(quote.vendor.name), a DOM node, as an el() text attribute. Shurik fixes the node/text handling and adds a meaningful rendered check for the actual vendor names and the absence of object-string artifacts.
- The current shippingServiceText() returns a certainty label rather than a delivery-method name. Render the actual method (home courier / distribution-center or pickup-point delivery / self-pickup) separately from certainty, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys.

### Acceptance for this owner correction

Checkpoint useful progress, then complete all three outcomes: real home index + reachable product page, reusable shipping research/policy resolution with the Pucks old-store case, and progressive disclosure that exposes the core decision values on the first mobile screen. Update browser QA to exercise the home-to-product navigation, directly loaded/shareable product URLs, opening/closing disclosures, method/quantity/destination changes, named vendors, honest unknowns and the money values' actual visibility. Preserve catalog exclusions, pack arithmetic, conditional coverage, scheduled refresh/backoff and last-known-good storage.

Run npm run verify and relevant offline/local-live browser QA after changes; inspect readable desktop/mobile viewport screenshots of both pages when image tools support them. The current pi-durable read tool rejects images: report that limitation accurately; character/pixel maps are only coarse evidence and cannot establish that text is correct. Save sanitized screenshots for overseer review and corroborate labels/arithmetic with DOM/API evidence. Keep docs/DESIGN.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/SOURCES.md and docs/STATUS.md aligned with the final implementation. Do not let waiting for a future production cron tick replace this work, and do not claim the correction is live solely because code or a policy was committed.

## Owner design direction — Canton Zürich design system (2026-10-12)

Use **the Canton Zürich design system specifically** for the shopping-page redesign. This owner direction supersedes the earlier generic Swiss transport-signage reference in this prompt and docs/DESIGN.md. Use its web-application/service patterns to make a compact shopping tool, with consistent alignment, responsive grids, flat surfaces, clear type hierarchy and concise disclosures. Keep the product identity our own; no cantonal crest, government wordmark or implied affiliation.

Read the official primary references before implementing:
- Design system: https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html
- Colors: https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/farben.html
- Typography: https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/typografie.html
- Layout/grid: https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/layout-und-raster.html

Chosen highlight scheme:
- **Blue theme:** official Blau `#0070B4`, paired with Softblau `#EDF5FA`. Use this sparingly for the selected shopping context and the clearly labelled best known delivered offer, with a blue rule or soft-blue panel. Do not paint arbitrary vendor names different colors or use green to mean cheapest.
- **Neutral structure:** white, black `#000000`, secondary text `#666666`, subtle surfaces `#F7F7F7` and dividers `#CCCCCC`. Follow the system's grey/black buttons and links; links must remain identifiable. Avoid decorative multicolor badges.
- **Stock:** official green `#1A7F1F` with `#EBF6EB` for verified in-stock labels; official red `#D93C1A` on white for unavailable/error labels.
- **Uncertainty:** amber text `#8A4B00` on `#FFF4E5` for unknown shipping, unconfirmed coverage and stale evidence. These amber tokens are our deliberate shopping-specific extension, not official Canton Zürich tokens; they preserve the owner's existing uncertainty semantics.
- Official Cyan `#009EE0` can mark active controls as a non-text indicator. It is not suitable for small text on white; use `#0070B4` for a consistently visible focus outline instead. Always retain written status labels and a distinct selected state.

Use **Inter**, explicitly supported by the official web-app typography guidance, with its recommended font features `ss07`, `ss08`, `cv03`, `cv04`, `cv10`; use a neutral system fallback and tabular numerals for prices. If adding a font, use an openly licensed self-hosted asset. Keep headings left aligned and compact: the home title must read "Attention shoppers" without a trailing period; the dedicated product page names the product and keeps the offer decision values near the top.

Update docs/DESIGN.md to this concrete design direction as part of your implementation. This is a usability redesign, not just recoloring: retain the shipping/subtotal/delivered-total grouping and mobile reflow requirements below. Validate actual rendered foreground/background contrast (at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for essential UI/focus), keyboard use, and readable desktop/mobile screenshots. Record the visual review and relevant checks. The current owner priorities above govern the home index, dedicated product page, progressive disclosure and generalized shipping workflow. Shurik owns all code, assets and tests.

## Current owner priority — shopping usability and shipping (2026-10-12)

The owner reviewed the site and finds it cluttered while still missing useful shipping information. Prioritize the following work now, before further status-label features, repeated unchanged vendor hunts or documentation-only iterations. The earlier Crema e Gusto-only correction remains mandatory.

1. **Simplify the shopping page.** Apply the Canton Zürich design direction above, and make the first screen answer: what coffee/pack am I buying, how much is the item subtotal, what shipping service and charge apply, and what delivered total can actually be established for this destination? Remove the trailing period from the home heading: use "Attention shoppers", not "Attention shoppers."; name the product in its dedicated detail heading. Reduce the oversized hero and repeated explanatory copy. Keep stock, quantity, destination and variant controls useful and visible.
2. **Keep decision information in view.** Item subtotal, shipping charge/service and delivered total must be visible together without sideways scrolling on desktop. On mobile use readable offer cards or an equally clear layout with those values together, rather than a wide spreadsheet. Move repeated pickup rows, duplicated coverage paragraphs, previous-check/debug metadata, FX/run/vendor diagnostics and detailed provenance into optional details where appropriate. Do not reduce clutter by concealing unknown shipping or removing offers. Avoid repeating the same shipping caveat several times on one offer.
3. **Present all existing shipping evidence clearly.** Show published rates, available delivery methods (courier, pickup point, self-pickup), coverage restrictions and any observed threshold/minimum/delivery time with short labels and accessible evidence. Unknown charges must say "Shipping not published" and explain what is needed; never substitute zero. A published rate with unconfirmed destination coverage must not be presented as guaranteed delivery or a fully confirmed checkout total. Preserve variant-specific ranking, but make the unstated-variant Coffee4U offer and its published shipping methods easy to discover without guessing which control reveals it. Do not merge it into Classico.
4. **Use an actual interactive browser for shipping research.** The runner already has real Google Chrome + ChromeDriver, used by scripts/browser-qa.mjs, and the configured DeepSeek model's pinned metadata supports image input. Use that browser beyond predetermined QA assertions: navigate the existing vendors' product, shipping/terms and public cart/estimator pages; allow JavaScript to render; inspect delivery controls and publicly displayed rates for the relevant quantity and Israeli locality/postcode. A temporary anonymous cart containing the target coffee is permitted solely to inspect a public shipping estimator. Do not submit an order, payment, login, account creation or a real street address; do not bypass bot challenges or access controls. Do not commit cart/session/cookie details. The initial Pucks/CoffeeMan quotes have already been established; reuse the recorded evidence through the generalized policy workflow above. Target fresh browser research at missing, contradictory or stale conditions and record the actual blocker when the public flow cannot establish one. Keep the public Worker deterministic; this browser is a research/development tool, not an LLM dependency in the runtime.
5. **Judge the page visually.** Open the current production page and revised desktop/mobile pages in Chrome, capture before/after screenshots, and actually inspect their image content through a supported image/read tool. Use viewport or section screenshots at readable resolution instead of shrinking an entire long page until the text is illegible. If image input is not working in the available tools, report that concrete limitation rather than claiming visual review. Review hierarchy, whitespace, density, duplicate labels and how easily a shopper finds shipping and a total. A passing DOM checklist alone is insufficient.
6. **Fix concrete observed UX defects.** The overseer's render of main at b75e296 (recorded fixtures, not a new live source observation) had a 2289 px comparison table inside a 1325 px container at 1440 px desktop width: "Delivered total" began at x=1641, offscreen. The 390 px mobile page was about 5491 px tall for five offers, with repeated shipping caveats and three separate pickup rows. The per-kilogram winner described a four-by-250 g multipack as "1 × 250 g"; fix all pack/quantity labels so multipack contents and purchased grams are accurate. These are examples to verify and improve, not a prescribed implementation.
7. **Validate meaningful outcomes and checkpoint useful progress.** Update browser QA to check the redesigned shopping behavior instead of requiring every old diagnostic label to remain permanently visible. Preserve shipping math, honest unknowns, quantity/pack rounding, variants, stock, scheduled refreshes and storage. Run npm run verify and relevant browser QA after substantive changes, then record concise results, screenshot review findings and shipping research evidence in docs/STATUS.md. Do not let waiting for a future cron tick block this UX/shipping work. Continue only within Crema e Gusto; leave the model/provider/reasoning, Worker target and Cloudflare administration rules unchanged.

Shurik implements this work. The overseer steers the prompt and reviews results; it does not publish competing application-code edits.

## Owner correction — 2026-10-12

This is the current task priority and supersedes the older multi-product plans in repository docs and session history.

1. Align the production Cloudflare Worker name with `attention-shoppers` in Wrangler and all deployment/project instructions. The owner reports the site is already deployed at https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev. Update the documented status accordingly, while distinguishing that report from independently verified production refreshes.

6. After these corrections, improve only Crema e Gusto vendor coverage, shipping evidence, freshness and comparison quality. Adding another product line requires an explicit new owner instruction.

Shurik is responsible for implementation, tests and code fixes. The overseer changes the loop prompt, checks its progress and controls the loop; it does not implement parallel code changes. Re-read the current PROMPT.md and AGENTS.md before starting each iteration, and treat this owner correction as the active objective.

Build a public, self-updating website on Cloudflare Workers that finds ways to order products online for delivery in Israel and compares the item price plus shipping. Track only Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee; make it straightforward to add vendors carrying this product. Do not expand into other product lines. This is a working shopping tool, not a marketing landing page.

The owner chose Shurik v1 and explicitly switched the coding loop to opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash at its maximum supported reasoning, max, after repeated Step 5 endpoint errors. Use concrete milestones, short feedback cycles and verifiable evidence. This specific model switch is authorized; do not change provider/model or add another fallback without the owner's instruction. The coding loop writes directly to main. The owner reports deployment at https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev. The production Worker name is attention-shoppers; main pushes are intended to auto-deploy through Cloudflare Workers Builds. Shurik has no Cloudflare credentials, API access or deployment tools. All development and integration validation must work locally. Read AGENTS.md and the design/architecture docs.

## Required shopping behavior

1. Discover and validate several actual vendor listings. Use public vendor APIs or public product pages and permitted structured data. Record source URLs, retrieval dates and what each source establishes. Prefer vendors serving Israel; international vendors qualify only when delivery to Israel is evidenced.
2. Match the actual product: Lavazza, Crema e Gusto, ground coffee in a vacuum brick. Record grams, pack count and blend variant. Do not confuse beans, capsules, pods or similarly named products. Classico, Forte and other variants must remain separate. A typical 250 g pack is a starting hypothesis, not a verified fact for every listing.

Different pack sizes and multipacks should normalize to delivered ILS per kilogram and the actual checkout total. Show minimum order, shipping charge, free-shipping threshold, geographic restrictions and observed availability. Keep pickup separate from delivery.
4. Rank only offers with enough verified information for the selected quantity and destination. Item price + shipping + mandatory fees is the comparison total. Unknown shipping, import charges or FX conversion must not become zero. Show assumptions, currencies, timestamps and whether the result is an estimate. Do not claim to know personalized checkout prices. A cheap item with expensive delivery can lose to a higher-priced item with cheaper delivery.

Stale and unrankable offers remain visible with honest labels. Do not label a price-only scrape as proof of stock.

## Self-updating runtime

Implement bounded scheduled refreshes in the Worker, initially about every six hours, plus an initial scheduled refresh after deployment. Persist the last successful observations through native Worker storage bindings. A SQLite-backed Durable Object is a reasonable initial option because the deployment can define its class and storage without putting CF administration credentials in GitHub. # Project status

Stage: **Crema e Gusto scope enforced; the Canton Zürich shopping board, the browser-researched
shipping rates and the redesigned UI validated locally (99/99 tests, 82/82 offline and 78/78 live browser
checks); production serves the redesigned assets, the first production cron tick was observed at
18:17:55 UTC (0 requests, exactly as expected) and its stored observations pick up the researched rates
at the 00:17 UTC cron tick; a fresh 19:07-19:16 UTC browser session independently reproduced all three
vendors' rendered shipping quotes; iteration 3-70 labels cart-observed rates as conditional checkout
rates and halves the pickup-row space; iteration 3-71 resolved the CoffeeMan single/4-pack delivery
methods in a fresh anonymous cart (₪25 courier / ₪15 distribution-center for 0.5-1 kg carts), recorded
the cart-dependent free-delivery behavior without inventing a threshold, and surfaced the adapter
shipping terms in the offer disclosure.**
The Worker implements the self-updating board for exactly one product line — **Lavazza Crema e Gusto
vacuum-packed ground coffee** — with three independent Israeli vendor adapters and five observed
listings. The owner reports the site deployed at
**https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev** with Worker name `attention-shoppers` and main-push
auto-deploy through Cloudflare Workers Builds. On 2026-10-12 15:51-15:54 UTC the coding loop independently
verified the public site from the runner with read-only GETs (no Cloudflare credentials, no admin API, no
deploy): `/health`, `/api/status`, `/api/catalog` and `/api/board` answered HTTP 200, the catalog exposed
exactly one product, the store held five observations, and the probe's first `/health` GET started the
site's documented initial refresh, which completed at 15:52:12.546 UTC and advanced `lastRefreshAt`. That
probe also exposed the gap iteration 3-61 fixes: before it, production had five saved observations and
vendor successes from 13:34/13:46 UTC but `lastRefreshAt` was null (an interrupted run), so the board read
as never refreshed even though its offers were recent. Outstanding production checks are listed below.
After the supervisor published the 3-61 commits, a second read-only probe at 16:17-16:18 UTC found
`/health` serving `lastObservationAt` — a field only the 3-61 code emits — so the pushed build is live in
production and the main-push Workers Builds path is independently verified from the runner; the Durable
Object store persisted across the deploy with the same refresh timestamps, and headless-Chrome browser QA
driven against the production URL passed **53/53** checks with zero console errors. Iteration 3-59 kept the single-product scope and improved freshness honesty and
comparison quality: the board's `lastRefreshAt` now advances only when at least one vendor actually saved
an observation (an FX-only or empty run can no longer look freshly checked), every offer stores one
step of previous-check evidence so the UI shows the unit-price change since the last successful check in
ILS (or explains why the comparison is impossible), and the cheapest per-kilogram offer is called out
when it differs from the cheapest delivered total. Iteration 3-60 adds written shipping-certainty labels
next to every ranked rate, a `+₪ vs best` line on each comparison row, an approximate next-source-check
time in the board footer, and records the fresh vendor-coverage probes (Zap, FreshCafe, Brioso) that
found no fourth vendor carrying the tracked ground listing. Iteration 3-61 adds a board-freshness fallback
so an interrupted refresh with fresh saved observations is not reported as never refreshed, and records the
first independently verified production refresh from the runner. Iteration 3-62 fixed a cron phase-lock in
that runtime: because a vendor's stored due time is `run time + 6 h` while the cron fires at fixed clock
times, a tick landing seconds early skipped every vendor and would silently drift the cadence to twelve
hours (with the board reporting stale for hours between runs). Successful vendors now count as due up to
15 minutes early; failure backoff stays strict. The fix is locally verified (**90/90** tests, fixture
refresh, **57/57** offline browser checks) and waits for the next main-push deployment. Iteration 3-63
added the repeatable read-only production probe and the multi-tick cron cadence test, and re-verified the
live sources at 16:50-16:53 UTC. Iteration 3-64 finished and verified the **failed-attempt disclosure**
that session 3-63 saved just before its timeout: when a vendor check fails, the attempt time and reason
are stamped on that offer's last successful observation row, so the board keeps ranking the last known
good price and stock while saying the most recent attempt failed instead of presenting the row as freshly
re-checked. Verified locally with **94/94** `node:test` cases, `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (80.12 KiB /
gzip 20.60 KiB), the fixture refresh (6 bounded requests, five offers), a live `check:sources` pass at
17:22 UTC (five listings unchanged), a live `cron:local -- --fresh` pass at 17:24 UTC (6 requests, five
offers, USD 3.078), **63/63** offline and **59/59** live browser checks including six new failed-attempt
checks. The same 3-64 code is live in production: read-only GETs at 17:31 UTC found the production board
quotes carrying `lastAttemptFailed`/`lastError` and the deployed `app.js` containing the failed-attempt
labels, and live browser QA against the production URL passed **59/59** with zero console errors.

The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa, Suerte and every other Lavazza
product line. They are no longer catalog entries, fetch targets or UI options. Their names survive only
as tombstones in `src/catalog.js` (so old links and historical pages are refused with an explicit reason)
and as historical evidence in docs/SOURCES.md and `tests/fixtures/historical-retired/`. Re-adding any
product line requires an explicit new owner instruction.

## What the Worker does now

- **One-product comparison board** (`/`, `/api/board`): ranks delivered offers for Lavazza Crema e Gusto
  ground coffee in a vacuum brick by item price + shipping + mandatory fees in ILS, normalized to
  delivered ILS/kg and to the packs a shopper actually buys. Destination (six Israeli locality/postcode
  areas, including "Elsewhere in Israel"), target grams and blend variant are selectable; no street
  address is collected or stored. `/api/catalog` exposes exactly one product, its variants and the
  three vendor adapters.
- **Variants and packs stay separate**: Classico, Forte, Ricco, Risveglio and decaf are filtered
  independently, and the Coffee4U listing (which states no blend variant) is stored as *Variant not
  stated*. The board reports how many offers the selected variant excluded instead of merging them.
  Single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g offers are never merged.
- **Retired lines cannot reappear**: `classifyListing()` rejects a retired listing with a reason naming
  the retired line; `resolveProductRequest()` maps an old `?product=lavazza-qualita-oro-vacuum-ground`
  (or Rossa/Suerte) URL back to the tracked product and returns `requestedRetiredProduct` so the board
  can explain the fallback; `pruneRetiredObservations()` deletes any stored retired observation or
  attempt marker on every refresh. The UI shows the tracked product as a static label (no dead
  one-option picker) and displays a written retired-line notice when a query URL asked for one.
- **Honest unknowns**: unknown shipping, unknown FX, unknown availability, stale observations and
  out-of-stock offers remain visible with plain-language reasons. Missing data never becomes zero and
  never wins. Pickup is shown separately and never competes with delivery.
- **Provenance**: every offer keeps its vendor link, product identity (variant, form, pack grams, pack
  count, SKU/GTIN), availability with its structured-data evidence URL, last successful check, last
  attempt, parser version and shipping certainty.
- **Failed attempts stay visible**: when a vendor check fails, the failure is stamped on that offer's last
  successful observation row (`attemptedAt` + `lastError`) instead of a detached marker, so the board still
  ranks the last known good price and stock while saying `Last attempt: Failed … — showing the last
  successful observation`. The comparison table repeats `Last attempt failed …` next to the checked time,
  the unknown list names the failure reason in plain language, and the footer lists each failing source
  with its consecutive failures, next attempt and last error. A successful check clears the failure mark.
- **Previous-check comparison**: each refresh stores the previous successful price, stock and pack weight
  for the same offer, and the board shows the unit-price change since that check in ILS with its timestamp
  ("Unit price down ₪2.00 since the previous check"). A pack-size change or a missing exchange rate makes
  the comparison say why instead of claiming no change, and a stock change is labelled separately.
- **Bulk-value callout**: when the cheapest delivered total is not the cheapest per-kilogram offer (for
  example, two single 250 g packs at 500 g versus the 4 × 250 g pack), the best-offer card and the
  comparison table name the per-kilogram winner without changing the delivered ranking.

# Canton Zürich design system (web-application patterns)

Owner direction, 2026-10-12. This supersedes the earlier generic Swiss transport-signage brief. The
shopping board adapts the **Canton Zürich design system** for a compact web service: flat surfaces,
strict alignment, a responsive grid, a clear type hierarchy and concise disclosures. The product
identity stays our own; there is no cantonal crest, government wordmark or implied affiliation.

Primary references read before implementation:

- Design system overview — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html
- Colors — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/farben.html
- Typography — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/typografie.html
- Layout and grid — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/layout-und-raster.html

## Tokens and roles

| Token | Value | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blau | `#0070B4` | Selected shopping context, the clearly labelled best known delivered offer, links and the focus outline. Used sparingly; vendor names are never painted arbitrary colors. |
| Softblau | `#EDF5FA` | Panel/background for the selected context and the best-offer rule. |
| Black | `#000000` | Primary text and neutral structure. |
| Secondary text | `#666666` | Notes, meta and secondary labels. |
| Surface | `#F7F7F7` | Subtle section surfaces. |
| Divider | `#CCCCCC` | Rules and cell borders. |
| Green | `#1A7F1F` on `#EBF6EB` | Verified in-stock labels only, always with the written status. |
| Red | `#D93C1A` on white | Unavailable/error labels only. |
| Amber | `#8A4B00` on `#FFF4E5` | Unknown shipping, unconfirmed coverage and stale evidence. This is a deliberate shopping-specific extension, **not** an official Canton Zürich token; it preserves the owner's uncertainty semantics. |
| Cyan | `#009EE0` | Non-text active indicator only (3.01:1 on white, so it is never used for small text). |
| Focus | `#0070B4` | 3 px outline on every focusable control (5.28:1 on white, 4.79:1 on Softblau). |

Meaning is never carried by color alone: every status keeps a written label (`In stock (observed)`,
`Shipping not published`, `Published rate (verified)`, `Checkout rate (observed, conditional)`,
`Coverage: …`) and the selected state is distinct. A rate that exists only in the vendor's anonymous
cart/checkout estimator is never called a published rate: it uses the `Checkout rate (observed,
conditional)` label so its quantity/destination condition stays visible.

# Architecture and authority

There are two independent loops:

1. Shurik on GitHub Actions develops and checkpoints source to main. It uses only OPENCODE_API_KEY and the repository GITHUB_TOKEN. Its state/history is public on shurik-control/main.
2. The deployed Worker refreshes vendor observations using deterministic scheduled adapters, persists them through runtime bindings and serves the public comparison board. It does not need Shurik or an LLM to keep refreshing.

Cloudflare Workers Builds is reported connected by the owner and is serving the production Worker; it observes main pushes and performs validation before deploying. The loop independently verified the public deployment once on 2026-10-12 with read-only GETs (docs/evidence/production-verification-20261012T1554Z.json). No CF deployment workflow or CF API secret belongs in GitHub. Exclude shurik-control/* and all other branches from Cloudflare builds and previews.

This prevents Shurik's Actions process from directly authenticating to CF. It is not a sandbox for agent-authored code: Shurik writes main, so its code and configuration can influence the CF build and live Worker. CF build commands can run source-controlled code in a credentialed environment. Restrict the CF build token to this Worker and the minimum required permissions; avoid broad account permissions or unrelated build/runtime secrets. Prefer runtime bindings over administrative API tokens. Never give the public Worker an administrative CF token.

GitHub normally does not trigger another push workflow for a push using GITHUB_TOKEN. Do not rely on CI being automatically triggered by every Shurik checkpoint. Shurik must run local verification, and Cloudflare's build command must run npm run verify for every deployment. After connecting CF, verify one actual Shurik push reaches Workers Builds; never assume third-party webhook behavior from GitHub Actions behavior alone.

## Implemented runtime

The tracked scope is one product line: `src/catalog.js` holds Lavazza Crema e Gusto (a ground vacuum
brick) with its blend variants and strict classification rules. The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired
Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte; their ids remain as tombstones so `classifyListing` and
`resolveProductRequest` reject or explain them instead of reviving them, and each refresh prunes any
stored observation or attempt marker that belongs to a retired line. Vendor-specific adapters under `src/vendors/` (CoffeeMan, Pucks, Coffee4U)
fetch fixed allowlisted product URLs through the bounded fetcher in `src/lib/http.js` and return versioned
observations. `src/lib/quote.js` is a pure, timestamp-aware ranking engine; `src/lib/fx.js` converts
non-ILS amounts with Bank of Israel reference rates and refuses to guess when a rate is missing. It keeps
variants separate, reports how many offers a variant filter withheld, and passes every published shipping
alternative (for example a cheaper pickup-point delivery) through to the UI without using it as the ranked
amount. A vendor that publishes a courier rate but makes home delivery subject to an unpublished locality
list keeps a structured coverage caveat, so the board discloses the geographic restriction instead of
claiming unconditional country-wide delivery; availability and shipping evidence are stamped with the
retrieval time of the page they came from. Each refresh also keeps one step of comparison evidence — the
previous successful price, stock and pack weight of the same offer — so the board can show the unit-price
change since the last check in ILS (and says why when a comparison is impossible), and it advances the
board's `lastRefreshAt` only when at least one vendor actually saved an observation, so a run that fetched
only the exchange-rate table cannot look like a fresh offer check. Board freshness also reports the newest
saved observation and falls back to it for the age when no completion marker exists, so an interrupted run
(for example a redeploy stopping the background job) with fresh saved offers is not labelled never
refreshed, while a recorded but old completion still reports the scheduled pipeline as stopped. A failed
vendor check does not erase the last known good row: the attempt time and reason are stamped on that
offer's existing observation row (or a marker is kept when the offer never succeeded), so the board still
ranks the last successful price and stock while saying the most recent attempt failed, and a later
successful check clears the mark.

`src/lib/policies.js` is the shared, versioned shipping-evidence model. A policy states the vendor,
product/SKU scope, service, destination scope, the amount or free-shipping threshold rule (with the
vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording preserved), the evidence URL and retrieval time, and a `reviewBy`
date. `quoteBoard()` applies the evaluator at read time: an observation whose own shipping is unknown
is enriched with a matching validated policy, while an observation that already carries a fresher
amount, threshold or destination is never overwritten. The evaluator is deterministic and refuses to
guess: conflicting policies for the same scope stay `inconsistent`, a malformed policy is `invalid`,
and a policy past its review date is `expired`, so the offer falls back to explicit unknown shipping
instead of a stale unconditional rate. Enrichment never touches the observation's price, stock,
`observedAt` or the refresh completion marker, so applying a newer shipping rule cannot claim a fresh
vendor price/stock check; `policySummary()` exposes the rule version, observation time and review date
through `/api/status`. Pucks' ₪30/free-above-₪100 home-delivery rule is the first validated policy and
is also the adapter's single source for that rate.

`src/refresh.js` is the deterministic scheduled pipeline (leases, bounded concurrency, per-vendor
backoff, last-known-good retention) and the same function runs in the Worker's `scheduled` handler, the
local cron simulation and tests. Successful vendors count as due up to fifteen minutes before their
stored `nextAttemptAt`, so a cron tick that lands seconds before the six-hour mark still refreshes
instead of silently drifting to a twelve-hour cadence; vendors inside a failure backoff keep their
strict due time. `src/store.js` defines the SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object plus
in-memory and file-backed stores with the same interface. Public routes in `src/index.js` are read-only
snapshots of that storage and never fetch visitor-supplied URLs.

  charge, named delivery method and written certainty label** and the **delivered total** plus
  per-kilogram normalization. The method (`Home delivery`, `Pickup-point delivery`,
  `Distribution-center delivery`, `Self-pickup`, or `Delivery method not stated`) is rendered separately
  from the certainty label, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys. On mobile the three cells stack

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

## Latest owner correction — remove the coffee-variant feature (2026-10-12)

The owner explicitly asks: "Get rid of the coffee variant. There's only two variants and it's the same coffee." Treat the tracked Crema e Gusto listings as **one coffee comparison**, not separate shopper-selectable blends. This latest instruction supersedes every older variant-separation/selector requirement in this prompt, AGENTS.md and the design/architecture/status documentation. Implement it first in the next fresh iteration, then continue the product index, progressive disclosure and shipping-policy work below.

- Remove the blend/variant selector, unobserved-variant menu entries, variant warnings, "other variant" counts/links and variant-as-a-shopping-configuration from the home and product page. Do not replace it with another blend toggle or add variant-specific product cards.
- Compare all eligible tracked Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground offers together for the selected quantity, locality and delivery method. Include the currently "Variant not stated" Coffee4U listing in that same comparison instead of hiding it behind a selector or withholding it as another blend. Offers can still be unavailable/unrankable for genuine stock, freshness, shipping or cart-scope reasons.
- Keep single packs, four-packs and eight-packs as distinct offers with correct whole-pack rounding, purchased grams, item prices, shipping conditions and totals. Removing the variant feature does not merge or duplicate SKUs, pack sizes, cart discounts or service-specific policies.
- Retain original vendor product wording and any raw listing identity metadata in evidence/optional offer details if useful. Do not invent a manufacturer blend or relabel an unstated listing as Classico to make it eligible. Raw wording is provenance, not a default ranking filter or repeated variant badge.
- Remove implicit variant filtering from the default API/quote flow, not just its visible widget. Old shared URLs containing variant=classico/unspecified/etc must still preserve product/quantity/locality but resolve to this unified comparison; discard or ignore the obsolete variant parameter without creating a second view.
- Update AGENTS.md, catalog/public API where appropriate, docs and browser QA so they no longer instruct variant separation. Verify that the single product comparison can include Coffee4U alongside the other Crema e Gusto listings, still names vendors correctly, calculates packs/shipping honestly and has no residual blend control/warning. Existing stock, policy-scope, unknown-shipping and retired-product safeguards remain mandatory.

The active catalog remains Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee only; Oro, Rossa, Suerte and other product lines stay excluded. The home is still the product index with one real card. Keep the Canton Zürich design system, Inter and established semantic palette. Shurik writes the code/tests; the overseer only steers and reviews.

## Current owner priorities — product index, reusable shipping knowledge, progressive disclosure (2026-10-12)

The owner has reviewed the updated website and still finds it very cluttered. The home page must become an overview index of products, with the comparison workflow on a dedicated product page. The owner also expects obvious browser-visible shipping rules, such as Pucks free shipping above ₪100, to be found systematically and actually used by the site. These priorities replace the earlier instruction to repeat the initial shipping investigation first in every fresh iteration. The first Pucks/CoffeeMan/Coffee4U browser investigation is already evidenced in iterations 3-67 through 3-72. Use that evidence; fresh browser work should address a specific missing, contradictory or stale condition. Do not spend whole iterations reproducing unchanged amounts while the requested product/UI work waits.

Shurik implements all code, assets, tests and documentation. The overseer only changes this brief and reviews results. Keep the Canton Zürich design direction, Inter, palette and Crema e Gusto-only active scope below.

### 1. Make the home page a product overview index

- The canonical home route must show a clean product index, not the full vendor comparison board. Render its cards from the active catalog. Today that means **one real card: Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**. Design the structure to support additional products later, but do not add or reactivate Oro, Rossa, Suerte, other product lines, fabricated offerings or placeholder cards. Crema e Gusto offers share one comparison; pack sizes and multipacks remain distinct.
- Each product card links to a real, directly loadable product-detail URL. The home page needs only product identity, a concise useful summary and a clear way to open the comparison. If a summary price is shown, its quantity, destination, freshness and conditional nature must be understandable; do not mix different cart sizes into a misleading "from" price.
- The product page identifies the coffee and provides the quantity/locality/delivery controls and offers. Provide a clear "All products" way back. Preserve shareable selection state and handle existing product/query links, including retired-line fallbacks, without losing quantity or locality; obsolete variant parameters are ignored. Keep existing read-only APIs and deterministic refresh behavior working.
- The home title is "Attention shoppers" without a period. The product-detail heading should name the product, e.g. "Lavazza Crema e Gusto", with compact site branding. Do not reproduce a giant branding hero or comparison explanation on both pages.

### 2. Generalize browser shipping research and deterministic shipping policies

- Reuse the real Chrome/ChromeDriver helper, but build a reusable research workflow with vendor-specific navigation recipes and a common evidence output. It must navigate the product/cart/estimator, select the actual delivery method, set whole-pack quantities and permitted locality/postcode, wait for recalculation, and compare displayed item subtotal, shipping and final total. A subtotal displayed before choosing a method is not a delivered quote: the Pucks cart only adds its ₪30 after the delivery card is selected.
- Research a meaningful cart matrix per SKU/pack/service/destination: normal quantities plus below/above a displayed free-shipping threshold. Capture the threshold language, exclusions, minimum order, fees, delivery methods, locality restrictions, any discount and the exact blocker if a quote requires personal details. Keep the anonymous-cart/locality permission and the no-order/payment/login/account/street-address/bot-bypass restrictions below. Sanitize all URLs and output so cart/session/cookie/token values never enter public records.
- Introduce a common, validated shipping-evidence/policy representation and evaluator used by every adapter/quote: distinguish published rules, observed conditional cart quotes and unknown/inconsistent rules. Preserve service, eligible product/SKU/pack, quantity or weight/subtotal scope, destination scope, currency, amount or threshold rule, source, observed/review time and certainty. Per-vendor recipes may differ; common policy interpretation, arithmetic, evidence storage and validation should be shared. Do not keep accumulating unrelated hard-coded adapter strings as the only shipping model.
- Pucks is the concrete acceptance case: the rendered estimator established **₪30 home delivery and free shipping above the stated ₪100 item subtotal**, including 2 × 250 g = ₪60 + ₪30 = ₪90 and 4 × 250 g = ₪120 with free delivery to Tel Aviv / 6100000. Apply the rule to eligible current offers and show the free-shipping condition in the appropriate delivery details. Preserve the threshold comparison/exclusions actually established by the vendor; do not silently turn "above" into "at least" without checking the boundary semantics. Coverage remains qualified beyond the destinations tested.
- CoffeeMan demonstrates why a single global threshold is insufficient: the ₪240 eight-pack cart still charged ₪20 while some single-pack/two-four-pack carts showed free shipping; the small single/four-pack carts showed a ₪15 distribution-center alternative. Store conditional evidence at its actual scope, and keep unverified rules unresolved. Do not infer a nationwide/free-over-X rule from one cart or flatten SKU/pack distinctions. Scoped discounts and alternatives must not silently change the ranked courier amount beyond their verified applicability.
- **Fix the known-knowledge/old-store gap.** The latest recorded production probes still had old shipping unknowns even after the policies were established and deployed. Implement a safe versioned policy resolution/enrichment or migration so newly validated shipping knowledge can apply to matching persisted offers promptly, without waiting hours for the next item refresh. Choose the mechanism within the existing Worker architecture; keep it deterministic, bounded and compatible with stored data. Preserve the item's actual price/stock observation time and shipping evidence's own time; applying a newer shipping rule must not claim a fresh vendor price/stock check or advance lastRefreshAt. Do not fabricate an item price, force a Cloudflare refresh through admin tools, or turn a policy into an unconditional coverage guarantee. Test an old persisted Pucks offer with unknown shipping gaining the evidenced rule after a policy update.
- The public Worker must continue to work without the coding loop or a browser open. It should consume validated policy data and bounded public sources; browser research is development/research tooling, not an LLM/browser session triggered by visitor traffic. Document how policy evidence is rechecked or becomes stale, and keep unresolved shipping explicit.

### 3. Use substantial progressive disclosure on the product page

The goal is a short decision flow, not merely smaller versions of every existing paragraph.

- Default view: compact product identity/selection, an easy quantity and locality change, and the best eligible offer with vendor, accurate purchased pack/grams, item subtotal, **named delivery method and charge**, delivered total, stock and a short necessary conditional/unknown/stale warning. On 390 × 844, the actual money values and method must be visible in the initial viewport; a card whose top edge begins at y=829 does not satisfy this. Achieve this by prioritizing content, not tiny text or hiding essential uncertainty.
- Use a clear "Compare other offers" disclosure or a compact comparison preview. The Coffee4U listing belongs in the same Crema e Gusto comparison; retain its original vendor wording in evidence without a separate blend choice. Keep relevant controls accessible, with secondary configuration in a clearly labelled section/drawer when useful.
- Delivery alternatives, pickup locations/fees, free-shipping conditions, detailed coverage and terms belong under "Delivery options" / "Offer details". Self-pickup stays separate from delivered ranking and should be collapsed by default rather than three always-expanded repeated rows. Show a brief coverage qualification beside a conditional total, with the full prose inside details.
- Price history, parser/source provenance, FX, refresh diagnostics and detailed timestamps are secondary disclosures. Retain concise visible stale/failure/unknown warnings when they change a shopping decision. Hide empty "missing information" sections and remove repeated teaching copy, duplicate headings, repeated product restrictions and the same caveat printed several times.
- Use the Canton Zürich native disclosure/accordion/service patterns and the selected blue/soft-blue scheme. Keep semantic stock/uncertainty colors and text labels, keyboard/focus behavior, RTL handling and readable type. Opening one useful detail must not require reading through unrelated diagnostics.
- Fix the independently observed pickup-name regression: the saved after-1440/after-390 screenshots and passing QA output contained **"[object HTMLSpanElement]"** instead of the vendor. Current renderPickupSection passes bidi(quote.vendor.name), a DOM node, as an el() text attribute. Shurik fixes the node/text handling and adds a meaningful rendered check for the actual vendor names and the absence of object-string artifacts.
- The current shippingServiceText() returns a certainty label rather than a delivery-method name. Render the actual method (home courier / distribution-center or pickup-point delivery / self-pickup) separately from certainty, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys.

### Acceptance for this owner correction

Checkpoint useful progress, then complete all three outcomes: real home index + reachable product page, reusable shipping research/policy resolution with the Pucks old-store case, and progressive disclosure that exposes the core decision values on the first mobile screen. Update browser QA to exercise the home-to-product navigation, directly loaded/shareable product URLs, opening/closing disclosures, method/quantity/destination changes, named vendors, honest unknowns and the money values' actual visibility. Preserve catalog exclusions, pack arithmetic, conditional coverage, scheduled refresh/backoff and last-known-good storage.

Run npm run verify and relevant offline/local-live browser QA after changes; inspect readable desktop/mobile viewport screenshots of both pages when image tools support them. The current pi-durable read tool rejects images: report that limitation accurately; character/pixel maps are only coarse evidence and cannot establish that text is correct. Save sanitized screenshots for overseer review and corroborate labels/arithmetic with DOM/API evidence. Keep docs/DESIGN.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/SOURCES.md and docs/STATUS.md aligned with the final implementation. Do not let waiting for a future production cron tick replace this work, and do not claim the correction is live solely because code or a policy was committed.

## Owner design direction — Canton Zürich design system (2026-10-12)

Use **the Canton Zürich design system specifically** for the shopping-page redesign. This owner direction supersedes the earlier generic Swiss transport-signage reference in this prompt and docs/DESIGN.md. Use its web-application/service patterns to make a compact shopping tool, with consistent alignment, responsive grids, flat surfaces, clear type hierarchy and concise disclosures. Keep the product identity our own; no cantonal crest, government wordmark or implied affiliation.

Read the official primary references before implementing:

Update docs/DESIGN.md to this concrete design direction as part of your implementation. content.text:
# Project status

Stage: **Crema e Gusto scope enforced; the Canton Zürich shopping board, the browser-researched
shipping rates and the redesigned UI validated locally (99/99 tests, 82/82 offline and 78/78 live browser
checks); production serves the redesigned assets, the first production cron tick was observed at
18:17:55 UTC (0 requests, exactly as expected) and its stored observations pick up the researched rates
at the 00:17 UTC cron tick; a fresh 19:07-19:16 UTC browser session independently reproduced all three
vendors' rendered shipping quotes; iteration 3-70 labels cart-observed rates as conditional checkout
rates and halves the pickup-row space; iteration 3-71 resolved the CoffeeMan single/4-pack delivery
methods in a fresh anonymous cart (₪25 courier / ₪15 distribution-center for 0.5-1 kg carts), recorded
the cart-dependent free-delivery behavior without inventing a threshold, and surfaced the adapter
shipping terms in the offer disclosure.**
The Worker implements the self-updating board for exactly one product line — **Lavazza Crema e Gusto
vacuum-packed ground coffee** — with three independent Israeli vendor adapters and five observed
listings. The owner reports the site deployed at
**https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev** with Worker name `attention-shoppers` and main-push
auto-deploy through Cloudflare Workers Builds. On 2026-10-12 15:51-15:54 UTC the coding loop independently
verified the public site from the runner with read-only GETs (no Cloudflare credentials, no admin API, no
deploy): `/health`, `/api/status`, `/api/catalog` and `/api/board` answered HTTP 200, the catalog exposed
exactly one product, the store held five observations, and the probe's first `/health` GET started the
site's documented initial refresh, which completed at 15:52:12.546 UTC and advanced `lastRefreshAt`. That
probe also exposed the gap iteration 3-61 fixes: before it, production had five saved observations and
vendor successes from 13:34/13:46 UTC but `lastRefreshAt` was null (an interrupted run), so the board read
as never refreshed even though its offers were recent. Outstanding production checks are listed below.
After the supervisor published the 3-61 commits, a second read-only probe at 16:17-16:18 UTC found
`/health` serving `lastObservationAt` — a field only the 3-61 code emits — so the pushed build is live in
production and the main-push Workers Builds path is independently verified from the runner; the Durable
Object store persisted across the deploy with the same refresh timestamps, and headless-Chrome browser QA
driven against the production URL passed **53/53** checks with zero console errors. Iteration 3-59 kept the single-product scope and improved freshness honesty and
comparison quality: the board's `lastRefreshAt` now advances only when at least one vendor actually saved
an observation (an FX-only or empty run can no longer look freshly checked), every offer stores one
step of previous-check evidence so the UI shows the unit-price change since the last successful check in
ILS (or explains why the comparison is impossible), and the cheapest per-kilogram offer is called out
when it differs from the cheapest delivered total. Iteration 3-60 adds written shipping-certainty labels
next to every ranked rate, a `+₪ vs best` line on each comparison row, an approximate next-source-check
time in the board footer, and records the fresh vendor-coverage probes (Zap, FreshCafe, Brioso) that
found no fourth vendor carrying the tracked ground listing. Iteration 3-61 adds a board-freshness fallback
so an interrupted refresh with fresh saved observations is not reported as never refreshed, and records the
first independently verified production refresh from the runner. Iteration 3-62 fixed a cron phase-lock in
that runtime: because a vendor's stored due time is `run time + 6 h` while the cron fires at fixed clock
times, a tick landing seconds early skipped every vendor and would silently drift the cadence to twelve
hours (with the board reporting stale for hours between runs). Successful vendors now count as due up to
15 minutes early; failure backoff stays strict. The fix is locally verified (**90/90** tests, fixture
refresh, **57/57** offline browser checks) and waits for the next main-push deployment. Iteration 3-63
added the repeatable read-only production probe and the multi-tick cron cadence test, and re-verified the
live sources at 16:50-16:53 UTC. Iteration 3-64 finished and verified the **failed-attempt disclosure**
that session 3-63 saved just before its timeout: when a vendor check fails, the attempt time and reason
are stamped on that offer's last successful observation row, so the board keeps ranking the last known
good price and stock while saying the most recent attempt failed instead of presenting the row as freshly
re-checked. Verified locally with **94/94** `node:test` cases, `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (80.12 KiB /
gzip 20.60 KiB), the fixture refresh (6 bounded requests, five offers), a live `check:sources` pass at
17:22 UTC (five listings unchanged), a live `cron:local -- --fresh` pass at 17:24 UTC (6 requests, five
offers, USD 3.078), **63/63** offline and **59/59** live browser checks including six new failed-attempt
checks. The same 3-64 code is live in production: read-only GETs at 17:31 UTC found the production board
quotes carrying `lastAttemptFailed`/`lastError` and the deployed `app.js` containing the failed-attempt
labels, and live browser QA against the production URL passed **59/59** with zero console errors.

The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa, Suerte and every other Lavazza
product line. They are no longer catalog entries, fetch targets or UI options. Their names survive only
as tombstones in `src/catalog.js` (so old links and historical pages are refused with an explicit reason)
and as historical evidence in docs/SOURCES.md and `tests/fixtures/historical-retired/`. Re-adding any
product line requires an explicit new owner instruction.

## What the Worker does now

- **One-product comparison board** (`/`, `/api/board`): ranks delivered offers for Lavazza Crema e Gusto
  ground coffee in a vacuum brick by item price + shipping + mandatory fees in ILS, normalized to
  delivered ILS/kg and to the packs a shopper actually buys. Destination (six Israeli locality/postcode
  areas, including "Elsewhere in Israel"), target grams and blend variant are selectable; no street
  address is collected or stored. `/api/catalog` exposes exactly one product, its variants and the
  three vendor adapters.
- **Variants and packs stay separate**: Classico, Forte, Ricco, Risveglio and decaf are filtered
  independently, and the Coffee4U listing (which states no blend variant) is stored as *Variant not
  stated*. The board reports how many offers the selected variant excluded instead of merging them.
  Single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g offers are never merged.
- **Retired lines cannot reappear**: `classifyListing()` rejects a retired listing with a reason naming
  the retired line; `resolveProductRequest()` maps an old `?product=lavazza-qualita-oro-vacuum-ground`
  (or Rossa/Suerte) URL back to the tracked product and returns `requestedRetiredProduct` so the board
  can explain the fallback; `pruneRetiredObservations()` deletes any stored retired observation or
  attempt marker on every refresh. The UI shows the tracked product as a static label (no dead
  one-option picker) and displays a written retired-line notice when a query URL asked for one.
- **Honest unknowns**: unknown shipping, unknown FX, unknown availability, stale observations and
  out-of-stock offers remain visible with plain-language reasons. Missing data never becomes zero and
  never wins. Pickup is shown separately and never competes with delivery.
- **Provenance**: every offer keeps its vendor link, product identity (variant, form, pack grams, pack
  count, SKU/GTIN), availability with its structured-data evidence URL, last successful check, last
  attempt, parser version and shipping certainty.
- **Failed attempts stay visible**: when a vendor check fails, the failure is stamped on that offer's last
  successful observation row (`attemptedAt` + `lastError`) instead of a detached marker, so the board still
  ranks the last known good price and stock while saying `Last attempt: Failed … — showing the last
  successful observation`. The comparison table repeats `Last attempt failed …` next to the checked time,
  the unknown list names the failure reason in plain language, and the footer lists each failing source
  with its consecutive failures, next attempt and last error. A successful check clears the failure mark.
- **Previous-check comparison**: each refresh stores the previous successful price, stock and pack weight
  for the same offer, and the board shows the unit-price change since that check in ILS with its timestamp
  ("Unit price down ₪2.00 since the previous check"). A pack-size change or a missing exchange rate makes
  the comparison say why instead of claiming no change, and a stock change is labelled separately.
- **Bulk-value callout**: when the cheapest delivered total is not the cheapest per-kilogram offer (for
  example, two single 250 g packs at 500 g versus the 4 × 250 g pack), the best-offer card and the
  comparison table name the per-kilogram winner without changing the delivered ranking.
- **Readable comparison rows**: every ranked row states its difference from the cheapest delivered total
  (`+₪58.00 vs best`; the best row says `Cheapest delivered total`, an equal total says
  `Same delivered total as best`), so the ranking is auditable without recomputing the arithmetic.
- **Shipping evidence, honestly framed**: each published or browser-observed rate carries a structured
  coverage caveat where the vendor terms make home delivery subject to a locality list the product page
  does not publish, so the board discloses the geographic restriction instead of claiming country-wide
  delivery. Every rate is also labelled in words: `Published rate (verified)`, `Checkout rate (observed,
  conditional)`, `Estimated rate` or `Not published before checkout`. Availability and shipping evidence
  are stamped with the retrieval time of the page (or estimator) they came from, and the best-offer card
  and comparison table show unit price × packs bought = ILS line total so the delivered total is
  auditable. A cart-observed rate is never relabelled as published and is never stretched to an
  unobserved cart size (the CoffeeMan 8-pack quote carries its 2000 g limit); a genuinely missing rate
  keeps the `Not published before checkout` label and never becomes zero.
- **Self-updating runtime**: `wrangler.jsonc` triggers `17 */6 * * *` (about every six hours); the first
  `/health` or `/api/board` after deployment starts one throttled initial refresh. Observations, vendor
  state, FX rates, run history and leases persist in the SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object. The
  board API and footer report board-level fresh/stale freshness and warn in plain language when no
  completed refresh is recent. A run only advances `lastRefreshAt` when at least one vendor actually saved
  an observation, so neither an empty run (every vendor inside its backoff window) nor a run that fetched
  only the exchange-rate table can mask a stalled pipeline as fresh; both are still recorded in the run
  history. When no completion marker exists (a run interrupted after saving observations, for example by a
  redeploy), the board falls back to the newest saved observation for the age, exposes it as
  `lastObservationAt`/`freshness.dataAsOf`, and names it in the footer instead of claiming no refresh ever
  happened; a recorded but old completion still reads as stale, because that is the scheduled pipeline
  having stopped. Only observations for product lines that are still tracked count toward freshness, so a
  lingering historical row cannot mask a stale board. A successful vendor is stored as due at `run time +
  6 h`, and because the cron fires on fixed clock times a successful vendor also counts as due up to 15
  minutes early (`EARLY_DUE_TOLERANCE_MS`); a tick landing seconds before the due time therefore still
  refreshes instead of skipping every vendor and silently drifting to a twelve-hour cadence, while vendors
  inside a failure backoff keep their strict due time. The board footer also names the earliest vendor `nextAttemptAt` as an approximate next source
  check time, so a shopper can see the board is scheduled to keep updating.
- **Bounded fetching**: host allowlists per adapter, 12 s timeout, 1.5 MB response cap, max two vendors
  in flight, one attempt per offer per run, published crawl delays honoured (`Crawl-delay: 7` on
  CoffeeMan and Coffee4U), 30 min→12 h backoff per vendor. Public routes never fetch a visitor-supplied
  URL and never start unbounded scraping. Responses are cacheable
  (`public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600`).
- **No LLM or paid scraper in the public runtime**: only deterministic adapters, official Bank of Israel
  rates and native Cloudflare storage.

## Live observations (recorded evidence)

Retrieved 2026-10-12 15:39 UTC and re-checked at 16:50 and 17:22 UTC with `npm run check:sources` (bounded
fetcher + production parsers) and stored under `.shurik-local/sources/`; review copies in
`docs/evidence/source-check-20261012T1544Z.json`, `docs/evidence/source-check-20261012T1650Z.json` and
`docs/evidence/source-check-20261012T1722Z.json`.
Full source record: docs/SOURCES.md. Exactly five listings are active; no retired line is fetched. Prices,
stock and shipping were unchanged across the 15:12, 15:39, 16:50 and 17:22 UTC checks, and the 3-60 re-check
of the CoffeeMan 8-pack page and the Pucks cart again found no published shipping rate
(`docs/evidence/vendor-probe-2026-10-12T1536Z.json`).

## Pages

- **Home `/` — product index.** Renders one card per tracked catalog product (today exactly one:
  Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee). A card carries identity, packaging, a concise
  summary of the comparison and tracked vendors, and a link to `/product/<id>`. The full comparison
  board is not rendered on the home route. A legacy board link that still carries
  `product`/`grams`/`dest`/`variant` state is forwarded to the product page with that state intact.
- **Product `/product/<id>` — decision page.** Directly loadable and shareable; the path plus
  `?grams=&dest=&variant=` query restores quantity, locality and variant (a retired-line or unknown id
  falls back to the tracked product with a written notice). Default view: compact product identity and
  the three controls, then the best eligible offer with vendor, stock, accurate pack/grams, the three
  money values and a one-line conditional warning. Everything else is progressively disclosed:
  `Delivery options and conditions` and `Offer details and check history` per offer, one
  `Compare other offers (n)` disclosure for the rest of the ranking, one collapsed
  `Self-pickup options (n)` disclosure, and an `Offers with missing information (n)` disclosure that is

It is not a sandbox for agent-authored code: Shurik writes main, so its code and configuration can influence the CF build and live Worker. CF build commands can run source-controlled code in a credentialed environment. Restrict the CF build token to this Worker and the minimum required permissions; avoid broad account permissions or unrelated build/runtime secrets. Prefer runtime bindings over administrative API tokens. Never give the public Worker an administrative CF token.

GitHub normally does not trigger another push workflow for a push using GITHUB_TOKEN. Do not rely on CI being automatically triggered by every Shurik checkpoint. Shurik must run local verification, and Cloudflare's build command must run npm run verify for every deployment. After connecting CF, verify one actual Shurik push reaches Workers Builds; never assume third-party webhook behavior from GitHub Actions behavior alone.

## What the Worker does now

- **One-product comparison board** (`/`, `/api/board`): ranks delivered offers for Lavazza Crema e Gusto
  ground coffee in a vacuum brick by item price + shipping + mandatory fees in ILS, normalized to
  delivered ILS/kg and to the packs a shopper actually buys. Destination (six Israeli locality/postcode
  areas, including "Elsewhere in Israel"), target grams and blend variant are selectable; no street
  address is collected or stored. `/api/catalog` exposes exactly one product, its variants and the
  three vendor adapters.
- **Variants and packs stay separate**: Classico, Forte, Ricco, Risveglio and decaf are filtered
  independently, and the Coffee4U listing (which states no blend variant) is stored as *Variant not
  stated*. The board reports how many offers the selected variant excluded instead of merging them.
  Single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g offers are never merged.
- **Retired lines cannot reappear**: `classifyListing()` rejects a retired listing with a reason naming
  the retired line; `resolveProductRequest()` maps an old `?product=lavazza-qualita-oro-vacuum-ground`
  (or Rossa/Suerte) URL back to the tracked product and returns `requestedRetiredProduct` so the board
  can explain the fallback; `pruneRetiredObservations()` deletes any stored retired observation or
  attempt marker on every refresh. The UI shows the tracked product as a static label (no dead
  one-option picker) and displays a written retired-line notice when a query URL asked for one.
- **Honest unknowns**: unknown shipping, unknown FX, unknown availability, stale observations and
  out-of-stock offers remain visible with plain-language reasons. Missing data never becomes zero and
  never wins. Pickup is shown separately and never competes with delivery.
- **Provenance**: every offer keeps its vendor link, product identity (variant, form, pack grams, pack
  count, SKU/GTIN), availability with its structured-data evidence URL, last successful check, last
  attempt, parser version and shipping certainty.
- **Failed attempts stay visible**: when a vendor check fails, the failure is stamped on that offer's last
  successful observation row (`attemptedAt` + `lastError`) instead of a detached marker, so the board still
  ranks the last known good price and stock while saying `Last attempt: Failed … — showing the last
  successful observation`. The comparison table repeats `Last attempt failed …` next to the checked time,
  the unknown list names the failure reason in plain language, and the footer lists each failing source
  with its consecutive failures, next attempt and last error. A successful check clears the failure mark.
- **Previous-check comparison**: each refresh stores the previous successful price, stock and pack weight
  for the same offer, and the board shows the unit-price change since that check in ILS with its timestamp
  ("Unit price down ₪2.00 since the previous check"). A pack-size change or a missing exchange rate makes
  the comparison say why instead of claiming no change, and a stock change is labelled separately.
- **Bulk-value callout**: when the cheapest delivered total is not the cheapest per-kilogram offer (for
  example, two single 250 g packs at 500 g versus the 4 × 250 g pack), the best-offer card and the
  comparison table name the per-kilogram winner without changing the delivered ranking.
