# Observed sources and vendor research

**Active scope (owner correction, 2026-10-12): Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee only.**
The Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte listings further down are **historical evidence** from earlier
iterations. They are not fetch targets, not part of the active catalog, and their page excerpts live in
`tests/fixtures/historical-retired/` as negative test inputs. Historical evidence does not authorize
re-adding a product line; that needs an explicit new owner instruction.

All observations below were retrieved by the deterministic adapters in `src/vendors/`
through the bounded fetcher. Re-run them at any time with `npm run check:sources`;
each run writes its evidence to `.shurik-local/sources/<timestamp>.json`; review snapshots are copied to
`docs/evidence/`.

## Tracked listings (live checks)

### Browser-researched shipping quotes (2026-10-12)

The owner asked for shipping quotes through a real interactive browser rather than product-page disclaimers.
`scripts/browser-research.mjs` kept one headless Chrome/ChromeDriver session alive to navigate each
vendor's product page, add the tracked product to a temporary anonymous cart, open the public
cart/checkout estimator and read the rendered delivery methods and charges. Only locality/postcode fields
were filled; no order, payment, login, account or street address was involved, and cart/session
identifiers are never recorded.

| Vendor | Cart | Locality | Service | Shipping | Item subtotal | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pucks | 2 × 250 g = 500 g | Tel Aviv / 6100000 | home delivery (only method) | ₪30 | ₪60 | free above ₪100 item subtotal; fee unchanged for Eilat / 8800000, no restriction displayed |
| Pucks | 4 × 250 g = 1 kg | Tel Aviv / 6100000 | home delivery | free | ₪120 | free-shipping threshold met; a 1 kg cart to Jerusalem / 9100000 reproduced free delivery on 2026-10-12T22:24Z with the same “free above ₪100” wording (`2026-10-12-pucks-jerusalem-1kg-recipe.json`) |
| CoffeeMan | 8 × 250 g = 2 kg | not requested by the estimator | home courier / distribution center | ₪20 / ₪20 | ₪240 | re-checked in a fresh cart at 20:07 UTC; still no published free-delivery threshold, and this SKU cart did not get the free delivery other large carts received |
| CoffeeMan | 8 × 250 g = 2 kg | not requested | self-pickup | ₪0 | ₪240 | a pickup branch must be chosen |
| CoffeeMan | 2 × 250 g = 500 g | not requested by the estimator | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / ₪15 | ₪66 | courier matches the product page; the ₪15 distribution-center rate is cart-observed, not published |
| CoffeeMan | 4 × 250 g = 1 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / ₪15 | ₪132 | same fee schedule as the 4-pack cart at 1 kg |
| CoffeeMan | 1 × 4-pack = 1 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / ₪15 | ₪124 | 4-pack product page rate confirmed in the cart |
| CoffeeMan | 6 × 250 g = 1.5 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / free | ₪198 | distribution-center fee dropped to free while the courier stayed ₪25 |
| CoffeeMan | 7 × 250 g = 1.75 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | free / free | ₪231 | free delivery observed, but no rule or threshold is published |
| CoffeeMan | 2 × 4-pack = 2 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | free / free | ₪248 | free at ₪248, unlike the ₪240 8-pack SKU cart: cart/product dependent, not a published threshold |
| Coffee4U | 1 × 250 g | not requested | door-to-door courier | ₪30 | ₪38 | 1,270-entry destination city list; locality-list caveat |
| Coffee4U | 1 × 250 g | not requested | Chiita Shops pickup point | ₪15 | ₪38 | 421-city list plus a per-city spot |
| Coffee4U | 1 × 250 g | not requested | self-pickup | ₪0 | ₪38 | pickup at the Tel Aviv shop |

Full evidence matrix, rendered-text excerpts and screenshots: `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-vendor-shipping-quotes.json` (observed 18:07-18:19 UTC) plus the fresh Pucks re-check `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-recheck.json` (observed 18:55 UTC), the independent all-vendor re-check `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-fresh-recheck-3-69.json` (observed 19:07-19:16 UTC, which reproduced the same amounts and added the note that Pucks applies the ₪30 to the summary total only after a delivery method is selected), the CoffeeMan single/4-pack cart batch `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-coffeeman-cart-single-4pack.json` (observed 19:56-20:09 UTC, which resolved the unpublished distribution-center fee and the cart-dependent free-delivery behavior) and the recipe-driven Pucks Jerusalem run `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-jerusalem-1kg-recipe.json` (observed 2026-10-12T22:24Z; 4 × 250 g = ₪120 subtotal, free delivery, “free above ₪100”, with the `#city`/`#zip` fields filled and read back). The available file-read tool rejects PNG input, so the screenshots could not be read as images by the model; every amount above is backed by rendered DOM text captured in the same session, and the screenshots are artifacts for a human reviewer. Since iteration 3-70 `scripts/inspect-screenshot.mjs` additionally decodes the PNGs with node:zlib and renders a coarse luminance map plus a Canton Zürich token-pixel report, so layout and colour regions can be checked without image input (see `docs/evidence/visual-review/2026-10-12-revised-layout-review.json`). A cart quote is conditional on its recorded quantity and destination: it is not an unconditional nationwide rate and not a completed checkout.

**Certainty labels:** a rate published on the vendor's product page keeps `certainty: verified` and the label `Published rate (verified)`. A rate that only exists in the vendor's anonymous cart/checkout estimator is stored as `certainty: checkout_quote` and rendered as `Checkout rate (observed, conditional)` (Pucks and the CoffeeMan 8 × 250 g cart). Coffee4U publishes its courier and pickup-point rates on the product page, so it keeps `verified`.

**Versioned policy promotion and staleness (iterations 3-73, 3-76 and 3-77):** a validated quote is promoted by hand into `src/lib/policies.js` as a versioned policy (vendor, product/SKU scope, service, destination scope, amount or free-shipping rule with the vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording, secondary delivery alternatives, evidence URL and retrieval time, `reviewBy`). The read-time evaluator in the same module enriches an observation whose own shipping is unknown, never overwrites a fresher parsed rate, treats conflicting policies as `inconsistent`, and stops applying a policy once `reviewBy` passes (the offer then shows explicit unknown shipping again). Four policies are checked in: Pucks' ₪30 / free-above-₪100 rule is `pucks-il-home-delivery` v1, observed 2026-10-12T18:10:10Z; CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule is `coffeeman-single-4pack-il-home-delivery` v1 with the cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center alternative (observed 2026-10-12T20:04:00Z); CoffeeMan's ₪20 one-8-pack (2 kg) checkout quote is `coffeeman-8pack-il-cart-quote` v1, observed 2026-10-12T20:07:00Z and scoped to the 8-pack offer URL with `maxTotalGrams: 2000`, no free threshold and the observed ₪20 distribution-center alternative; Coffee4U's published ₪30 door-to-door rule is `coffee4u-il-home-delivery` v1 with the ₪15 pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list coverage shape (observed 2026-10-12T20:25:00Z). All carry `reviewBy` 2026-11-11; re-checking the rendered estimator or the product page renews the evidence and version, and `/api/status` exposes the current version, service, alternative ids, observation time and review date. Each policy is also the adapter's single source for the researched values it describes, so the parsed row, the read-time evaluator and the tests share one representation. Enrichment never changes the offer's price/stock observation time or the refresh completion marker. Since iteration 3-78 the adapters honor the same review window at parse time (`policyIsCurrent()`): once a policy is past its review date, its researched rate and any policy-derived alternative are withheld, so a freshly parsed offer falls back to explicit unknown shipping instead of carrying a stale quote; page-published rates (CoffeeMan's ₪25, Coffee4U's ₪30/₪15) stay because they are parsed from the vendor page, not from the policy.

**Recipe-driven rechecks:** `scripts/research-workflow.mjs` defines per-vendor navigation recipes (Pucks, CoffeeMan, Coffee4U) and one common evidence schema (`browser-research-quote`, schema v1). `npm run research:browser -- recipes` lists them and `npm run research:browser -- recipe <id> --grams 500 --locality "תל אביב" --postcode 6100000 --out <file>` executes one against the live Chrome session, then writes a sanitized record whose `status` is `quoted`, `partial` (rate read but cart quantity unverified or arithmetic inconsistent), `blocked` (public flow stopped, with the exact step and rendered excerpt) or `failed`. URLs lose query strings/fragments and session/token-like runs are redacted before anything is written. A live Pucks recipe run on 2026-10-12 21:06-21:10 UTC verified the product page and the add-to-cart label (`הוסף לעגלה`, cart showed 1 × 250 g = ₪30) but direct navigation to `https://pucks.co.il/payment/request` did not keep the cart in that session; the cart-checkout link (`a.slide_cart__btn-checkout`) is now a recipe step and reached the estimator. Iteration 3-76 fixed the destination step after a live run recorded a locality that was never set: the Pucks estimator's only `<select>` is the language dropdown, so the recipe now fills the named `#city` and `#zip` text inputs as **required** steps (a run that cannot set them is `blocked`, not attributed to a destination) and each `fill` records the value the page actually holds in the evidence steps. Destination-setting steps are marked `verifies: 'destination'`; the runner compares what was set with what was requested, records `destinationVerified` (`true`/`false`/`null`) and, when a requested locality could not be verified, adds a qualification to the record (a quoted record with `destinationVerified: false` fails schema validation without that disclosure). Two live records back this: `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-jerusalem-1kg-recipe.json` (1 kg Jerusalem, free over ₪100) and `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-telaviv-500g-recipe-verified.json` (500 g Tel Aviv, ₪60 + ₪30 = ₪90, `destinationVerified: true`, `#city`/`#zip` readbacks recorded).

### CoffeeMan / Amigo — coffeeman.co.il (Israel)

Tracked listings (three Crema e Gusto offers, never merged):

- **250 g single pack** — `https://www.coffeeman.co.il/product/250-%D7%92%D7%A8%D7%9D-%D7%A7%D7%A4%D7%94-%D7%98%D7%97%D7%95%D7%9F-lavazza-crema-e-gusto-classico`
  - Retrieved: 2026-10-12 11:04, 11:20, 11:29, 11:48, 12:57, 15:12, 16:50 and 17:22 UTC (adapters `coffeeman/1` to `coffeeman/5`)
  - Establishes: name "250 גרם קפה טחון lavazza Crema e Gusto Classico חוזק 7", SKU 930333, variant Classico, ground, 250 g single pack, price ₪33 (regular ₪36), schema.org availability `InStock`, and the published delivery options on the page: courier delivery ₪25, free self-pickup, plus a distribution-center option whose price is not published.
  - Cart research (2026-10-12 19:56-20:09 UTC, anonymous cart): the 500 g and 1 kg carts quoted ₪25 home courier (matching the page) and ₪15 distribution-center delivery up to 5 kg; the distribution-center fee became free at a ₪198 (1.5 kg) cart and the courier at ₪231 (1.75 kg). The free-delivery rule is not published and the ₪240 8-pack cart was still charged, so the board keeps the published ₪25 as the ranked rate and shows the ₪15 distribution-center option as a conditional alternative.
  - Shipping certainty: **verified** for the published courier rate. Coverage caveat: the terms page (`https://www.coffeeman.co.il/page/%D7%AA%D7%A0%D7%90%D7%99-%D7%A9%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%95%D7%A9`, section 4) states home delivery is performed "subject to Amigo's list of localities where home delivery is performed", and the product page does not publish that list, so the observation carries a structured coverage caveat instead of claiming country-wide coverage. A shipping-policy page (`page.asp?page=237`) linked from the terms now returns HTTP 404, so no additional flat rate is available.
- **4 × 250 g multipack** — `https://www.coffeeman.co.il/product/4-%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%96%D7%95%D7%AA-250-%D7%92%D7%A8%D7%9D-%D7%A7%D7%A4%D7%94-%D7%98%D7%97%D7%95%D7%9F-lavazza-crema-e-gusto-classico`
  - Retrieved: 2026-10-12 11:46, 11:48, 12:57, 15:12, 16:50 and 17:22 UTC (adapters `coffeeman/1` to `coffeeman/5`)
  - Establishes: name "4 אריזות 250 גרם קפה טחון lavazza Crema e Gusto Classico", SKU 930334, variant Classico, ground, 4 × 250 g = 1000 g, price ₪124.00, schema.org availability `InStock`, courier ₪25 published on the page.
  - Cart research (2026-10-12 20:04-20:09 UTC, anonymous cart): the 1 kg cart quoted ₪25 home courier (matching the page) and ₪15 distribution-center delivery up to 5 kg; a 2 kg two-4-pack cart was shown free delivery, but the rule is not published, so the board keeps the published ₪25 and shows the ₪15 option as a conditional alternative.
  - Shipping certainty: **verified** (₪25 courier; the same terms-page locality-list caveat applies).
- **8 × 250 g multipack** — `https://www.coffeeman.co.il/product/8-%D7%90%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%96%D7%95%D7%AA-250-%D7%92%D7%A8%D7%9D-%D7%A7%D7%A4%D7%94-%D7%98%D7%97%D7%95%D7%9F-lavazza-crema-e-gusto-classico`
  - Retrieved: 2026-10-12 11:46, 11:48, 12:57, 15:12, 16:50 and 17:22 UTC (adapters `coffeeman/1` to `coffeeman/5`)

content.text:
Single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g offers are never merged.
- **Retired lines cannot reappear**: `classifyListing()` rejects a retired listing with a reason naming
  the retired line; `resolveProductRequest()` maps an old `?product=lavazza-qualita-oro-vacuum-ground`
  (or Rossa/Suerte) URL back to the tracked product and returns `requestedRetiredProduct` so the board
  can explain the fallback; `pruneRetiredObservations()` deletes any stored retired observation or
  attempt marker on every refresh. The UI shows the tracked product as a static label (no dead
  one-option picker) and displays a written retired-line notice when a query URL asked for one.
- **Honest unknowns**: unknown shipping, unknown FX, unknown availability, stale observations and
  out-of-stock offers remain visible with plain-language reasons. Missing data never becomes zero and
  never wins. Pickup is shown separately and never competes with delivery.
- **Provenance**: every offer keeps its vendor link, product identity (variant, form, pack grams, pack
  count, SKU/GTIN), availability with its structured-data evidence URL, last successful check, last
  attempt, parser version and shipping certainty.
- **Failed attempts stay visible**: when a vendor check fails, the failure is stamped on that offer's last
  successful observation row (`attemptedAt` + `lastError`) instead of a detached marker, so the board still
  ranks the last known good price and stock while saying `Last attempt: Failed … — showing the last
  successful observation`. The comparison table repeats `Last attempt failed …` next to the checked time,
  the unknown list names the failure reason in plain language, and the footer lists each failing source
  with its consecutive failures, next attempt and last error. A successful check clears the failure mark.
- **Previous-check comparison**: each refresh stores the previous successful price, stock and pack weight
  for the same offer, and the board shows the unit-price change since that check in ILS with its timestamp
  ("Unit price down ₪2.00 since the previous check"). A pack-size change or a missing exchange rate makes
  the comparison say why instead of claiming no change, and a stock change is labelled separately.
- **Bulk-value callout**: when the cheapest delivered total is not the cheapest per-kilogram offer (for
  example, two single 250 g packs at 500 g versus the 4 × 250 g pack), the best-offer card and the
  comparison table name the per-kilogram winner without changing the delivered ranking.
- **Readable comparison rows**: every ranked row states its difference from the cheapest delivered total
  (`+₪58.00 vs best`; the best row says `Cheapest delivered total`, an equal total says
  `Same delivered total as best`), so the ranking is auditable without recomputing the arithmetic.
- **Shipping evidence, honestly framed**: each published or browser-observed rate carries a structured
  coverage caveat where the vendor terms make home delivery subject to a locality list the product page
  does not publish, so the board discloses the geographic restriction instead of claiming country-wide
  delivery. Every rate is also labelled in words: `Published rate (verified)`, `Checkout rate (observed,
  conditional)`, `Estimated rate` or `Not published before checkout`. Availability and shipping evidence
  are stamped with the retrieval time of the page (or estimator) they came from, and the best-offer card
  and comparison table show unit price × packs bought = ILS line total so the delivered total is
  auditable. A cart-observed rate is never relabelled as published and is never stretched to an
  unobserved cart size (the CoffeeMan 8-pack quote carries its 2000 g limit); a genuinely missing rate
  keeps the `Not published before checkout` label and never becomes zero. Every researched delivery
  rule is a versioned policy in `src/lib/policies.js` (iteration 3-77): Pucks ₪30 / free-above-₪100,
  CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule with the cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center
  alternative, CoffeeMan's ₪20 one-8-pack quote with its ₪20 alternative, and Coffee4U's published
  ₪30 door-to-door rule with its ₪15 pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list
  coverage shape. The read-time evaluator fills a stored row's missing rate, threshold, service,
  alternatives and coverage caveat from the matching policy, never overwriting what the row already
  states and never touching its price, stock or `observedAt`; the adapters derive their researched
  constants from the same policies instead of separate hard-coded strings.
- **Self-updating runtime**: `wrangler.jsonc` triggers `17 */6 * * *` (about every six hours); the first
  `/health` or `/api/board` after deployment starts one throttled initial refresh. Observations, vendor
  state, FX rates, run history and leases persist in the SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object. The
  board API and footer report board-level fresh/stale freshness and warn in plain language when no
  completed refresh is recent. A run only advances `lastRefreshAt` when at least one vendor actually saved
  an observation, so neither an empty run (every vendor inside its backoff window) nor a run that fetched
  only the exchange-rate table can mask a stalled pipeline as fresh; both are still recorded in the run
  history. When no completion marker exists (a run interrupted after saving observations, for example by a
  redeploy), the board falls back to the newest saved observation for the age, exposes it as
  `lastObservationAt`/`freshness.dataAsOf`, and names it in the footer instead of claiming no refresh ever
  happened; a recorded but old completion still reads as stale, because that is the scheduled pipeline
  having stopped. Only observations for product lines that are still tracked count toward freshness, so a
  lingering historical row cannot mask a stale board. A successful vendor is stored as due at `run time +
  6 h`, and because the cron fires on fixed clock times a successful vendor also counts as due up to 15
  minutes early (`EARLY_DUE_TOLERANCE_MS`); a tick landing seconds before the due time therefore still
  refreshes instead of skipping every vendor and silently drifting to a twelve-hour cadence, while vendors
  inside a failure backoff keep their strict due time. The board footer also names the earliest vendor `nextAttemptAt` as an approximate next source
  check time, so a shopper can see the board is scheduled to keep updating.
- **Bounded fetching**: host allowlists per adapter, 12 s timeout, 1.5 MB response cap, max two vendors
  in flight, one attempt per offer per run, published crawl delays honoured (`Crawl-delay: 7` on
  CoffeeMan and Coffee4U), 30 min→12 h backoff per vendor. Public routes never fetch a visitor-supplied
  URL and never start unbounded scraping. Responses are cacheable
  (`public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600`).
- **No LLM or paid scraper in the public runtime**: only deterministic adapters, official Bank of Israel
  rates and native Cloudflare storage.

offer's existing observation row (or a marker is kept when the offer never succeeded), so the board still
ranks the last successful price and stock while saying the most recent attempt failed, and a later
successful check clears the mark.

`src/lib/policies.js` is the shared, versioned shipping-evidence model. A policy states the vendor,
product/SKU scope, service, destination scope, the amount or free-shipping threshold rule (with the
vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording preserved), the evidence URL and retrieval time, and a `reviewBy`
date. `quoteBoard()` applies the evaluator at read time: an observation whose own shipping is unknown
is enriched with a matching validated policy, while an observation that already carries a fresher
amount, threshold or destination is never overwritten. The evaluator is deterministic and refuses to
guess: conflicting policies for the same scope stay `inconsistent`, a malformed policy is `invalid`,
and a policy past its review date is `expired`, so the offer falls back to explicit unknown shipping
instead of a stale unconditional rate. Enrichment never touches the observation's price, stock,
`observedAt` or the refresh completion marker, so applying a newer shipping rule cannot claim a fresh
vendor price/stock check; `policySummary()` exposes the rule version, observation time and review date
through `/api/status`. Four validated policies are checked in: Pucks' ₪30/free-above-₪100 home-delivery
rule, CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule with its cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center
alternative, CoffeeMan's ₪20 checkout quote for the one-8-pack (2 kg) cart (which carries
`maxTotalGrams: 2000` so the quote engine never stretches it to an unobserved larger cart and records
no free threshold for this SKU), and Coffee4U's published ₪30 door-to-door rule with its ₪15
pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list coverage shape. Secondary delivery
methods are part of the policy representation: the evaluator adds them only when a stored row has
none, and they never replace the ranked amount. Each policy is also the adapter's single source for
the researched values it describes, so the parsed row, the read-time evaluator and the tests share one
representation instead of separate hard-coded strings. The adapters honor the same `reviewBy` gate at
parse time (`policyIsCurrent()`): once a policy is past its review date, its researched rate and any
policy-derived alternative are withheld, so a freshly parsed offer falls back to explicit unknown
shipping rather than carrying a stale quote forward. Page-published rates (CoffeeMan's ₪25 and
Coffee4U's ₪30/₪15) are parsed from the vendor page and stay independent of the policy window.

content.text:
## Layout and components

- A single centered column (max 1240 px) with a responsive control grid that reflows to one column on
  mobile. No horizontal page scrolling at 1440 px or 390 px.
- **Offer cards** replace the former wide comparison table. The best known delivered offer carries a
  blue rule, the written tag "Best known delivered total" and its selection context; other ranked
  offers state their difference (`+₪x vs best delivered total`).
- Each card keeps the decision values together in one `.totals` row: **item subtotal**, **shipping
  charge, named delivery method and written certainty label** and the **delivered total** plus
  per-kilogram normalization. The method (`Home delivery`, `Pickup-point delivery`,
  `Distribution-center delivery`, `Self-pickup`, or `Delivery method not stated`) is rendered separately
  from the certainty label, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys. On mobile the three cells stack
  but remain in the same card, inside the first viewport.
- Conditions are one short list per offer (free-shipping threshold, minimum order, delivery area,
  alternative services, self-pickup, delivery time, cart-size limit) inside that offer's
  `Delivery options and conditions` disclosure. A coverage caveat is written once inside the same
  disclosure; the card face keeps only a one-line amber qualification. Pickup-only offers live in their
  own collapsed disclosure and never compete in the delivered ranking; each is one compact row (vendor,
  pack/quantity, item subtotal, pickup fee and the written "Self-pickup, not delivery"), with the
  repeated pickup terms behind a `Pickup terms` disclosure.
- Debug/provenance metadata (previous checks, failed attempts, the applied shipping-policy version, the
  adapter's shipping terms, shipping evidence, FX, per-vendor refresh state, next source check) lives
  behind `Offer details and check history` / `Refresh diagnostics` disclosures instead of the first
  screen. A cart-observed alternative (for example CoffeeMan's distribution-center delivery) carries
  its cart condition in the short label and its full observation in the disclosure.
- Unknown shipping says **"Shipping not published"** with the exact reason and is never shown as zero;
  a published rate with unconfirmed destination coverage is labelled as such, not as a guaranteed
  checkout total.

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

A public online shopping board for delivery in Israel tracking **one product**: **Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**, with every eligible tracked listing — including a listing whose blend wording is not stated — compared in one board and every pack size or multipack kept as a distinct offer. There is no shopper-facing blend/variant selection (owner correction, 2026-10-12). The board compares actual availability and item price plus shipping for a selected quantity and Israeli locality, with visible source evidence and freshness. Unknown shipping is never silently treated as free, and a published courier rate that the vendor's terms make subject to an unpublished locality list is disclosed as a coverage caveat instead of being assumed country-wide.

The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired the earlier multi-product scope: Lavazza Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte are no longer fetched, ranked or shown. Their old listings survive only as historical evidence in [docs/SOURCES.md](docs/SOURCES.md), labelled as such, and as negative fixtures that prove the adapters refuse them. Re-adding any product line needs an explicit new owner instruction.

Three Israeli vendor adapters currently observe **five real Crema e Gusto listings**: CoffeeMan single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g, Pucks 250 g and Coffee4U 250 g. Swiss signage design, meaningful status colors, no emoji typography.

The board is implemented and self-updating: deterministic vendor adapters observe real product pages, a
pure quote engine ranks delivered ILS totals, and a scheduled Durable Object refresh keeps the data
current without a browser or the coding loop. Each refresh keeps the previous successful price and stock
for the same offer, so the board shows the unit-price change since the last check (or explains why a
comparison is impossible), and it reports a completed refresh only when a vendor was actually re-observed.
If a run is interrupted after saving observations, freshness falls back to the newest saved observation
instead of claiming the board never refreshed. A failed vendor check keeps the last successful
observation ranked but stamps the attempt time and reason on it, so the board says the most recent check
failed instead of presenting the row as freshly re-checked. See [current status](docs/STATUS.md),
[observed sources](docs/SOURCES.md), [design](docs/DESIGN.md) and [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Coding loop

The workflow uses [igor-makarov/shurik@v1](https://github.com/igor-makarov/shurik), opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash and max reasoning. The owner chose direct work on main and has added the OPENCODE_API_KEY Actions secret. The first handoff is complete; the main loop will develop the tracker while Cloudflare remains disconnected. Check the Actions page and shurik-control/main for live loop state.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is present in Shurik's pinned Pi AI catalog and supports low, high and max reasoning. Its native adapter preserves reasoning content across tool calls. The owner authorized this switch after Step 5 returned repeated unavailable-endpoint errors. No further model fallback is permitted without an owner instruction.

## Deployment and refreshing

The owner reports auto-deploy enabled on main pushes from **Cloudflare Workers Builds** with the
production Worker `attention-shoppers`, already served at
https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev. On 2026-10-12 15:51-15:54 UTC the coding loop
independently verified that public URL from the runner with read-only GETs (no Cloudflare credentials,
admin API or deploy): the site answered HTTP 200, the catalog exposed exactly one product, five
observations were persisted, and a request-triggered initial refresh completed and advanced
`lastRefreshAt`; see
[the production verification evidence](docs/evidence/production-verification-20261012T1554Z.json). The
loop still does not administer the deployment. GitHub stores no CF credentials and has no deployment job.
Cloudflare Cron Triggers run the Worker's scheduled handler about every six hours, and the
SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object defined in `wrangler.jsonc` persists the last known
observations, vendor refresh state, FX rates and run history.

Follow [the deployment notes and outstanding production checks](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). Agent-authored code can affect the CF build and production Worker once auto-deploy is enabled; keeping CF API credentials out of Shurik does not remove that authority.

## Develop locally

Node 24.14.0, pinned dependencies:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run verify          # node:test suite + wrangler deploy --dry-run
npm run check:sources   # live fetch + parse of every tracked vendor page
npm run cron:offline    # full refresh pipeline against recorded fixtures
npm run cron:local      # full refresh pipeline against the live vendor pages
npm run probe:production # read-only GETs against the deployed board (no credentials, no deploy)
npm run dev             # local Worker with a local SQLite Durable Object
```

`probe:production` checks the deployed site from the outside with fixed public GETs only: one catalog
product, no retired row in any board, the retired-URL fallback, freshness and the ranked totals. It never
authenticates or deploys, and it saves a JSON snapshot under `.shurik-local/production/` (or `--out`) so a
later iteration can diff production state; pass `--url http://127.0.0.1:8789` to check a local Worker.

## Latest owner correction — remove the coffee-variant feature (2026-10-12)

The owner explicitly asks: "Get rid of the coffee variant. There's only two variants and it's the same coffee." Treat the tracked Crema e Gusto listings as **one coffee comparison**, not separate shopper-selectable blends. This latest instruction supersedes every older variant-separation/selector requirement in this prompt, AGENTS.md and the design/architecture/status documentation. Implement it first in the next fresh iteration, then continue the product index, progressive disclosure and shipping-policy work below.

- Remove the blend/variant selector, unobserved-variant menu entries, variant warnings, "other variant" counts/links and variant-as-a-shopping-configuration from the home and product page. Do not replace it with another blend toggle or add variant-specific product cards.
- Compare all eligible tracked Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground offers together for the selected quantity, locality and delivery method. Include the currently "Variant not stated" Coffee4U listing in that same comparison instead of hiding it behind a selector or withholding it as another blend. Offers can still be unavailable/unrankable for genuine stock, freshness, shipping or cart-scope reasons.
- Keep single packs, four-packs and eight-packs as distinct offers with correct whole-pack rounding, purchased grams, item prices, shipping conditions and totals. Removing the variant feature does not merge or duplicate SKUs, pack sizes, cart discounts or service-specific policies.
- Retain original vendor product wording and any raw listing identity metadata in evidence/optional offer details if useful. Do not invent a manufacturer blend or relabel an unstated listing as Classico to make it eligible. Raw wording is provenance, not a default ranking filter or repeated variant badge.
- Remove implicit variant filtering from the default API/quote flow, not just its visible widget. Old shared URLs containing variant=classico/unspecified/etc must still preserve product/quantity/locality but resolve to this unified comparison; discard or ignore the obsolete variant parameter without creating a second view.
- Update AGENTS.md, catalog/public API where appropriate, docs and browser QA so they no longer instruct variant separation. Verify that the single product comparison can include Coffee4U alongside the other Crema e Gusto listings, still names vendors correctly, calculates packs/shipping honestly and has no residual blend control/warning.   `Same delivered total as best`), so the ranking is auditable without recomputing the arithmetic.

  coverage caveat where the vendor terms make home delivery subject to a locality list the product page
  does not publish, so the board discloses the geographic restriction instead of claiming country-wide
  delivery. Every rate is also labelled in words: `Published rate (verified)`, `Checkout rate (observed,
  conditional)`, `Estimated rate` or `Not published before checkout`. Availability and shipping evidence
  are stamped with the retrieval time of the page (or estimator) they came from, and the best-offer card
  and comparison table show unit price × packs bought = ILS line total so the delivered total is
  auditable. A cart-observed rate is never relabelled as published and is never stretched to an
  unobserved cart size (the CoffeeMan 8-pack quote carries its 2000 g limit); a genuinely missing rate
  keeps the `Not published before checkout` label and never becomes zero. Every researched delivery

  CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule with the cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center

  ₪30 door-to-door rule with its ₪15 pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list
  coverage shape. The read-time evaluator fills a stored row's missing rate, threshold, service,
  alternatives and coverage caveat from the matching policy, never overwriting what the row already
  states and never touching its price, stock or `observedAt`; the adapters derive their researched
  constants from the same policies instead of separate hard-coded strings.

  checked page with no banner records an explicit empty list; a checked-in fallback covers rows stored
  before banner parsing and stops after its review date. The base unit price, stock and observation time
  are never changed, and no shipping discount is inferred from an item promotion.
- **Self-updating runtime**: `wrangler.jsonc` triggers `17 */6 * * *` (about every six hours); the first
  `/health` or `/api/board` after deployment starts one throttled initial refresh. Observations, vendor
  state, FX rates, run history and leases persist in the SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object. The
  board API and footer report board-level fresh/stale freshness and warn in plain language when no
  completed refresh is recent. A run only advances `lastRefreshAt` when at least one vendor actually saved
  an observation, so neither an empty run (every vendor inside its backoff window) nor a run that fetched
  only the exchange-rate table can mask a stalled pipeline as fresh; both are still recorded in the run
  history. When no completion marker exists (a run interrupted after saving observations, for example by a
  redeploy), the board falls back to the newest saved observation for the age, exposes it as

  happened; a recorded but old completion still reads as stale, because that is the scheduled pipeline

  inside a failure backoff keep their strict due time. The board footer also names the earliest vendor `nextAttemptAt` as an approximate next source
  check time, so a shopper can see the board is scheduled to keep updating.

## Implemented runtime

The tracked scope is one product line: `src/catalog.js` holds Lavazza Crema e Gusto (a ground vacuum
brick) with strict classification rules. The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired
Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte; their ids remain as tombstones so `classifyListing` and
`resolveProductRequest` reject or explain them instead of reviving them, and each refresh prunes any
stored observation or attempt marker that belongs to a retired line. Vendor-specific adapters under `src/vendors/` (CoffeeMan, Pucks, Coffee4U)
fetch fixed allowlisted product URLs through the bounded fetcher in `src/lib/http.js` and return versioned
observations. `src/lib/quote.js` is a pure, timestamp-aware ranking engine; `src/lib/fx.js` converts
non-ILS amounts with Bank of Israel reference rates and refuses to guess when a rate is missing. It
compares every eligible tracked listing — including one that states no blend wording — in one board and
passes every published shipping
alternative (for example a cheaper pickup-point delivery) through to the UI without using it as the ranked
amount. A vendor that publishes a courier rate but makes home delivery subject to an unpublished locality
list keeps a structured coverage caveat, so the board discloses the geographic restriction instead of
claiming unconditional country-wide delivery; availability and shipping evidence are stamped with the
retrieval time of the page they came from. Each refresh also keeps one step of comparison evidence — the
previous successful price, stock and pack weight of the same offer — so the board can show the unit-price
change since the last check in ILS (and says why when a comparison is impossible), and it advances the
board's `lastRefreshAt` only when at least one vendor actually saved an observation, so a run that fetched
only the exchange-rate table cannot look like a fresh offer check. Board freshness also reports the newest
saved observation and falls back to it for the age when no completion marker exists, so an interrupted run
(for example a redeploy stopping the background job) with fresh saved offers is not labelled never
refreshed, while a recorded but old completion still reports the scheduled pipeline as stopped. A failed
vendor check does not erase the last known good row: the attempt time and reason are stamped on that
offer's existing observation row (or a marker is kept when the offer never succeeded), so the board still
ranks the last successful price and stock while saying the most recent attempt failed, and a later
successful check clears the mark.

`src/lib/policies.js` is the shared, versioned shipping-evidence model. A policy states the vendor,
product/SKU scope, service, destination scope, the amount or free-shipping threshold rule (with the
vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording preserved), the evidence URL and retrieval time, and a `reviewBy`
date. `quoteBoard()` applies the evaluator at read time: an observation whose own shipping is unknown
is enriched with a matching validated policy, while an observation that already carries a fresher
amount, threshold or destination is never overwritten. The evaluator is deterministic and refuses to
guess: conflicting policies for the same scope stay `inconsistent`, a malformed policy is `invalid`,
and a policy past its review date is `expired`, so the offer falls back to explicit unknown shipping
instead of a stale unconditional rate. Enrichment never touches the observation's price, stock,

vendor price/stock check; `policySummary()` exposes the rule version, observation time and review date

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

A public online shopping board for delivery in Israel tracking **one product**: **Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**, with every eligible tracked listing — including a listing whose blend wording is not stated — compared in one board and every pack size or multipack kept as a distinct offer. There is no shopper-facing blend/variant selection (owner correction, 2026-10-12). The board compares actual availability and item price plus shipping for a selected quantity and Israeli locality, with visible source evidence and freshness. Unknown shipping is never silently treated as free, and a published courier rate that the vendor's terms make subject to an unpublished locality list is disclosed as a coverage caveat instead of being assumed country-wide.

The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired the earlier multi-product scope: Lavazza Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte are no longer fetched, ranked or shown. Their old listings survive only as historical evidence in [docs/SOURCES.md](docs/SOURCES.md), labelled as such, and as negative fixtures that prove the adapters refuse them. Re-adding any product line needs an explicit new owner instruction.

Three Israeli vendor adapters currently observe **five real Crema e Gusto listings**: CoffeeMan single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g, Pucks 250 g and Coffee4U 250 g. Swiss signage design, meaningful status colors, no emoji typography.

Vendor conditions are modeled, not hard-coded: browser-researched delivery rules live in validated,
versioned shipping policies (Pucks ₪30 / free above a ₪100 item subtotal, CoffeeMan's published ₪25
single/4-pack courier with its cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center alternative and the ₪20 one-8-pack
checkout quote, Coffee4U's published ₪30 door-to-door rate with its ₪15 pickup-point alternative), and
the CoffeeMan **published quantity promotion** — 10% off the ground-coffee item subtotal from a ₪250
subtotal, multipacks excluded — is parsed from the product-page banner on every refresh and applied to
the item subtotal with the vendor's own wording disclosed in the offer details. A missing rate or a
promotion the vendor stops advertising never becomes a silent zero or an invented discount.

The board is implemented and self-updating: deterministic vendor adapters observe real product pages, a
pure quote engine ranks delivered ILS totals, and a scheduled Durable Object refresh keeps the data
current without a browser or the coding loop. Each refresh keeps the previous successful price and stock
for the same offer, so the board shows the unit-price change since the last check (or explains why a
comparison is impossible), and it reports a completed refresh only when a vendor was actually re-observed.
If a run is interrupted after saving observations, freshness falls back to the newest saved observation
instead of claiming the board never refreshed. A failed vendor check keeps the last successful
observation ranked but stamps the attempt time and reason on it, so the board says the most recent check
failed instead of presenting the row as freshly re-checked. See [current status](docs/STATUS.md),
[observed sources](docs/SOURCES.md), [design](docs/DESIGN.md) and [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

export function coverageQualifier(quote) {
  const shipping = quote.shipping ?? {};
  const parts = [];
  if (shipping.freeThresholdOrigin === 'observed_cart' && shipping.amountIls === 0) {
    parts.push('Free delivery applied from an anonymous-cart observation; confirm it at checkout.');

  if (shipping.coverageCaveat) parts.push('Coverage not confirmed for every locality — full terms under Delivery options.');
  else if (shipping.certainty === 'checkout_quote') parts.push('Rate observed in an anonymous cart; confirm the destination at checkout.');
  else if (shipping.certainty === 'estimated') parts.push('Includes a converted or estimated component.');
  else if (shipping.certainty === 'unknown') parts.push('Shipping not published: a delivered total cannot be established yet.');
  return parts.length ? parts.join(' ') : null;
}

content.text:
through `/api/status`. Four validated policies are checked in: Pucks' ₪30/free-above-₪100 home-delivery
rule, CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule with its cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center
alternative, CoffeeMan's ₪20 checkout quote for the one-8-pack (2 kg) cart (which carries
`maxTotalGrams: 2000` so the quote engine never stretches it to an unobserved larger cart and records
no free threshold for this SKU), and Coffee4U's published ₪30 door-to-door rule with its ₪15
pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list coverage shape. Secondary delivery
methods are part of the policy representation: the evaluator adds them only when a stored row has
none, and they never replace the ranked amount. Each policy is also the adapter's single source for
the researched values it describes, so the parsed row, the read-time evaluator and the tests share one
representation instead of separate hard-coded strings. The adapters honor the same `reviewBy` gate at
parse time (`policyIsCurrent()`): once a policy is past its review date, its researched rate and any
policy-derived alternative are withheld, so a freshly parsed offer falls back to explicit unknown
shipping rather than carrying a stale quote forward. Page-published rates (CoffeeMan's ₪25 and
Coffee4U's ₪30/₪15) are parsed from the vendor page and stay independent of the policy window.

`src/lib/promotions.js` is the shared, validated model for published item-price promotions (quantity
discounts). A promotion states the vendor, product/URL scope, the percent off, the activating
item-subtotal rule (with the vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording preserved), whether multipacks are
excluded, the vendor's own wording and the evidence URL/retrieval time. The adapters parse the vendor's
promotion banner on every fetch (`parseCoffeemanPromotion`), so an ended promotion stops applying with
the next observation; a checked page with no banner records an explicit empty `promotions: []`, which is
never re-enriched. The checked-in fallback (`coffeeman-ground-coffee-percent-off` v1: 10% off ground
coffee from a ₪250 item subtotal, multipacks excluded, observed in the anonymous 8 × 250 g cart at ₪264
→ ₪237.60) only covers persisted rows stored before banner parsing and stops applying past its
`reviewBy`. `quoteOffer()` applies the resolved discount to the item subtotal before shipping, exposes
`itemSubtotalBeforeDiscountIls`/`itemDiscount` and discloses the vendor wording in the offer details;
the base unit price, stock and `observedAt` are never touched, and no shipping discount is inferred
from an item promotion. `promotionSummary()` exposes the rule, percent, threshold and review date
through `/api/status`.

`src/refresh.js` is the deterministic scheduled pipeline (leases, bounded concurrency, per-vendor
backoff, last-known-good retention) and the same function runs in the Worker's `scheduled` handler, the
local cron simulation and tests. Successful vendors count as due up to fifteen minutes before their
stored `nextAttemptAt`, so a cron tick that lands seconds before the six-hour mark still refreshes
instead of silently drifting to a twelve-hour cadence; vendors inside a failure backoff keep their
strict due time. `src/store.js` defines the SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object plus
in-memory and file-backed stores with the same interface. Public routes in `src/index.js` are read-only
snapshots of that storage and never fetch visitor-supplied URLs. A source can also be blocked at the
network edge instead of failing to parse: on 2026-10-13 the production Worker received HTTP 403 for all
three CoffeeMan product pages while the same bounded request (same user agent, headers, crawl delay and
host allowlist) succeeded from the coding runner. The pipeline treats that like any other failure — the

only rendered when something is actually missing.

## Layout and components

- A single centered column (max 1240 px) with a responsive control grid that reflows to one column on
  mobile. No horizontal page scrolling at 1440 px or 390 px.
- **Offer cards** replace the former wide comparison table. The best known delivered offer carries a
  blue rule, the written tag "Best known delivered total" and its selection context; other ranked
  offers state their difference (`+₪x vs best delivered total`).
- Each card keeps the decision values together in one `.totals` row: **item subtotal**, **shipping
  charge, named delivery method and written certainty label** and the **delivered total** plus
  per-kilogram normalization. The method (`Home delivery`, `Pickup-point delivery`,
  `Distribution-center delivery`, `Self-pickup`, or `Delivery method not stated`) is rendered separately
  from the certainty label, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys. When a published quantity
  promotion reduced the subtotal, the item-subtotal cell adds one muted line (`10% promotion applied —
  was ₪264.00`); the vendor's own wording and the evidence stay inside the offer details. On mobile the
  three cells stack but remain in the same card, inside the first viewport.
- Conditions are one short list per offer (free-shipping threshold, minimum order, delivery area,
  alternative services, self-pickup, delivery time, cart-size limit) inside that offer's
  `Delivery options and conditions` disclosure. A coverage caveat is written once inside the same
  disclosure; the card face keeps only a one-line amber qualification. Pickup-only offers live in their
  own collapsed disclosure and never compete in the delivered ranking; each is one compact row (vendor,
  pack/quantity, item subtotal, pickup fee and the written "Self-pickup, not delivery"), with the
  repeated pickup terms behind a `Pickup terms` disclosure.
- Debug/provenance metadata (previous checks, failed attempts, the applied shipping-policy version, the
  applied promotion's vendor wording and evidence, the adapter's shipping terms, shipping evidence, FX,
  per-vendor refresh state, next source check) lives behind `Offer details and check history` /
  `Refresh diagnostics` disclosures instead of the first screen. A cart-observed alternative (for
  example CoffeeMan's distribution-center delivery) carries its cart condition in the short label and
  its full observation in the disclosure.
- Unknown shipping says **"Shipping not published"** with the exact reason and is never shown as zero;
  a published rate with unconfirmed destination coverage is labelled as such, not as a guaranteed
  checkout total.
- A ranked offer whose most recent vendor check failed shows one short amber card-face line
  (`Last check failed — showing the last successful observation.`) directly under its money values;
  the attempt time, the error and the last successful check stay in `Offer details and check history`,
  and the footer names the failing source. This warning is deliberately visible: the price still ranks
  but may be out of date, which can change the shopping decision.

## Iteration 3-82 — CoffeeMan's observed free condition applied at its scope; the 2 kg comparison matches the vendor's own cart (2026-10-13)

**The gap.** The CoffeeMan anonymous-cart research on 2026-10-12 (19:56-20:09 UTC) had already recorded
that home courier was charged ₪25 on the ₪66/₪124/₪132/₪198 carts but **free** from the ₪231

best — even though the vendor's own anonymous cart showed that exact offer at **₪237.60 delivered**. That
is the owner's "store conditional evidence at its actual scope" case, not a rule the board should infer
globally: the ₪240 8-pack SKU cart kept its own ₪20 quote.

**What changed (implementation).**

- `coffeeman-single-4pack-il-home-delivery` is now **v2**: the published ₪25 base rate stays, and the
  policy carries `freeThreshold: ₪231`, `thresholdSemantics: 'at_least'`, `freeThresholdOrigin:
  'observed_cart'` and its own `freeThresholdEvidence` (anonymous checkout, 2026-10-12T20:09:00Z).
  ₪231 is the **lowest observed free subtotal** — the ₪198 cart was charged ₪25 — so the engine can only
  under-promise free delivery below it, never invent it. The ₪240 8-pack SKU has a separate policy with
  its own ₪20 quote and no free threshold.
- The policy validator rejects an unknown threshold origin, an origin without a threshold, and an
  `observed_cart` threshold without evidence; `ruleKey` now includes the threshold semantics/origin so
  two conflicting policies still resolve as `inconsistent`.

  parsed single/4-pack rows while the policy is current. When `reviewBy` passes, the free condition is
  withheld with the policy and the offer falls back to the published ₪25.

  condition `Free shipping threshold met (from ₪231.00, observed in the vendor's anonymous cart)`. The
  product page renders `Free (threshold met)` + `Home delivery` + `Published rate (verified) · free
  condition cart-observed`, a card-face qualifier ("Free delivery applied from an anonymous-cart
  observation; confirm it at checkout.") and the full provenance in `Delivery options` and `Offer
  details`.

**Verified locally (2026-10-13 UTC):**

- `npm run verify` — **155/155** `node:test` cases pass (up from 153; new coverage: the policy shape and
  origin/evidence validation, the old persisted single row gaining the free condition at read time, the
  ₪231 boundary free and the ₪198 cart still charged, the two-4-pack ₪248 cart free, the 8-pack SKU
  keeping ₪20 with no threshold, the expired-policy path withholding the free condition, and the

  the parsed CoffeeMan rows carry the new threshold fields and the updated cart note.
- Fresh-store `wrangler dev` initial refresh (01:24:05.165Z → 01:24:23.281Z, live vendor fetches, no
  browser opened for the refresh): **6 bounded requests**, all three vendors saved, five observations.
  The 2 kg board ranks **CoffeeMan 8 × 250 g singles ₪237.60** (10% promotion → ₪237.60 item, free
  observed threshold, ₪118.80/kg), Pucks ₪240.00 (free above ₪100), CoffeeMan 2 × 4-pack ₪248.00 (free
  observed threshold), CoffeeMan 8-pack ₪260.00 (its own ₪20 quote) and Coffee4U ₪334.00. At 250 g/500 g
  the ranking is unchanged (CoffeeMan ₪58, Pucks ₪90). Evidence:
  `docs/evidence/worker-runtime-status-2026-10-13T0124Z.json`.
- **Every observed anonymous-cart courier amount is reproduced by the engine**
  (`docs/evidence/coffeeman-free-condition-20261013.json`): ₪66→₪25, ₪124→₪25, ₪132→₪25, ₪198→₪25,
  ₪231→free, ₪264/₪237.60→free, ₪248 (2 × 4-pack)→free, ₪240 (8-pack SKU)→₪20. The 8-pack SKU never

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

## Latest owner correction — remove the coffee-variant feature (2026-10-12)

The owner explicitly asks: "Get rid of the coffee variant. There's only two variants and it's the same coffee." Treat the tracked Crema e Gusto listings as **one coffee comparison**, not separate shopper-selectable blends. This latest instruction supersedes every older variant-separation/selector requirement in this prompt, AGENTS.md and the design/architecture/status documentation. Implement it first in the next fresh iteration, then continue the product index, progressive disclosure and shipping-policy work below.

- Remove the blend/variant selector, unobserved-variant menu entries, variant warnings, "other variant" counts/links and variant-as-a-shopping-configuration from the home and product page. Do not replace it with another blend toggle or add variant-specific product cards.
- Compare all eligible tracked Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground offers together for the selected quantity, locality and delivery method. Include the currently "Variant not stated" Coffee4U listing in that same comparison instead of hiding it behind a selector or withholding it as another blend. Offers can still be unavailable/unrankable for genuine stock, freshness, shipping or cart-scope reasons.
- Keep single packs, four-packs and eight-packs as distinct offers with correct whole-pack rounding, purchased grams, item prices, shipping conditions and totals. Removing the variant feature does not merge or duplicate SKUs, pack sizes, cart discounts or service-specific policies.
- Retain original vendor product wording and any raw listing identity metadata in evidence/optional offer details if useful. Do not invent a manufacturer blend or relabel an unstated listing as Classico to make it eligible. Raw wording is provenance, not a default ranking filter or repeated variant badge.
- Remove implicit variant filtering from the default API/quote flow, not just its visible widget. Old shared URLs containing variant=classico/unspecified/etc must still preserve product/quantity/locality but resolve to this unified comparison; discard or ignore the obsolete variant parameter without creating a second view.
- Update AGENTS.md, catalog/public API where appropriate, docs and browser QA so they no longer instruct variant separation. Verify that the single product comparison can include Coffee4U alongside the other Crema e Gusto listings, still names vendors correctly, calculates packs/shipping honestly and has no residual blend control/warning. Existing stock, policy-scope, unknown-shipping and retired-product safeguards remain mandatory.

The active catalog remains Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee only; Oro, Rossa, Suerte and other product lines stay excluded. The home is still the product index with one real card. Keep the Canton Zürich design system, Inter and established semantic palette. Shurik writes the code/tests; the overseer only steers and reviews.

## Current owner priorities — product index, reusable shipping knowledge, progressive disclosure (2026-10-12)

The owner has reviewed the updated website and still finds it very cluttered. The home page must become an overview index of products, with the comparison workflow on a dedicated product page. The owner also expects obvious browser-visible shipping rules, such as Pucks free shipping above ₪100, to be found systematically and actually used by the site. These priorities replace the earlier instruction to repeat the initial shipping investigation first in every fresh iteration. The first Pucks/CoffeeMan/Coffee4U browser investigation is already evidenced in iterations 3-67 through 3-72. Use that evidence; fresh browser work should address a specific missing, contradictory or stale condition. Do not spend whole iterations reproducing unchanged amounts while the requested product/UI work waits.

Shurik implements all code, assets, tests and documentation. The overseer only changes this brief and reviews results. Keep the Canton Zürich design direction, Inter, palette and Crema e Gusto-only active scope below.

### 1. Make the home page a product overview index

- The canonical home route must show a clean product index, not the full vendor comparison board. Render its cards from the active catalog. Today that means **one real card: Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**. Design the structure to support additional products later, but do not add or reactivate Oro, Rossa, Suerte, other product lines, fabricated offerings or placeholder cards. Crema e Gusto offers share one comparison; pack sizes and multipacks remain distinct.
- Each product card links to a real, directly loadable product-detail URL. The home page needs only product identity, a concise useful summary and a clear way to open the comparison. If a summary price is shown, its quantity, destination, freshness and conditional nature must be understandable; do not mix different cart sizes into a misleading "from" price.
- The product page identifies the coffee and provides the quantity/locality/delivery controls and offers. Provide a clear "All products" way back. Preserve shareable selection state and handle existing product/query links, including retired-line fallbacks, without losing quantity or locality; obsolete variant parameters are ignored. Keep existing read-only APIs and deterministic refresh behavior working.
- The home title is "Attention shoppers" without a period. The product-detail heading should name the product, e.g. "Lavazza Crema e Gusto", with compact site branding. Do not reproduce a giant branding hero or comparison explanation on both pages.

### 2. Generalize browser shipping research and deterministic shipping policies

- Reuse the real Chrome/ChromeDriver helper, but build a reusable research workflow with vendor-specific navigation recipes and a common evidence output. It must navigate the product/cart/estimator, select the actual delivery method, set whole-pack quantities and permitted locality/postcode, wait for recalculation, and compare displayed item subtotal, shipping and final total. A subtotal displayed before choosing a method is not a delivered quote: the Pucks cart only adds its ₪30 after the delivery card is selected.
- Research a meaningful cart matrix per SKU/pack/service/destination: normal quantities plus below/above a displayed free-shipping threshold. Capture the threshold language, exclusions, minimum order, fees, delivery methods, locality restrictions, any discount and the exact blocker if a quote requires personal details. Keep the anonymous-cart/locality permission and the no-order/payment/login/account/street-address/bot-bypass restrictions below. Sanitize all URLs and output so cart/session/cookie/token values never enter public records.
- Introduce a common, validated shipping-evidence/policy representation and evaluator used by every adapter/quote: distinguish published rules, observed conditional cart quotes and unknown/inconsistent rules. Preserve service, eligible product/SKU/pack, quantity or weight/subtotal scope, destination scope, currency, amount or threshold rule, source, observed/review time and certainty. Per-vendor recipes may differ; common policy interpretation, arithmetic, evidence storage and validation should be shared. Do not keep accumulating unrelated hard-coded adapter strings as the only shipping model.
- Pucks is the concrete acceptance case: the rendered estimator established **₪30 home delivery and free shipping above the stated ₪100 item subtotal**, including 2 × 250 g = ₪60 + ₪30 = ₪90 and 4 × 250 g = ₪120 with free delivery to Tel Aviv / 6100000. Apply the rule to eligible current offers and show the free-shipping condition in the appropriate delivery details. Preserve the threshold comparison/exclusions actually established by the vendor; do not silently turn "above" into "at least" without checking the boundary semantics. Coverage remains qualified beyond the destinations tested.
- CoffeeMan demonstrates why a single global threshold is insufficient: the ₪240 eight-pack cart still charged ₪20 while some single-pack/two-four-pack carts showed free shipping; the small single/four-pack carts showed a ₪15 distribution-center alternative. Store conditional evidence at its actual scope, and keep unverified rules unresolved. Do not infer a nationwide/free-over-X rule from one cart or flatten SKU/pack distinctions. Scoped discounts and alternatives must not silently change the ranked courier amount beyond their verified applicability.
- **Fix the known-knowledge/old-store gap.** The latest recorded production probes still had old shipping unknowns even after the policies were established and deployed. Implement a safe versioned policy resolution/enrichment or migration so newly validated shipping knowledge can apply to matching persisted offers promptly, without waiting hours for the next item refresh. Choose the mechanism within the existing Worker architecture; keep it deterministic, bounded and compatible with stored data.
