## Iteration 3-85 — CoffeeMan free evidence bound to its observed carts; Coffee4U method recorded; index and locality readability (2026-10-13)

**The defect.** Iteration 3-82 promoted CoffeeMan's free-delivery observation as a monotone threshold
(`₪231, at_least`), so any single/4-pack cart at or above ₪231 would be free. The vendor publishes no such
threshold and the sampled carts are not monotone (a ₪198 cart paid ₪25, the ₪240 8-pack SKU cart paid
₪20, while the ₪231/₪264/₪248 carts were free), so a 3 kg single-pack cart or three 4-packs could inherit
free delivery merely from a subtotal. The same review found the Coffee4U destination-extension evidence
records carried `service: null` even though the runs had successfully selected door-to-door delivery, and
that the home index card still repeated a long comparison explanation while the 390 px locality control
clipped the selected locality inside a half-width column.

**What changed (evidence scope first).**

- `coffeeman-single-4pack-il-home-delivery` is now **v3**. `rule.freeThreshold` is removed; the free
  observations live in `rule.freeCartConditions`, one entry per observed free cart with validated listing
  prefix + SKU, pack count, whole-pack units, ordered grams, item subtotal before any discount, paid item
  total, the named method, destination evidence, observation time and its own evidence note: `singles-7`
  (SKU 930333, 7 units, ₪231), `singles-8` (8 units, ₪264 before the automatic 10% promotion → ₪237.60)
  and `fourpack-2` (SKU 930334, 2 units, ₪248). No threshold is recorded. `supersedes` names the exact
  superseded v2 threshold (₪231, `at_least`, `observed_cart`) so a persisted row stamped by v2 stops
  applying it at read time — the published ₪25 base amount, the item price, stock and `observedAt` are
  untouched — and a rule that changes any amount is still never swapped in at read time.
- The quote engine matches a cart against each condition exactly (listing prefix, SKU, service, pack
  count, units, ordered grams and the pre-discount subtotal, falling back to the paid total when no
  discount applies). A matched cart becomes free with a label naming the exact observed cart; an
  unmatched cart keeps the published ₪25, and when its subtotal is at or above an observed free subtotal
  the card says free delivery was observed only on specific carts. `base.shipping` exposes
  `freeCartConditions`/`freeCondition`; `policySummary()` exposes the condition ids/SKUs/subtotals.
- The CoffeeMan adapter derives its free conditions from the policy (never a hard-coded threshold), and
  the 8-pack SKU policy is unchanged: it keeps its own ₪20 quote and never inherits the conditions.
- **Coffee4U method evidence.** Recipe method steps now declare `confirmsService`; a successful run
  records `service` + `serviceConfirmed: true`, and an optional method step that could not be confirmed
  records `service: null` + `serviceConfirmed: false` plus a qualification (schema validation rejects
  both a claimed-but-unnamed method and an undisclosed unconfirmed one). The nine checked-in Pucks and
  Coffee4U quote records were backfilled from their recorded successful method step with a note saying
  so, and `coffee4u-il-home-delivery` names the method in `observedFor.method`; the public quote output
  keeps `shipping.service`/`serviceLabel` and the quantity/destination restrictions (`maxTotalGrams`,
  closed-locality-list caveat, alternatives) unchanged.
- **Readability.** The home index card is one compact line (`3 vendors · 5 listings: …`) instead of the
  comparison walkthrough, and the catalog intro is one sentence. On ≤720 px the locality group takes the
  full row and the option text drops the redundant “area” suffix, so `Tel Aviv–Yafo · 6100000` is fully
  readable at 390 px (measured width 343 px, label one line).

**Verified locally (2026-10-13 UTC).**

- `npm run verify` — **162/162** `node:test` cases (new/updated: the scoped-condition policy validation,
  exact-cart matching, the v2→v3 read-time migration, the 3 kg/three-4-pack/repriced carts keeping ₪25,
  the expired-policy fallback, and the confirmed/unconfirmed service schema), plus
  `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (bundle builds; bindings `BOARD` + `ASSETS`).
- `npm run evidence:coffeeman-scope` — every observed cart reproduces its recorded fee
  (₪25/₪25/₪25/₪0/₪0/₪25/₪0/₪20) and every unobserved cart keeps ₪25; evidence rewritten at
  `docs/evidence/coffeeman-free-condition-20261013.json` with `reproduced: true`.
- `npm run qa:browser` (offline fixtures) — **94/94** checks, zero console errors. New checks cover the
  exact free condition on the 2 kg card, the 3 kg cart keeping the base rate, the concise home card, the
  full-width readable locality control, and the 2 kg / 500 g CoffeeMan cards with the real
  last-check-failed state. Screenshots and DOM geometry:
  `docs/evidence/visual-review/2026-10-13-coffeeman-scope-and-readability-review.json`,
  `docs/evidence/browser-qa-fixtures-20261013T0240Z.json`.
- `scripts/probe-production.mjs` gained read-only checks for the scoped conditions: the 2 kg single-pack
  cart must apply `singles-8` with `freeThreshold: null`, and the 3 kg cart must keep ₪25; they activate
  once the deployed build serves the new fields, so the probe stays green while the main-push build rolls
  out. The policy-version check now compares the scoped condition ids too.
- PNG limitation (unchanged): the pinned file-read tool rejects image input, so the saved screenshots
  were not inspected as images; the coarse pixel/colour maps and the rendered DOM geometry are recorded
  in the review file, and labels/arithmetic are corroborated by DOM/API assertions, not by image reading.

**Production verification (read-only, 02:42-02:49 UTC):** the main-push build deployed and the scoped
migration is live on the old persisted store **without a vendor refresh** — `/api/status` serves
`coffeeman-single-4pack-il-home-delivery` **v3** with `singles-7`/`singles-8`/`fourpack-2`, the 2 kg board
returns the CoffeeMan single-pack cart free via `singles-8` with `freeThreshold: null`, the 3 kg board
returns 12 singles at the published ₪25 (total ₪381.40; Pucks' 3 kg published-threshold total ₪360 ranks
best), and `lastRefreshAt` is still the 00:18:15.896Z cron completion — so the item price, stock and
observation time were not touched by the policy correction. `npm run probe:production` passed all checks
including the two new scope checks (evidence `docs/evidence/production-probe-20261013T0246Z.json`), and
headless-Chrome QA against the deployed URL passed **90/90** with zero console errors, including the
live-only failed-check warning on the production CoffeeMan rows and the exact-free-condition card
(evidence `docs/evidence/browser-qa-production-20261013T0248Z.json`). The 06:17 UTC cron tick remains the
next actual CoffeeMan vendor attempt; the 00:17 UTC tick's Worker-egress HTTP 403 is still recorded and
not bypassed.

**Next step:** after the **06:17 UTC tick** record whether the CoffeeMan egress block persists and whether
the refreshed rows parse (the scoped conditions are already applied to the old store at read time, so this
is a vendor-egress question, not a policy-delivery question). Continue within Crema e Gusto coverage,
shipping evidence, freshness and comparison quality.

content.text:
# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

A public online shopping board for delivery in Israel tracking **one product**: **Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**, with every eligible tracked listing — including a listing whose blend wording is not stated — compared in one board and every pack size or multipack kept as a distinct offer. There is no shopper-facing blend/variant selection (owner correction, 2026-10-12). The board compares actual availability and item price plus shipping for a selected quantity and Israeli locality, with visible source evidence and freshness. Unknown shipping is never silently treated as free, and a published courier rate that the vendor's terms make subject to an unpublished locality list is disclosed as a coverage caveat instead of being assumed country-wide.

The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired the earlier multi-product scope: Lavazza Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte are no longer fetched, ranked or shown. Their old listings survive only as historical evidence in [docs/SOURCES.md](docs/SOURCES.md), labelled as such, and as negative fixtures that prove the adapters refuse them. Re-adding any product line needs an explicit new owner instruction.

Three Israeli vendor adapters currently observe **five real Crema e Gusto listings**: CoffeeMan single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g, Pucks 250 g and Coffee4U 250 g. Swiss signage design, meaningful status colors, no emoji typography.

Vendor conditions are modeled, not hard-coded: browser-researched delivery rules live in validated,
versioned shipping policies (Pucks ₪30 / free above a ₪100 item subtotal, CoffeeMan's published ₪25
single/4-pack courier with its cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center alternative and its anonymous-cart
free condition from a ₪231 item subtotal, the ₪20 one-8-pack checkout quote, Coffee4U's published ₪30
door-to-door rate with its ₪15 pickup-point alternative), and
the CoffeeMan **published quantity promotion** — 10% off the ground-coffee item subtotal from a ₪250
subtotal, multipacks excluded — is parsed from the product-page banner on every refresh and applied to
the item subtotal with the vendor's own wording disclosed in the offer details. A missing rate or a
promotion the vendor stops advertising never becomes a silent zero or an invented discount.

The board is implemented and self-updating: deterministic vendor adapters observe real product pages, a
pure quote engine ranks delivered ILS totals, and a scheduled Durable Object refresh keeps the data
current without a browser or the coding loop. Each refresh keeps the previous successful price and stock
for the same offer, so the board shows the unit-price change since the last check (or explains why a
comparison is impossible), and it reports a completed refresh only when a vendor was actually re-observed.
If a run is interrupted after saving observations, freshness falls back to the newest saved observation
instead of claiming the board never refreshed. A failed vendor check keeps the last successful
observation ranked but stamps the attempt time and reason on it, so the board says the most recent check
failed instead of presenting the row as freshly re-checked. See [current status](docs/STATUS.md),
[observed sources](docs/SOURCES.md), [design](docs/DESIGN.md) and [architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Coding loop

The workflow uses [igor-makarov/shurik@v1](https://github.com/igor-makarov/shurik), opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash and max reasoning. The owner chose direct work on main and has added the OPENCODE_API_KEY Actions secret. The first handoff is complete; the main loop will develop the tracker while Cloudflare remains disconnected. Check the Actions page and shurik-control/main for live loop state.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is present in Shurik's pinned Pi AI catalog and supports low, high and max reasoning. Its native adapter preserves reasoning content across tool calls. The owner authorized this switch after Step 5 returned repeated unavailable-endpoint errors. No further model fallback is permitted without an owner instruction.

## Deployment and refreshing

The owner reports auto-deploy enabled on main pushes from **Cloudflare Workers Builds** with the
production Worker `attention-shoppers`, already served at
https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev. On 2026-10-12 15:51-15:54 UTC the coding loop
independently verified that public URL from the runner with read-only GETs (no Cloudflare credentials,
admin API or deploy): the site answered HTTP 200, the catalog exposed exactly one product, five
observations were persisted, and a request-triggered initial refresh completed and advanced
`lastRefreshAt`; see
[the production verification evidence](docs/evidence/production-verification-20261012T1554Z.json). The
loop still does not administer the deployment. GitHub stores no CF credentials and has no deployment job.
Cloudflare Cron Triggers run the Worker's scheduled handler about every six hours, and the
SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object defined in `wrangler.jsonc` persists the last known
observations, vendor refresh state, FX rates and run history.

Follow [the deployment notes and outstanding production checks](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). Agent-authored code can affect the CF build and production Worker once auto-deploy is enabled; keeping CF API credentials out of Shurik does not remove that authority.

## Develop locally

Node 24.14.0, pinned dependencies:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run verify          # node:test suite + wrangler deploy --dry-run
npm run check:sources   # live fetch + parse of every tracked vendor page
npm run cron:offline    # full refresh pipeline against recorded fixtures
npm run cron:local      # full refresh pipeline against the live vendor pages
npm run probe:production # read-only GETs against the deployed board (no credentials, no deploy)
npm run dev             # local Worker with a local SQLite Durable Object
```

`probe:production` checks the deployed site from the outside with fixed public GETs only: one catalog
product, no retired row in any board, the retired-URL fallback, freshness and the ranked totals. It never
authenticates or deploys, and it saves a JSON snapshot under `.shurik-local/production/` (or `--out`) so a
later iteration can diff production state; pass `--url http://127.0.0.1:8789` to check a local Worker.

`cron:offline` starts from a clean `.shurik-local/board-offline.json` on every run, so the fixture
pipeline is repeatable and never consumes the live run's schedule. `cron:local` keeps
`.shurik-local/board.json` and honours the same six-hour vendor window as the deployed cron; add
`npm run cron:local -- --fresh` for a manual live run outside that window.

With `npm run dev` running on port 8789, browser QA is self-contained and offline by default:

```sh
npm run qa:browser                            # fixture server + headless Chrome, no network
npm run qa:browser -- http://127.0.0.1:8789   # live: QA a running local Worker
```

The default mode serves `public/` plus fixture-backed API responses from `scripts/qa-server.mjs`, drives
headless Chrome through the desktop and mobile board, and derives expected totals from the API. The live
mode checks the same UI against a Worker you started. The verification build is `wrangler deploy --dry-run`
and does not publish to Cloudflare.

so a validated coverage or re-check update reaches persisted offers promptly; a version that changes
any amount is left for the next vendor refresh and never swapped in at read time. The one deliberate
exception is a rule **correction** declared in the new policy's `supersedes`: when a row stamped by
the same policy id still carries the exact superseded free threshold (amount, currency, semantics and
origin), the evaluator removes that policy-derived threshold and applies the scoped conditions instead,
so a scope error stops applying without waiting for a vendor refresh; the published base amount, the
item price, stock and observation time are untouched. The evaluator is deterministic and refuses to
guess: conflicting policies for the same scope stay `inconsistent`, a malformed policy is `invalid`,
and a policy past its review date is `expired`, so the offer falls back to explicit unknown shipping
instead of a stale unconditional rate. Enrichment never touches the observation's price, stock,
`observedAt` or the refresh completion marker, so applying a newer shipping rule cannot claim a fresh
vendor price/stock check; `policySummary()` exposes the rule version, observation time, review date and
scoped condition ids through `/api/status`. Four validated policies are checked in: Pucks'
₪30/free-above-₪100 home-delivery rule v2 (its coverage caveat names the five selectable localities
sampled in the estimator), CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule **v3** with its cart-observed
₪15 distribution-center alternative and the exact cart-observed free conditions (7 singles at ₪231,
8 singles at ₪264 → ₪237.60 and 2 × 4-pack at ₪248; a ₪198 cart was charged ₪25 and the sampled carts
are not monotone, so no threshold is recorded and a larger or repriced cart keeps the published base
rate), CoffeeMan's ₪20 checkout quote for the one-8-pack (2 kg) cart (which carries
`maxTotalGrams: 2000` so the quote engine never stretches it to an unobserved larger cart and records
no free condition for this SKU), and Coffee4U's published ₪30 door-to-door rule with its ₪15
pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list coverage shape. Secondary delivery
methods are part of the policy representation: the evaluator adds them only when a stored row has
none, and they never replace the ranked amount. Each policy is also the adapter's single source for
the researched values it describes, so the parsed row, the read-time evaluator and the tests share one
representation instead of separate hard-coded strings. The adapters honor the same `reviewBy` gate at
parse time (`policyIsCurrent()`): once a policy is past its review date, its researched rate and any
policy-derived alternative are withheld, so a freshly parsed offer falls back to explicit unknown
shipping rather than carrying a stale quote forward. Page-published rates (CoffeeMan's ₪25 and
Coffee4U's ₪30/₪15) are parsed from the vendor page and stay independent of the policy window.

# Canton Zürich design system (web-application patterns)

Owner direction, 2026-10-12. This supersedes the earlier generic Swiss transport-signage brief. The
shopping board adapts the **Canton Zürich design system** for a compact web service: flat surfaces,
strict alignment, a responsive grid, a clear type hierarchy and concise disclosures. The product
identity stays our own; there is no cantonal crest, government wordmark or implied affiliation.

Primary references read before implementation:

- Design system overview — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html
- Colors — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/farben.html
- Typography — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/typografie.html

## Tokens and roles

| Token | Value | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blau | `#0070B4` | Selected shopping context, the clearly labelled best known delivered offer, links and the focus outline. Used sparingly; vendor names are never painted arbitrary colors. |
| Softblau | `#EDF5FA` | Panel/background for the selected context and the best-offer rule. |
| Black | `#000000` | Primary text and neutral structure. |
| Secondary text | `#666666` | Notes, meta and secondary labels. |
| Surface | `#F7F7F7` | Subtle section surfaces. |
| Divider | `#CCCCCC` | Rules and cell borders. |
| Green | `#1A7F1F` on `#EBF6EB` | Verified in-stock labels only, always with the written status. |
| Red | `#D93C1A` on white | Unavailable/error labels only. |
| Amber | `#8A4B00` on `#FFF4E5` | Unknown shipping, unconfirmed coverage and stale evidence. This is a deliberate shopping-specific extension, **not** an official Canton Zürich token; it preserves the owner's uncertainty semantics. |
| Cyan | `#009EE0` | Non-text active indicator only (3.01:1 on white, so it is never used for small text). |
| Focus | `#0070B4` | 3 px outline on every focusable control (5.28:1 on white, 4.79:1 on Softblau). |

Meaning is never carried by color alone: every status keeps a written label (`In stock (observed)`,
`Shipping not published`, `Published rate (verified)`, `Checkout rate (observed, conditional)`,
`Coverage: …`) and the selected state is distinct. A rate that exists only in the vendor's anonymous
cart/checkout estimator is never called a published rate: it uses the `Checkout rate (observed,
conditional)` label so its quantity/destination condition stays visible.

Current state (2026-10-12): handoff 1 (OpenCode key plus loop control) is complete, and the owner
reports the Cloudflare side connected and serving **https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev**
with the production Worker name `attention-shoppers`. On 2026-10-12 15:51-15:54 UTC the coding loop

in docs/evidence/production-verification-20261012T1554Z.json. The loop still does not administer

## 1. OpenCode key

Add OPENCODE_API_KEY under repository Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret. Paste it only in GitHub's secret form, never into chat, a prompt, a dispatch input or a commit.

The repository variable SHURIK_ENABLED starts false, so scheduled recovery and manual dispatch cannot start a model loop before setup is finished. The owner has added the key and authorized DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on OpenCode Go. After the key is present, the maintainer sets SHURIK_ENABLED true and dispatches:

```sh
gh workflow run shurik.yml --repo igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting --ref main \
  -f command=start -f loop_id=main -f seconds=1800
```

Provider, model and reasoning are fixed in the workflow's control action to opencode-go / deepseek-v4.1-flash / max. Further model changes require an owner instruction and a workflow update. The initial loop writes directly to main. Unless a deadline is supplied it continues until stopped, including after ordinary agent answers. Provider availability and the owner's OpenCode Go allowance apply.

To stop, dispatch command=stop and loop_id=main. Record the durable stop before turning SHURIK_ENABLED false. To resume, use command=resume, loop_id=main; the workflow supplies max reasoning again and updates the saved model to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Control/session history and Actions logs are public; do not add private material to this task.

## 2. Cloudflare Git integration

Expected as configured by the owner; the coding loop does not administer Cloudflare. The owner connects the repo from the Cloudflare dashboard, not through Shurik.

- Workers & Pages → Create application → Import a repository.
- Select igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting.
- Worker name: `attention-shoppers` (must match `name` in wrangler.jsonc).
- Production branch: main. Root directory: repository root.
- Build command: `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run verify`. The verify script runs the node:test suite and `wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir dist`, which builds the Worker bundle locally without any Cloudflare credential. Confirm Node 24.14.0 where supported.
- Deploy command: `npx --no-install wrangler deploy`.
- Disable builds and previews for non-production branches, especially `shurik-control/*`.
- Keep CF credentials inside Cloudflare. No CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or CF account secret belongs in GitHub.
- Minimum token scope for Workers Builds: Workers Scripts:Edit for this Worker only (the deploy command creates/updates the script and applies the Durable Object migration). No account-wide or unrelated permissions are needed. The runtime needs no administrative credential at all.

## Required bindings and provisioning

`wrangler.jsonc` declares everything; the owner needs no manual dashboard resource creation:

| Binding | Type | Provisioning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env.BOARD` | Durable Object, class `BoardStore`, SQLite-backed | Created by migration tag `v1` (`new_sqlite_classes: ["BoardStore"]`) during `wrangler deploy` |
| `env.ASSETS` | Static assets from `public/` | Packaged from the repository |

Nothing else is required: the Worker persists observations, vendor refresh state, FX rates and run history in the Durable Object's SQLite tables (`observations`, `vendor_state`, `meta`, `runs`; refresh leases live under `meta` as `lease:*` keys) and reads vendor pages over plain outbound HTTPS.

Alternative storage was considered and rejected: KV or R2 would add a separate consistency problem and still need a migration path for the lease/last-known-good semantics; the SQLite-backed Durable Object is created by the deployment itself with no extra credential.

## Cron behavior

- `wrangler.jsonc` triggers the scheduled handler on `17 */6 * * *` (UTC), about every six hours.
- A successful vendor is stored as due at `run time + 6 h`. Because the cron fires on fixed clock times, a successful vendor also counts as due up to 15 minutes early (`EARLY_DUE_TOLERANCE_MS` in `src/refresh.js`). Without that tolerance a tick landing seconds before the due time skips every vendor, the board drifts to a twelve-hour cadence and reports stale for hours between runs; vendors inside a failure backoff keep their strict due time, so backoff is not weakened.
- The first tick after an off-phase initial refresh can legitimately record a run that saves nothing because every vendor is still inside its six-hour window. That run appears in the run history but does not advance `lastRefreshAt` (no offer was re-observed); the following tick refreshes normally.
- The first `GET /health` or `GET /api/board` after a deployment starts one initial refresh in the background so the board is not empty until the first cron tick. It is lease- and throttle-protected (10 minutes) and can never be triggered repeatedly by public traffic.
- Each run fetches at most one URL per tracked offer plus the Bank of Israel rate file, capped at two vendors concurrently, 12 s per request and 1.5 MB per response, with hosts restricted to each adapter's allowlist. Five Crema e Gusto offers from three independent vendors (CoffeeMan, Pucks, Coffee4U) are tracked today; the product and offers are visible in `/api/catalog`.

# Observed sources and vendor research

**Active scope (owner correction, 2026-10-12): Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee only.**
The Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte listings further down are **historical evidence** from earlier
iterations. They are not fetch targets, not part of the active catalog, and their page excerpts live in
`tests/fixtures/historical-retired/` as negative test inputs. Historical evidence does not authorize
re-adding a product line; that needs an explicit new owner instruction.

All observations below were retrieved by the deterministic adapters in `src/vendors/`
through the bounded fetcher. Re-run them at any time with `npm run check:sources`;
each run writes its evidence to `.shurik-local/sources/<timestamp>.json`; review snapshots are copied to
`docs/evidence/`.

## Tracked listings (live checks)

### Browser-researched shipping quotes (2026-10-12)

The owner asked for shipping quotes through a real interactive browser rather than product-page disclaimers.
`scripts/browser-research.mjs` kept one headless Chrome/ChromeDriver session alive to navigate each
vendor's product page, add the tracked product to a temporary anonymous cart, open the public
cart/checkout estimator and read the rendered delivery methods and charges. Only locality/postcode fields
were filled; no order, payment, login, account or street address was involved, and cart/session
identifiers are never recorded.

| Vendor | Cart | Locality | Service | Shipping | Item subtotal | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pucks | 2 × 250 g = 500 g | Tel Aviv / 6100000 | home delivery (only method) | ₪30 | ₪60 | free above ₪100 item subtotal; fee unchanged for Eilat / 8800000, no restriction displayed |
| Pucks | 4 × 250 g = 1 kg | Tel Aviv / 6100000 | home delivery | free | ₪120 | free-shipping threshold met; a 1 kg cart to Jerusalem / 9100000 reproduced free delivery on 2026-10-12T22:24Z with the same “free above ₪100” wording (`2026-10-12-pucks-jerusalem-1kg-recipe.json`) |
| CoffeeMan | 8 × 250 g = 2 kg | not requested by the estimator | home courier / distribution center | ₪20 / ₪20 | ₪240 | re-checked in a fresh cart at 20:07 UTC; still no published free-delivery threshold, and this SKU cart did not get the free delivery other large carts received |
| CoffeeMan | 8 × 250 g = 2 kg | not requested | self-pickup | ₪0 | ₪240 | a pickup branch must be chosen |
| CoffeeMan | 2 × 250 g = 500 g | not requested by the estimator | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / ₪15 | ₪66 | courier matches the product page; the ₪15 distribution-center rate is cart-observed, not published |
| CoffeeMan | 4 × 250 g = 1 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / ₪15 | ₪132 | same fee schedule as the 4-pack cart at 1 kg |
| CoffeeMan | 1 × 4-pack = 1 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / ₪15 | ₪124 | 4-pack product page rate confirmed in the cart |
| CoffeeMan | 6 × 250 g = 1.5 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | ₪25 / free | ₪198 | distribution-center fee dropped to free while the courier stayed ₪25 — below the observed free courier subtotal |
| CoffeeMan | 7 × 250 g = 1.75 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | free / free | ₪231 | free delivery observed on this exact cart; no rule is published, so the observation is stored as one exact cart condition (listing SKU 930333, 7 units, ₪231 subtotal), never as a monotone threshold |
| CoffeeMan | 8 × 250 g = 2 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | free / free | ₪264 → ₪237.60 | both free; the 10% automatic promotion also applied. Stored as an exact cart condition (8 units, ₪264 subtotal before the promotion, ₪237.60 paid) |
| CoffeeMan | 2 × 4-pack = 2 kg | not requested | home courier / distribution center | free / free | ₪248 | free at ₪248, unlike the ₪240 8-pack SKU cart. Stored as an exact cart condition (SKU 930334, 2 units, ₪248 subtotal); never flattened into a threshold |
| Coffee4U | 1 × 250 g | not requested | door-to-door courier | ₪30 | ₪38 | 1,270-entry destination city list; locality-list caveat |
| Coffee4U | 1 × 250 g | not requested | Chiita Shops pickup point | ₪15 | ₪38 | 421-city list plus a per-city spot |
| Coffee4U | 1 × 250 g | not requested | self-pickup | ₪0 | ₪38 | pickup at the Tel Aviv shop |

Full evidence matrix, rendered-text excerpts and screenshots: `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-vendor-shipping-quotes.json` (observed 18:07-18:19 UTC) plus the fresh Pucks re-check `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-recheck.json` (observed 18:55 UTC), the independent all-vendor re-check `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-fresh-recheck-3-69.json` (observed 19:07-19:16 UTC, which reproduced the same amounts and added the note that Pucks applies the ₪30 to the summary total only after a delivery method is selected), the CoffeeMan single/4-pack cart batch `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-coffeeman-cart-single-4pack.json` (observed 19:56-20:09 UTC, which resolved the unpublished distribution-center fee and the cart-dependent free-delivery behavior) and the recipe-driven Pucks Jerusalem run `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-jerusalem-1kg-recipe.json` (observed 2026-10-12T22:24Z; 4 × 250 g = ₪120 subtotal, free delivery, “free above ₪100”, with the `#city`/`#zip` fields filled and read back). The available file-read tool rejects PNG input, so the screenshots could not be read as images by the model; every amount above is backed by rendered DOM text captured in the same session, and the screenshots are artifacts for a human reviewer. Since iteration 3-70 `scripts/inspect-screenshot.mjs` additionally decodes the PNGs with node:zlib and renders a coarse luminance map plus a Canton Zürich token-pixel report, so layout and colour regions can be checked without image input (see `docs/evidence/visual-review/2026-10-12-revised-layout-review.json`). A cart quote is conditional on its recorded quantity and destination: it is not an unconditional nationwide rate and not a completed checkout.

**Certainty labels:** a rate published on the vendor's product page keeps `certainty: verified` and the label `Published rate (verified)`. A rate that only exists in the vendor's anonymous cart/checkout estimator is stored as `certainty: checkout_quote` and rendered as `Checkout rate (observed, conditional)` (Pucks and the CoffeeMan 8 × 250 g cart). Coffee4U publishes its courier and pickup-point rates on the product page, so it keeps `verified`. A published rate whose free condition was observed in the anonymous cart keeps the published certainty for the base amount and adds `· free condition cart-observed` plus a written qualifier when the free condition actually applies, so an observed free delivery is never presented as a verified unconditional rate. CoffeeMan's free observations are stored as **exact cart conditions** (`rule.freeCartConditions`: listing prefix + SKU, pack count, whole-pack units, ordered grams, item subtotal before discount and paid item total, named method, destination evidence and observation time). The quote engine applies free delivery only when the current cart matches one of them exactly; a larger or repriced cart keeps the published ₪25 base rate, and the card says the free condition was observed only on specific carts.

**Versioned policy promotion and staleness (iterations 3-73, 3-76 and 3-77):** a validated quote is promoted by hand into `src/lib/policies.js` as a versioned policy (vendor, product/SKU scope, service, destination scope, amount or free-shipping rule with the vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording, secondary delivery alternatives, evidence URL and retrieval time, `reviewBy`). The read-time evaluator in the same module enriches an observation whose own shipping is unknown, never overwrites a fresher parsed rate, treats conflicting policies as `inconsistent`, and stops applying a policy once `reviewBy` passes (the offer then shows explicit unknown shipping again). Four policies are checked in: Pucks' ₪30 / free-above-₪100 rule is `pucks-il-home-delivery` v2, observed 2026-10-12T18:10:10Z and extended on 2026-10-13T01:41:10Z to the remaining selectable localities (Haifa and Be’er Sheva below the threshold, Haifa free above it); CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule is `coffeeman-single-4pack-il-home-delivery` **v3** with the cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center alternative and the exact cart-observed free conditions (`rule.freeCartConditions`): 7 singles (SKU 930333, ₪231), 8 singles (₪264 before the automatic 10% promotion, ₪237.60 paid) and 2 × 4-pack (SKU 930334, ₪248), each with its own evidence from 2026-10-12T20:09:00Z. No threshold is recorded — the sampled carts are not monotone (the ₪198 cart was charged ₪25 while the ₪240 8-pack SKU cart was charged ₪20). v3 names the superseded v2 threshold (₪231, `at_least`) in `supersedes`, so a persisted row stamped by v2 stops applying it at read time and keeps only the published base rate plus the scoped conditions; a rule that changes any amount is still never swapped in at read time; CoffeeMan's ₪20 one-8-pack (2 kg) checkout quote is `coffeeman-8pack-il-cart-quote` v1, observed 2026-10-12T20:07:00Z and scoped to the 8-pack offer URL with `maxTotalGrams: 2000`, no free threshold and the observed ₪20 distribution-center alternative; Coffee4U's published ₪30 door-to-door rule is `coffee4u-il-home-delivery` v1 with the ₪15 pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list coverage shape (observed 2026-10-12T20:25:00Z). All carry `reviewBy` 2026-11-11; re-checking the rendered estimator or the product page renews the evidence and version, and `/api/status` exposes the current version, service, alternative ids, observation time and review date. Each policy is also the adapter's single source for the researched values it describes, so the parsed row, the read-time evaluator and the tests share one representation. Enrichment never changes the offer's price/stock observation time or the refresh completion marker. Since iteration 3-78 the adapters honor the same review window at parse time (`policyIsCurrent()`): once a policy is past its review date, its researched rate and any policy-derived alternative are withheld, so a freshly parsed offer falls back to explicit unknown shipping instead of carrying a stale quote; page-published rates (CoffeeMan's ₪25, Coffee4U's ₪30/₪15) stay because they are parsed from the vendor page, not from the policy.

**Recipe-driven rechecks:** `scripts/research-workflow.mjs` defines per-vendor navigation recipes (Pucks, CoffeeMan, Coffee4U) and one common evidence schema (`browser-research-quote`, schema v1). `npm run research:browser -- recipes` lists them and `npm run research:browser -- recipe <id> --grams 500 --locality "תל אביב" --postcode 6100000 --out <file>` executes one against the live Chrome session, then writes a sanitized record whose `status` is `quoted`, `partial` (rate read but cart quantity unverified or arithmetic inconsistent), `blocked` (public flow stopped, with the exact step and rendered excerpt) or `failed`. URLs lose query strings/fragments and session/token-like runs are redacted before anything is written. A live Pucks recipe run on 2026-10-12 21:06-21:10 UTC verified the product page and the add-to-cart label (`הוסף לעגלה`, cart showed 1 × 250 g = ₪30) but direct navigation to `https://pucks.co.il/payment/request` did not keep the cart in that session; the cart-checkout link (`a.slide_cart__btn-checkout`) is now a recipe step and reached the estimator. Iteration 3-76 fixed the destination step after a live run recorded a locality that was never set: the Pucks estimator's only `<select>` is the language dropdown, so the recipe now fills the named `#city` and `#zip` text inputs as **required** steps (a run that cannot set them is `blocked`, not attributed to a destination) and each `fill` records the value the page actually holds in the evidence steps. Destination-setting steps are marked `verifies: 'destination'`; the runner compares what was set with what was requested, records `destinationVerified` (`true`/`false`/`null`) and, when a requested locality could not be verified, adds a qualification to the record (a quoted record with `destinationVerified: false` fails schema validation without that disclosure). Live records back this: `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-jerusalem-1kg-recipe.json` (1 kg Jerusalem, free over ₪100) and `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-12-pucks-telaviv-500g-recipe-verified.json` (500 g Tel Aviv, ₪60 + ₪30 = ₪90, `destinationVerified: true`, `#city`/`#zip` readbacks recorded), plus the 2026-10-13 destination-extension runs for Haifa and Be’er Sheva (`docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-13-pucks-*.json`, summarized in `2026-10-13-pucks-destination-extension.json`). Since iteration 3-85 a method-selection step can declare `confirmsService`, and the runner records the confirmed delivery method in the shared schema (`service` plus `serviceConfirmed`): a quoted record whose method step succeeded carries the method the shipping line belongs to, while a record whose optional method step could not be confirmed carries `service: null`, `serviceConfirmed: false` and a qualification saying the shipping line is not attributed to a named method (schema validation enforces both). The Coffee4U destination-extension runs selected the door-to-door method and their records were backfilled from the recorded successful step (`"selected: שליחות מדלת לדלת עד 1-5 ימי עסקים - 30 ₪"`) with a note saying so; the Coffee4U policy also names the method in `observedFor.method`.

### CoffeeMan / Amigo — coffeeman.co.il (Israel)

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

A public online shopping board for delivery in Israel tracking **one product**: **Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**, with every eligible tracked listing — including a listing whose blend wording is not stated — compared in one board and every pack size or multipack kept as a distinct offer. There is no shopper-facing blend/variant selection (owner correction, 2026-10-12). The board compares actual availability and item price plus shipping for a selected quantity and Israeli locality, with visible source evidence and freshness. Unknown shipping is never silently treated as free, and a published courier rate that the vendor's terms make subject to an unpublished locality list is disclosed as a coverage caveat instead of being assumed country-wide.

The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired the earlier multi-product scope: Lavazza Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte are no longer fetched, ranked or shown. Their old listings survive only as historical evidence in [docs/SOURCES.md](docs/SOURCES.md), labelled as such, and as negative fixtures that prove the adapters refuse them. Re-adding any product line needs an explicit new owner instruction.

Three Israeli vendor adapters currently observe **five real Crema e Gusto listings**: CoffeeMan single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g, Pucks 250 g and Coffee4U 250 g. The interface follows the **Canton Zürich design system** (official Blau/Softblau palette, Inter, flat service patterns, concise disclosures), with meaningful status colors and no emoji typography.

Vendor conditions are modeled, not hard-coded: browser-researched delivery rules live in validated,
versioned shipping policies (Pucks ₪30 / free above a ₪100 item subtotal, CoffeeMan's published ₪25
single/4-pack courier with its cart-observed ₪15 distribution-center alternative and its **exact
cart-observed free conditions** — 7 singles at ₪231, 8 singles at ₪264 → ₪237.60 and 2 × 4-packs at
₪248; the vendor publishes no threshold and the sampled carts are not monotone, so no larger cart
inherits free delivery from its subtotal alone — the ₪20 one-8-pack checkout quote, Coffee4U's published
₪30 door-to-door rate with its ₪15 pickup-point alternative), and
the CoffeeMan **published quantity promotion** — 10% off the ground-coffee item subtotal from a ₪250
subtotal, multipacks excluded — is parsed from the product-page banner on every refresh and applied to
the item subtotal with the vendor's own wording disclosed in the offer details. A missing rate or a
promotion the vendor stops advertising never becomes a silent zero or an invented discount.

content.text:
44:**Certainty labels:** a rate published on the vendor's product page keeps `certainty: verified` and the label `Published rate (verified)`. A rate that only exists in the vendor's anonymous cart/checkout estimator is stored as `certainty: checkout_quote` and rendered as `Checkout rate (observed, conditional)` (Pucks and the CoffeeMan 8 × 250 g cart). Coffee4U publishes its courier and pickup-point rates on the product page, so it keeps `verified`. A published rate whose free condition was observed in the anonymous cart keeps the published certainty for the base amount and adds `· free condition cart-observed` plus a written qualifier when the free condition actually applies, so an observed free delivery is never presented as a verified unconditional rate. CoffeeMan's free observations are stored as **exact cart conditions** (`rule.freeCartConditions`: listing prefix + SKU, pack count, whole-pack units, ordered grams, item subtotal before discount and paid item total, named method, destination evidence and observation time). The quote engine applies free delivery only when the current cart matches one of them exactly; a larger or repriced cart keeps the published ₪25 base rate, and the card says the free condition was observed only on specific carts.
57:  - Cart research (2026-10-12 19:56-20:09 UTC, anonymous cart): the 500 g and 1 kg carts quoted ₪25 home courier (matching the page) and ₪15 distribution-center delivery up to 5 kg; the distribution-center fee became free at a ₪198 (1.5 kg) cart and the courier at ₪231 (1.75 kg). The free-delivery rule is not published and the sampled carts are not monotone: the ₪198 cart was charged ₪25, the ₪240 8-pack SKU cart was charged ₪20, and only the exact 7-singles (₪231), 8-singles (₪264 → ₪237.60) and 2 × 4-pack (₪248) carts were free. The free observations are therefore stored as **exact cart conditions** (`rule.freeCartConditions`, policy v3) rather than a threshold: the quote engine applies free delivery only when the current cart matches an observed configuration exactly (listing prefix/SKU, pack count, units, ordered grams and item subtotal before any discount). content.text:
`Distribution-center delivery`, `Self-pickup`, or `Delivery method not stated`) is rendered separately
  from the certainty label, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys. When a published quantity
  promotion reduced the subtotal, the item-subtotal cell adds one muted line (`10% promotion applied —
  was ₪264.00`); the vendor's own wording and the evidence stay inside the offer details. On mobile the
  three cells stack but remain in the same card, inside the first viewport.
- Conditions are one short list per offer (free-shipping threshold, minimum order, delivery area,
  alternative services, self-pickup, delivery time, cart-size limit) inside that offer's
  `Delivery options and conditions` disclosure. A coverage caveat is written once inside the same
  disclosure; the card face keeps only a one-line amber qualification. A free condition that comes
  from an anonymous-cart observation is written as observed and conditional. CoffeeMan's free
  observations are exact cart conditions, not a threshold: when the current cart matches one, the
  shipping cell reads `Free (observed for this cart)`, the certainty line adds
  `free condition cart-observed`, and the qualifier names the exact observed cart and says it must be
  confirmed at checkout; when the cart does not match (for example 3 kg of singles), the published base
  rate is shown and, if the subtotal is at or above an observed free subtotal, the qualifier says free
  delivery was observed only on specific carts. A published threshold (Pucks' free above ₪100) keeps
  the `Free (threshold met)` wording. An observed free condition is never merged into the published
  rate label. Pickup-only offers live in their
  own collapsed disclosure and never compete in the delivered ranking; each is one compact row (vendor,
  pack/quantity, item subtotal, pickup fee and the written "Self-pickup, not delivery"), with the
  repeated pickup terms behind a `Pickup terms` disclosure.

## Latest owner correction — remove the coffee-variant feature (2026-10-12)

The owner explicitly asks: "Get rid of the coffee variant. There's only two variants and it's the same coffee." Treat the tracked Crema e Gusto listings as **one coffee comparison**, not separate shopper-selectable blends. This latest instruction supersedes every older variant-separation/selector requirement in this prompt, AGENTS.md and the design/architecture/status documentation. Implement it first in the next fresh iteration, then continue the product index, progressive disclosure and shipping-policy work below.

- Remove the blend/variant selector, unobserved-variant menu entries, variant warnings, "other variant" counts/links and variant-as-a-shopping-configuration from the home and product page. Do not replace it with another blend toggle or add variant-specific product cards.
- Compare all eligible tracked Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground offers together for the selected quantity, locality and delivery method. Include the currently "Variant not stated" Coffee4U listing in that same comparison instead of hiding it behind a selector or withholding it as another blend. Offers can still be unavailable/unrankable for genuine stock, freshness, shipping or cart-scope reasons.
- Keep single packs, four-packs and eight-packs as distinct offers with correct whole-pack rounding, purchased grams, item prices, shipping conditions and totals. Removing the variant feature does not merge or duplicate SKUs, pack sizes, cart discounts or service-specific policies.
- Retain original vendor product wording and any raw listing identity metadata in evidence/optional offer details if useful. Do not invent a manufacturer blend or relabel an unstated listing as Classico to make it eligible. Raw wording is provenance, not a default ranking filter or repeated variant badge.
- Remove implicit variant filtering from the default API/quote flow, not just its visible widget. Old shared URLs containing variant=classico/unspecified/etc must still preserve product/quantity/locality but resolve to this unified comparison; discard or ignore the obsolete variant parameter without creating a second view.
- Update AGENTS.md, catalog/public API where appropriate, docs and browser QA so they no longer instruct variant separation. Verify that the single product comparison can include Coffee4U alongside the other Crema e Gusto listings, still names vendors correctly, calculates packs/shipping honestly and has no residual blend control/warning. Existing stock, policy-scope, unknown-shipping and retired-product safeguards remain mandatory.

The active catalog remains Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee only; Oro, Rossa, Suerte and other product lines stay excluded. The home is still the product index with one real card. Keep the Canton Zürich design system, Inter and established semantic palette. Shurik writes the code/tests; the overseer only steers and reviews.

## Overseer review follow-up — bind cart evidence to its actual scope, then finish shopping readability (2026-10-13)

This is review feedback under the existing owner shipping/UX brief, not a change to the one-product/no-blend correction above. Address the evidence-scope defect first in the next fresh iteration. Shurik implements the changes and tests; the overseer edits only this brief.

- **Do not infer a monotone CoffeeMan threshold from sampled carts.** The 3-82 policy makes every eligible single/4-pack cart at or above ₪231 free, with no cart-size cap. The vendor publishes no such threshold. Observing free courier for 7 singles (₪231), 8 singles (₪264 before the 10% promotion / ₪237.60 after it), and two 4-packs (₪248) does not establish free delivery for every larger or otherwise unobserved cart. Calling this inference "conservative" does not prove it. Preserve the correct, explicitly conditional results for those observed cart configurations, and the separate one-eight-pack ₪20 quote; represent the free observations with validated SKU/pack count, whole-pack quantity, item-subtotal/discount, named-method, destination-evidence and review scope. Outside the verified scope, retain the published base fee or explicit unresolved condition instead of inventing zero shipping. A general threshold is acceptable only with a new published rule or browser evidence that actually supports the stated range and limits. Do not add unrelated products or infer a universal CoffeeMan rule.
- Verify that the saved cart examples still reproduce their recorded fees, while an unobserved larger cart (for example 3 kg of singles or three 4-packs) cannot inherit free delivery merely because its subtotal exceeds ₪231. Check expired/conflicting evidence and price/promotion changes too. Keep read-time enrichment honest: no price/stock/observedAt/lastRefreshAt advance, no stretching the eight-pack quote, and no merging distinct packs/SKUs.
- The Coffee4U extractor now correctly records ₪76 + ₪30 = ₪106 for Jerusalem, Haifa and Be’er Sheva. Keep that fix. However, those common evidence records still carry `service: null` despite a successful step selecting door-to-door delivery. Record the actual confirmed method in the reusable evidence schema and preserve method/quantity/destination restrictions through policy interpretation and public quote output. Retain exact public-flow blockers when a required field or quote genuinely cannot be obtained; an extractor failure is not a vendor restriction.
- After the scope fix, finish the outstanding shopping readability work: the home card still repeats a long explanation of how comparison works, and the mobile locality label is clipped. Make the one-card index concise and the selected locality readable. Preserve the dedicated/shareable product route, quantity/locality state, all eligible Crema e Gusto listings, native keyboard disclosures and necessary stock/failure/conditional/stale warnings.
- Inspect and save readable views of the affected offer, not just the page top. Cover both 500 g and the 2 kg CoffeeMan winner on mobile (including the real last-check-failed state), with the actual vendor, accurate purchased packs/grams, item subtotal, named shipping method/charge and delivered total visible in the first 390×844 viewport. Save desktop/home views too. If the pinned PNG reader still rejects images, say so; DOM geometry and pixel maps are not native image inspection. Do not relaunch identical quote probes as a substitute for the scope/UI implementation.

CoffeeMan's production Worker requests returned HTTP 403 at the 00:17 cron while runner requests succeeded. Keep last-known-good observations and visible failure warnings; do not bypass vendor controls or administer Cloudflare. The next scheduled production retry is 06:17 UTC, so work on the scoped evidence and shopping UI rather than claiming a separate retry at the backoff-due timestamp.

## Current owner priorities — product index, reusable shipping knowledge, progressive disclosure (2026-10-12)

The owner has reviewed the updated website and still finds it very cluttered. The home page must become an overview index of products, with the comparison workflow on a dedicated product page. The owner also expects obvious browser-visible shipping rules, such as Pucks free shipping above ₪100, to be found systematically and actually used by the site. These priorities replace the earlier instruction to repeat the initial shipping investigation first in every fresh iteration. The first Pucks/CoffeeMan/Coffee4U browser investigation is already evidenced in iterations 3-67 through 3-72. Use that evidence; fresh browser work should address a specific missing, contradictory or stale condition. Do not spend whole iterations reproducing unchanged amounts while the requested product/UI work waits.

Shurik implements all code, assets, tests and documentation. The overseer only changes this brief and reviews results. Keep the Canton Zürich design direction, Inter, palette and Crema e Gusto-only active scope below.

### 1. Make the home page a product overview index

Crema e Gusto offers share one comparison; pack sizes and multipacks remain distinct.

Preserve shareable selection state and handle existing product/query links, including retired-line fallbacks, without losing quantity or locality; obsolete variant parameters are ignored. - Introduce a common, validated shipping-evidence/policy representation and evaluator used by every adapter/quote: distinguish published rules, observed conditional cart quotes and unknown/inconsistent rules. Apply the rule to eligible current offers and show the free-shipping condition in the appropriate delivery details. Preserve the threshold comparison/exclusions actually established by the vendor; do not silently turn "above" into "at least" without checking the boundary semantics. Coverage remains qualified beyond the destinations tested.
- CoffeeMan demonstrates why a single global threshold is insufficient: the ₪240 eight-pack cart still charged ₪20 while some single-pack/two-four-pack carts showed free shipping; the small single/four-pack carts showed a ₪15 distribution-center alternative. Scoped discounts and alternatives must not silently change the ranked courier amount beyond their verified applicability.
- **Fix the known-knowledge/old-store gap.** The latest recorded production probes still had old shipping unknowns even after the policies were established and deployed. Implement a safe versioned policy resolution/enrichment or migration so newly validated shipping knowledge can apply to matching persisted offers promptly, without waiting hours for the next item refresh. Choose the mechanism within the existing Worker architecture; keep it deterministic, bounded and compatible with stored data. Preserve the item's actual price/stock observation time and shipping evidence's own time; applying a newer shipping rule must not claim a fresh vendor price/stock check or advance lastRefreshAt. Do not fabricate an item price, force a Cloudflare refresh through admin tools, or turn a policy into an unconditional coverage guarantee. Test an old persisted Pucks offer with unknown shipping gaining the evidenced rule after a policy update.

### 3. Use substantial progressive disclosure on the product page

The goal is a short decision flow, not merely smaller versions of every existing paragraph.

- **One-product comparison board** (`/`, `/api/board`): ranks delivered offers for Lavazza Crema e Gusto
  ground coffee in a vacuum brick by item price + shipping + mandatory fees in ILS, normalized to
  delivered ILS/kg and to the packs a shopper actually buys. Destination (six Israeli locality/postcode

  address bar. A stored offer's identity key is vendor + SKU/product + form + pack size, not the blend
  wording, and rows for one listing URL are collapsed at read time (newest observation wins), so a
  wording change cannot duplicate one SKU. Single 250 g, 4 × 250 g and 8 × 250 g offers are never merged.

  (or Rossa/Suerte) URL back to the tracked product and returns `requestedRetiredProduct` so the board
  can explain the fallback; `pruneRetiredObservations()` deletes any stored retired observation or
  attempt marker on every refresh. The UI shows the tracked product as a static label (no dead
  one-option picker) and displays a written retired-line notice when a query URL asked for one.
- **Honest unknowns**: unknown shipping, unknown FX, unknown availability, stale observations and
  out-of-stock offers remain visible with plain-language reasons. Missing data never becomes zero and
  never wins. Pickup is shown separately and never competes with delivery.
- **Provenance**: every offer keeps its vendor link, product identity (variant, form, pack grams, pack
  count, SKU/GTIN), availability with its structured-data evidence URL, last successful check, last
  attempt, parser version and shipping certainty.
- **Failed attempts stay visible**: when a vendor check fails, the failure is stamped on that offer's last
  successful observation row (`attemptedAt` + `lastError`) instead of a detached marker, so the board still
  ranks the last known good price and stock while saying `Last attempt: Failed … — showing the last
  successful observation`. The comparison table repeats `Last attempt failed …` next to the checked time,
  the unknown list names the failure reason in plain language, and the footer lists each failing source
  with its consecutive failures, next attempt and last error. A successful check clears the failure mark.
- **Previous-check comparison**: each refresh stores the previous successful price, stock and pack weight
  for the same offer, and the board shows the unit-price change since that check in ILS with its timestamp
  ("Unit price down ₪2.00 since the previous check"). A pack-size change or a missing exchange rate makes
  the comparison say why instead of claiming no change, and a stock change is labelled separately.
- **Bulk-value callout**: when the cheapest delivered total is not the cheapest per-kilogram offer (for
  example, two single 250 g packs at 500 g versus the 4 × 250 g pack), the best-offer card and the
  comparison table name the per-kilogram winner without changing the delivered ranking.
- **Readable comparison rows**: every ranked row states its difference from the cheapest delivered total
  (`+₪58.00 vs best`; the best row says `Cheapest delivered total`, an equal total says
  `Same delivered total as best`), so the ranking is auditable without recomputing the arithmetic.

  coverage caveat where the vendor terms make home delivery subject to a locality list the product page
  does not publish, so the board discloses the geographic restriction instead of claiming country-wide
  delivery. Every rate is also labelled in words: `Published rate (verified)`, `Checkout rate (observed,
  conditional)`, `Estimated rate` or `Not published before checkout`. Availability and shipping evidence
  are stamped with the retrieval time of the page (or estimator) they came from, and the best-offer card
  and comparison table show unit price × packs bought = ILS line total so the delivered total is
  auditable. A cart-observed rate is never relabelled as published and is never stretched to an
  unobserved cart size (the CoffeeMan 8-pack quote carries its 2000 g limit); a genuinely missing rate
  keeps the `Not published before checkout` label and never becomes zero. Every researched delivery
  rule is a versioned policy in `src/lib/policies.js` (iteration 3-77): Pucks ₪30 / free-above-₪100,

  alternatives and coverage caveat from the matching policy, never overwriting what the row already
  states and never touching its price, stock or `observedAt`; the adapters derive their researched
  constants from the same policies instead of separate hard-coded strings.

  are never changed, and no shipping discount is inferred from an item promotion.

  `/health` or `/api/board` after deployment starts one throttled initial refresh. Observations, vendor
  state, FX rates, run history and leases persist in the SQLite-backed `BoardStore` Durable Object. The
  board API and footer report board-level fresh/stale freshness and warn in plain language when no
  completed refresh is recent. A run only advances `lastRefreshAt` when at least one vendor actually saved

  only the exchange-rate table can mask a stalled pipeline as fresh; both are still recorded in the run

## Iteration 3-83 — Pucks destination coverage extended to every selectable locality; same-rule policy updates refresh persisted provenance at read time (2026-10-13)

**The gap.** The checked-in Pucks policy v1 had sampled Tel Aviv / 6100000, Eilat / 8800000 and
Jerusalem / 9100000 only, while the site offers Haifa / 3100000 and Be’er Sheva / 8400000 as
destinations with no estimator evidence behind them. The coverage caveat said only "Tel Aviv and
Eilat carts". Separately, the read-time evaluator filled *unknown* shipping from a validated policy but
left an already-stamped row's **evidence** untouched, so after a same-rule policy update (newer
coverage evidence, new retrieval time) the board kept serving the older caveat and the older policy
version until the next 6-hour vendor refresh — a provenance version of the known-knowledge gap.

**What changed (research + implementation).**

- Three bounded recipe runs through the real Chrome/ChromeDriver workflow
  (`npm run research:browser -- recipe pucks`) with the destination step verified on the page:
  a 2 × 250 g cart to Haifa / 3100000 and a 2 × 250 g cart to Be’er Sheva / 8400000 each showed
  **₪60 + ₪30 = ₪90**, and a 4 × 250 g cart to Haifa showed **₪120 + ₪0 = ₪120** (the free-over-₪100
  rule reproduced at a third locality). No order, payment, login, account or street address was
  involved and no bot challenge was bypassed; cart/session identifiers are stripped from the records.
  Evidence: `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-13-pucks-haifa-500g.json`,
  `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-13-pucks-beersheva-500g.json`,
  `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-13-pucks-haifa-1kg.json` and the summary
  `docs/evidence/browser-research/2026-10-13-pucks-destination-extension.json`.
- `pucks-il-home-delivery` is now **v2**: the ₪30 / free-above-₪100 rule and its strict `above`
  semantics are unchanged, the coverage caveat names all five selectable localities with a postcode,
  and the evidence note/time record the 2026-10-13 re-check. The adapter derives its parsed row from
  the policy, so a fresh parse carries v2 directly.
- `enrichObservationShipping()` now distinguishes "fill missing fields" from "refresh stale
  provenance": when a row already carries a `shipping.policy` stamp for the **same policy id with an
  older version** and the money/scope is identical (amount, threshold, semantics, origin, min order,
  max grams and alternatives all equal), the evaluator refreshes only the policy stamp, the coverage
  caveat and evidence that came from this policy (same evidence URL). A version that changes any
  amount leaves the row untouched for the next vendor refresh — a parsed rate is never overwritten at
  read time. The item's `observedAt`, price and stock, and the refresh completion marker, stay
  untouched.

## Iteration 3-85 — CoffeeMan free evidence bound to its observed carts; Coffee4U method recorded; index and locality readability (2026-10-13)

**The defect.** Iteration 3-82 promoted CoffeeMan's free-delivery observation as a monotone threshold
(`₪231, at_least`), so any single/4-pack cart at or above ₪231 would be free. The vendor publishes no such
threshold and the sampled carts are not monotone (a ₪198 cart paid ₪25, the ₪240 8-pack SKU cart paid
₪20, while the ₪231/₪264/₪248 carts were free), so a 3 kg single-pack cart or three 4-packs could inherit
free delivery merely from a subtotal. The same review found the Coffee4U destination-extension evidence
records carried `service: null` even though the runs had successfully selected door-to-door delivery, and
that the home index card still repeated a long comparison explanation while the 390 px locality control
clipped the selected locality inside a half-width column.

**What changed (evidence scope first).**

- `coffeeman-single-4pack-il-home-delivery` is now **v3**. `rule.freeThreshold` is removed; the free
  observations live in `rule.freeCartConditions`, one entry per observed free cart with validated listing
  prefix + SKU, pack count, whole-pack units, ordered grams, item subtotal before any discount, paid item
  total, the named method, destination evidence, observation time and its own evidence note: `singles-7`
  (SKU 930333, 7 units, ₪231), `singles-8` (8 units, ₪264 before the automatic 10% promotion → ₪237.60)
  and `fourpack-2` (SKU 930334, 2 units, ₪248). No threshold is recorded. `supersedes` names the exact
  superseded v2 threshold (₪231, `at_least`, `observed_cart`) so a persisted row stamped by v2 stops
  applying it at read time — the published ₪25 base amount, the item price, stock and `observedAt` are
  untouched — and a rule that changes any amount is still never swapped in at read time.
- The quote engine matches a cart against each condition exactly (listing prefix, SKU, service, pack
  count, units, ordered grams and the pre-discount subtotal, falling back to the paid total when no
  discount applies). A matched cart becomes free with a label naming the exact observed cart; an
  unmatched cart keeps the published ₪25, and when its subtotal is at or above an observed free subtotal
  the card says free delivery was observed only on specific carts. `base.shipping` exposes
  `freeCartConditions`/`freeCondition`; `policySummary()` exposes the condition ids/SKUs/subtotals.
- The CoffeeMan adapter derives its free conditions from the policy (never a hard-coded threshold), and
  the 8-pack SKU policy is unchanged: it keeps its own ₪20 quote and never inherits the conditions.
- **Coffee4U method evidence.** Recipe method steps now declare `confirmsService`; a successful run
  records `service` + `serviceConfirmed: true`, and an optional method step that could not be confirmed
  records `service: null` + `serviceConfirmed: false` plus a qualification (schema validation rejects
  both a claimed-but-unnamed method and an undisclosed unconfirmed one). The nine checked-in Pucks and
  Coffee4U quote records were backfilled from their recorded successful method step with a note saying
  so, and `coffee4u-il-home-delivery` names the method in `observedFor.method`; the public quote output
  keeps `shipping.service`/`serviceLabel` and the quantity/destination restrictions (`maxTotalGrams`,
  closed-locality-list caveat, alternatives) unchanged.
- **Readability.** The home index card is one compact line (`3 vendors · 5 listings: …`) instead of the
  comparison walkthrough, and the catalog intro is one sentence. On ≤720 px the locality group takes the
  full row and the option text drops the redundant “area” suffix, so `Tel Aviv–Yafo · 6100000` is fully
  readable at 390 px (measured width 343 px, label one line).

- `scripts/probe-production.mjs` gained read-only checks for the scoped conditions: the 2 kg single-pack

# Canton Zürich design system (web-application patterns)

Owner direction, 2026-10-12. This supersedes the earlier generic Swiss transport-signage brief. The
shopping board adapts the **Canton Zürich design system** for a compact web service: flat surfaces,
strict alignment, a responsive grid, a clear type hierarchy and concise disclosures. The product
identity stays our own; there is no cantonal crest, government wordmark or implied affiliation.

Primary references read before implementation:

- Design system overview — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html
- Colors — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/farben.html
- Typography — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/typografie.html
- Layout and grid — https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/design-grundlagen/layout-und-raster.html

## Tokens and roles

| Token | Value | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blau | `#0070B4` | Selected shopping context, the clearly labelled best known delivered offer, links and the focus outline. Used sparingly; vendor names are never painted arbitrary colors. |
| Softblau | `#EDF5FA` | Panel/background for the selected context and the best-offer rule. |
| Black | `#000000` | Primary text and neutral structure. |
| Secondary text | `#666666` | Notes, meta and secondary labels. |
| Surface | `#F7F7F7` | Subtle section surfaces. |
| Divider | `#CCCCCC` | Rules and cell borders. |
| Green | `#1A7F1F` on `#EBF6EB` | Verified in-stock labels only, always with the written status. |
| Red | `#D93C1A` on white | Unavailable/error labels only. |
| Amber | `#8A4B00` on `#FFF4E5` | Unknown shipping, unconfirmed coverage and stale evidence. This is a deliberate shopping-specific extension, **not** an official Canton Zürich token; it preserves the owner's uncertainty semantics. |
| Cyan | `#009EE0` | Non-text active indicator only (3.01:1 on white, so it is never used for small text). |
| Focus | `#0070B4` | 3 px outline on every focusable control (5.28:1 on white, 4.79:1 on Softblau). |

Meaning is never carried by color alone: every status keeps a written label (`In stock (observed)`,
`Shipping not published`, `Published rate (verified)`, `Checkout rate (observed, conditional)`,
`Coverage: …`) and the selected state is distinct. A rate that exists only in the vendor's anonymous
cart/checkout estimator is never called a published rate: it uses the `Checkout rate (observed,
conditional)` label so its quantity/destination condition stays visible.

  locality and delivery method. Do not add a blend selector, unobserved-variant menu entries, variant

  and any stated blend wording may stay as evidence inside optional offer details, never as a filter or
  a repeated badge, and an unstated listing must never be relabelled as Classico. Old shared URLs with
  an obsolete `variant=` parameter keep their product/quantity/locality and resolve to this unified
  comparison.

  the site deployed at https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev; on 2026-10-12 the loop independently

  deploy Cloudflare.

**What changed (evidence scope first).**

- `coffeeman-single-4pack-il-home-delivery` is now **v3**. `rule.freeThreshold` is removed; the free
  observations live in `rule.freeCartConditions`, one entry per observed free cart with validated listing
  prefix + SKU, pack count, whole-pack units, ordered grams, item subtotal before any discount, paid item
  total, the named method, destination evidence, observation time and its own evidence note: `singles-7`
  (SKU 930333, 7 units, ₪231), `singles-8` (8 units, ₪264 before the automatic 10% promotion → ₪237.60)
  and `fourpack-2` (SKU 930334, 2 units, ₪248). No threshold is recorded. `supersedes` names the exact
  superseded v2 threshold (₪231, `at_least`, `observed_cart`) so a persisted row stamped by v2 stops
  applying it at read time — the published ₪25 base amount, the item price, stock and `observedAt` are
  untouched — and a rule that changes any amount is still never swapped in at read time.
- The quote engine matches a cart against each condition exactly (listing prefix, SKU, service, pack
  count, units, ordered grams and the pre-discount subtotal, falling back to the paid total when no
  discount applies). A matched cart becomes free with a label naming the exact observed cart; an
  unmatched cart keeps the published ₪25, and when its subtotal is at or above an observed free subtotal
  the card says free delivery was observed only on specific carts. `base.shipping` exposes
  `freeCartConditions`/`freeCondition`; `policySummary()` exposes the condition ids/SKUs/subtotals.
- The CoffeeMan adapter derives its free conditions from the policy (never a hard-coded threshold), and
  the 8-pack SKU policy is unchanged: it keeps its own ₪20 quote and never inherits the conditions.
- **Coffee4U method evidence.** Recipe method steps now declare `confirmsService`; a successful run
  records `service` + `serviceConfirmed: true`, and an optional method step that could not be confirmed
  records `service: null` + `serviceConfirmed: false` plus a qualification (schema validation rejects
  both a claimed-but-unnamed method and an undisclosed unconfirmed one). The nine checked-in Pucks and
  Coffee4U quote records were backfilled from their recorded successful method step with a note saying
  so, and `coffee4u-il-home-delivery` names the method in `observedFor.method`; the public quote output
  keeps `shipping.service`/`serviceLabel` and the quantity/destination restrictions (`maxTotalGrams`,
  closed-locality-list caveat, alternatives) unchanged.
- **Readability.** The home index card is one compact line (`3 vendors · 5 listings: …`) instead of the
  comparison walkthrough, and the catalog intro is one sentence. On ≤720 px the locality group takes the
  full row and the option text drops the redundant “area” suffix, so `Tel Aviv–Yafo · 6100000` is fully

## Iteration 3-87 — rendered-contrast verification restored, readable offer views saved (2026-10-13)

**The defect.** `docs/DESIGN.md` has claimed since iteration 3-80 that `scripts/browser-qa.mjs` "walks
visible text ... and compares the computed text color with the effective background" and that the suite
passes with no contrast violations. The 3-75 browser-QA rewrite (`86a992e`, the index/product split)
dropped that walk while the documentation kept the claim, so the rendered 4.5:1/3:1 requirement in the
owner's Canton Zürich design direction was no longer actually verified by any check. The saved offer
screenshots also only existed as full-page captures; the coding agent's file-read tool rejects PNG input,
so the affected offer could not be inspected in a cropped, readable view.

**What changed (verification tooling only; no application or policy code touched).**

- `scripts/browser-qa.mjs` gained a composited-contrast walk: for every visible text element in a scope it
  composites the background actually behind the text (translucent layers blended down to the root, alpha
  text blended with its background) and compares the WCAG relative-luminance ratio with the requirement
  for the rendered font size/weight (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large). It runs on seven page states: the home
  index, the product page at desktop and mobile, the 2 kg CoffeeMan winner with the failed-check warning,
  the 500 g CoffeeMan comparison card with the same warning, the stale-refresh warning state and the
  unknown-shipping state. A violation fails the run and is printed with text, colors, size and ratio.
- The keyboard check now also measures the focus outline against the control's own rendered background
  and requires 3:1 (essential UI), instead of only asserting the token color.
- New `elementScreenshot()` captures the affected offer cards cropped to the element: the 500 g best card

  failed-check state, plus the home index card. When the live board itself has a ranked offer whose last
  check failed (the deployed store's CoffeeMan HTTP 403 rows), the live-only QA block now also opens the

  every recorded cart reproduces its fee (₪25/₪25/₪25/₪0/₪0/₪25/₪0/₪20), and the unobserved 3 kg
