1. Shurik on GitHub Actions develops and checkpoints source to main. It uses only OPENCODE_API_KEY and the repository GITHUB_TOKEN. Its state/history is public on shurik-control/main.
2. The deployed Worker refreshes vendor observations using deterministic scheduled adapters, persists them through runtime bindings and serves the public comparison board. It does not need Shurik or an LLM to keep refreshing.

Cloudflare Workers Builds is reported connected by the owner and is serving the production Worker; it observes main pushes and performs validation before deploying. The loop independently verified the public deployment once on 2026-10-12 with read-only GETs (docs/evidence/production-verification-20261012T1554Z.json). No CF deployment workflow or CF API secret belongs in GitHub. Exclude shurik-control/* and all other branches from Cloudflare builds and previews.

This prevents Shurik's Actions process from directly authenticating to CF. It is not a sandbox for agent-authored code: Shurik writes main, so its code and configuration can influence the CF build and live Worker. CF build commands can run source-controlled code in a credentialed environment. Restrict the CF build token to this Worker and the minimum required permissions; avoid broad account permissions or unrelated build/runtime secrets. Prefer runtime bindings over administrative API tokens. Never give the public Worker an administrative CF token.

GitHub normally does not trigger another push workflow for a push using GITHUB_TOKEN. Do not rely on CI being automatically triggered by every Shurik checkpoint. Shurik must run local verification, and Cloudflare's build command must run npm run verify for every deployment. After connecting CF, verify one actual Shurik push reaches Workers Builds; never assume third-party webhook behavior from GitHub Actions behavior alone.

## Implemented runtime

The tracked scope is one product line: `src/catalog.js` holds Lavazza Crema e Gusto (a ground vacuum
brick) with strict classification rules. The 2026-10-12 owner correction retired
Qualità Oro, Qualità Rossa and Suerte; their ids remain as tombstones so `classifyListing` and
`resolveProductRequest` reject or explain them instead of reviving them, and each refresh prunes any
stored observation or attempt marker that belongs to a retired line. Vendor-specific adapters under `src/vendors/` (CoffeeMan, Pucks, Coffee4U)
fetch fixed allowlisted product URLs through the bounded fetcher in `src/lib/http.js` and return versioned
observations. `src/lib/quote.js` is a pure, timestamp-aware ranking engine; `src/lib/fx.js` converts
non-ILS amounts with Bank of Israel reference rates and refuses to guess when a rate is missing. It
compares every eligible tracked listing — including one that states no blend wording — in one board and
passes every published shipping
alternative (for example a cheaper pickup-point delivery) through to the UI without using it as the ranked
amount. A vendor that publishes a courier rate but makes home delivery subject to an unpublished locality
list keeps a structured coverage caveat, so the board discloses the geographic restriction instead of
claiming unconditional country-wide delivery; availability and shipping evidence are stamped with the
retrieval time of the page they came from. Each refresh also keeps one step of comparison evidence — the
previous successful price, stock and pack weight of the same offer — so the board can show the unit-price
change since the last check in ILS (and says why when a comparison is impossible), and it advances the
board's `lastRefreshAt` only when at least one vendor actually saved an observation, so a run that fetched
only the exchange-rate table cannot look like a fresh offer check. Board freshness also reports the newest
saved observation and falls back to it for the age when no completion marker exists, so an interrupted run
(for example a redeploy stopping the background job) with fresh saved offers is not labelled never
refreshed, while a recorded but old completion still reports the scheduled pipeline as stopped. A failed
vendor check does not erase the last known good row: the attempt time and reason are stamped on that
offer's existing observation row (or a marker is kept when the offer never succeeded), so the board still
ranks the last successful price and stock while saying the most recent attempt failed, and a later
successful check clears the mark. A stored offer's identity is vendor + SKU/product + form + pack size —
never the blend wording a listing happens to print (owner correction, 2026-10-12), so a listing that
changes or drops that wording cannot persist a second row for one SKU. Rows written under the old
blend-wording key and their stable-key replacements are collapsed at read time by vendor + listing URL,
keeping the newest observation, and failure markers plus the previous-check comparison resolve to the
newest row for the same URL, so the key migration can never show a duplicate offer, hide a failed check
or lose the previous price evidence.

`src/lib/policies.js` is the shared, versioned shipping-evidence model. A policy states the vendor,
product/SKU scope, service, destination scope, the amount or free-shipping threshold rule (with the
vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording preserved), the evidence URL and retrieval time, and a `reviewBy`
date. A rule may also carry **exact cart-observed free conditions** (`rule.freeCartConditions`)
instead of a threshold: each condition names the listing prefix and SKU, pack count, whole-pack units,
ordered grams, the item subtotal before any discount, the paid item total, the named method, the
destination evidence and its own observation time. `quoteBoard()` applies the evaluator at read time:
an observation whose own shipping is unknown is enriched with a matching validated policy, while an
observation that already carries a fresher amount, threshold or destination is never overwritten. A
row already stamped by an **older version of the same policy** whose money/scope is identical gets its
provenance refreshed at read time (newer version, retrieval time, coverage caveat and evidence note)
so a validated coverage or re-check update reaches persisted offers promptly; a version that changes
any amount is left for the next vendor refresh and never swapped in at read time. The one deliberate
exception is a rule **correction** declared in the new policy's `supersedes`: when a row stamped by
the same policy id still carries the exact superseded free threshold (amount, currency, semantics and
origin), the evaluator removes that policy-derived threshold and applies the scoped conditions instead,
so a scope error stops applying without waiting for a vendor refresh; the published base amount, the
item price, stock and observation time are untouched. The evaluator is deterministic and refuses to
guess: conflicting policies for the same scope stay `inconsistent`, a malformed policy is `invalid`,
and a policy past its review date is `expired`, so the offer falls back to explicit unknown shipping
instead of a stale unconditional rate. Enrichment never touches the observation's price, stock,
`observedAt` or the refresh completion marker, so applying a newer shipping rule cannot claim a fresh
vendor price/stock check; `policySummary()` exposes the rule version, observation time, review date and
scoped condition ids through `/api/status`. Four validated policies are checked in: Pucks'
₪30/free-above-₪100 home-delivery rule v2 (its coverage caveat names the five selectable localities
sampled in the estimator), CoffeeMan's published ₪25 single/4-pack rule **v3** with its cart-observed
₪15 distribution-center alternative and the exact cart-observed free conditions (7 singles at ₪231,
8 singles at ₪264 → ₪237.60 and 2 × 4-pack at ₪248; a ₪198 cart was charged ₪25 and the sampled carts
are not monotone, so no threshold is recorded and a larger or repriced cart keeps the published base
rate), CoffeeMan's ₪20 checkout quote for the one-8-pack (2 kg) cart (which carries
`maxTotalGrams: 2000` so the quote engine never stretches it to an unobserved larger cart and records
no free condition for this SKU), and Coffee4U's published ₪30 door-to-door rule with its ₪15
pickup-point alternative and the observed closed-locality-list coverage shape. Secondary delivery
methods are part of the policy representation: the evaluator adds them only when a stored row has
none, and they never replace the ranked amount. Each policy is also the adapter's single source for
the researched values it describes, so the parsed row, the read-time evaluator and the tests share one
representation instead of separate hard-coded strings. The adapters honor the same `reviewBy` gate at
parse time (`policyIsCurrent()`): once a policy is past its review date, its researched rate and any
policy-derived alternative are withheld, so a freshly parsed offer falls back to explicit unknown
shipping rather than carrying a stale quote forward. Page-published rates (CoffeeMan's ₪25 and
Coffee4U's ₪30/₪15) are parsed from the vendor page and stay independent of the policy window.

The browser-research evidence schema (`scripts/research-workflow.mjs`, `browser-research-quote` v1)
records the delivery method a shipping line belongs to: a recipe step that selects the method declares
`confirmsService`, and a successful run stores `service` plus `serviceConfirmed: true`. A quoted record
whose optional method step could not be confirmed stores `service: null`, `serviceConfirmed: false`
and a qualification that the shipping line is not attributed to a named method; schema validation
rejects both a claimed-but-unnamed method and an undisclosed unconfirmed one. The Coffee4U
destination-extension records were backfilled from their recorded successful method step, and the
Coffee4U policy names the method in `observedFor.method`.

`src/lib/promotions.js` is the shared, validated model for published item-price promotions (quantity
discounts). A promotion states the vendor, product/URL scope, the percent off, the activating
item-subtotal rule (with the vendor's `above`/`at_least` wording preserved), whether multipacks are
excluded, the vendor's own wording and the evidence URL/retrieval time. The adapters parse the vendor's
promotion banner on every fetch (`parseCoffeemanPromotion`), so an ended promotion stops applying with
the next observation; a checked page with no banner records an explicit empty `promotions: []`, which is
never re-enriched. The checked-in fallback (`coffeeman-ground-coffee-percent-off` v1: 10% off ground
coffee from a ₪250 item subtotal, multipacks excluded, observed in the anonymous 8 × 250 g cart at ₪264
→ ₪237.60) only covers persisted rows stored before banner parsing and stops applying past its

the base unit price, stock and `observedAt` are never touched, and no shipping discount is inferred
from an item promotion. `promotionSummary()` exposes the rule, percent, threshold and review date
through `/api/status`.

content.text:
- A single centered column (max 1240 px) with a responsive control grid that reflows on mobile; on
  small screens the quantity group and the locality group each take the full row, so the selected
  locality text is not clipped inside a half-width native `<select>` (verified at 390 px). No
  horizontal page scrolling at 1440 px or 390 px.
- **Offer cards** replace the former wide comparison table. The best known delivered offer carries a
  blue rule, the written tag "Best known delivered total" and its selection context; other ranked
  offers state their difference (`+₪x vs best delivered total`).
- Each card keeps the decision values together in one `.totals` row: **item subtotal**, **shipping
  charge, named delivery method and written certainty label** and the **delivered total** plus
  per-kilogram normalization. The method (`Home delivery`, `Pickup-point delivery`,
  `Distribution-center delivery`, `Self-pickup`, or `Delivery method not stated`) is rendered separately
  from the certainty label, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys. When a published quantity
  promotion reduced the subtotal, the item-subtotal cell adds one muted line (`10% promotion applied —
  was ₪264.00`); the vendor's own wording and the evidence stay inside the offer details. On mobile the
  three cells stack but remain in the same card, inside the first viewport.
- Conditions are one short list per offer (free-shipping threshold, minimum order, delivery area,
  alternative services, self-pickup, delivery time, cart-size limit) inside that offer's
  `Delivery options and conditions` disclosure. A coverage caveat is written once inside the same
  disclosure; the card face keeps only a one-line amber qualification. A free condition that comes
  from an anonymous-cart observation is written as observed and conditional. CoffeeMan's free
  observations are exact cart conditions, not a threshold: when the current cart matches one, the
  shipping cell reads `Free (observed for this cart)`, the certainty line adds
  `free condition cart-observed`, and the qualifier names the exact observed cart and says it must be
  confirmed at checkout; when the cart does not match (for example 3 kg of singles), the published base
  rate is shown and, if the subtotal is at or above an observed free subtotal, the qualifier says free
  delivery was observed only on specific carts. A published threshold (Pucks' free above ₪100) keeps
  the `Free (threshold met)` wording. An observed free condition is never merged into the published
  rate label. Pickup-only offers live in their
  own collapsed disclosure and never compete in the delivered ranking; each is one compact row (vendor,
  pack/quantity, item subtotal, pickup fee and the written "Self-pickup, not delivery"), with the
  repeated pickup terms behind a `Pickup terms` disclosure.
- Debug/provenance metadata (previous checks, failed attempts, the applied shipping-policy version, the
  applied promotion's vendor wording and evidence, the adapter's shipping terms, shipping evidence, FX,
  per-vendor refresh state, next source check) lives behind `Offer details and check history` /
  `Refresh diagnostics` disclosures instead of the first screen. A cart-observed alternative (for
  example CoffeeMan's distribution-center delivery) carries its cart condition in the short label and
  its full observation in the disclosure.
- Unknown shipping says **"Shipping not published"** with the exact reason and is never shown as zero;
  a published rate with unconfirmed destination coverage is labelled as such, not as a guaranteed
  checkout total.
- A ranked offer whose most recent vendor check failed shows one short amber card-face line
  (`Last check failed — showing the last successful observation.`) directly under its money values;
  the attempt time, the error and the last successful check stay in `Offer details and check history`,
  and the footer names the failing source. This warning is deliberately visible: the price still ranks
  but may be out of date, which can change the shopping decision.

- Readable offer views: the affected offers are also saved as element-level screenshots (cropped to the

evaluator (including an old persisted Pucks row and an old persisted CoffeeMan 8-pack row each gaining

`scripts/research-workflow.mjs` defines the vendor navigation recipes and the common, sanitized
evidence schema, and `scripts/browser-research.mjs` (`npm run research:browser -- recipe <vendor>`)
executes a recipe in the real Chrome session and writes one evidence record whether the run quoted, hit
a public-flow blocker or failed; `scripts/qa-server.mjs` serves the
production front-end against fixture-backed API data so `npm run qa:browser` drives headless Chrome
offline and derives its expectations from the API. The front-end is two pages: the home route renders

ranked totals — and writes a snapshot for the status docs. Browser QA also loads an old

with a written retired-line notice rather than reviving the retired line. See docs/STATUS.md for the

content.text:
- Each run fetches at most one URL per tracked offer plus the Bank of Israel rate file, capped at two vendors concurrently, 12 s per request and 1.5 MB per response, with hosts restricted to each adapter's allowlist. Five Crema e Gusto offers from three independent vendors (CoffeeMan, Pucks, Coffee4U) are tracked today; the product and offers are visible in `/api/catalog`.
- A run that fetched nothing because every vendor is inside its backoff window is recorded in the run history but does not update `lastRefreshAt`, so an empty run cannot mask a stalled pipeline as fresh.
- A run that is interrupted after saving observations (for example a redeploy stops the background job) leaves no completion marker. `/health`, `/api/status` and `/api/board` therefore also report `lastObservationAt` (the newest saved successful observation) and `freshness.dataAsOf`, and use the observation time as the age anchor only when no completed refresh exists. A recorded but old completion still reads as stale: that is the scheduled pipeline having stopped, not missing data.
- Requests to the same host are spaced by the vendor's published crawl delay (`Crawl-delay: 7` on CoffeeMan and Coffee4U, declared as `crawlDelayMs` on the adapter), so a full live run takes about 40 s of wall time but never fires its offers back to back. The pacing waits do not consume CPU and are bounded by the number of tracked offers, so a run stays inside the cron trigger's limits.
- Failures keep the previous good observation, back off (30 min doubling to 12 h) and are surfaced in `/api/status` and the board footer. One broken vendor cannot stop the others. If no scheduled refresh has completed for more than eight hours, `/api/board` and `/api/status` report `freshness.stale` and the site footer says plainly that prices may be out of date. When no refresh has ever completed but saved observations exist, the age anchor is the newest observation instead, and the footer names that observation time rather than claiming the board never refreshed.

## Local verification without a Cloudflare account

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run verify          # node:test suite + wrangler deploy --dry-run
npm run check:sources   # live fetch + parse of every tracked vendor page
npm run cron:offline    # full refresh pipeline against recorded fixtures
npm run cron:local      # full refresh pipeline against the live vendor pages
npm run probe:production # read-only GETs against the deployed board (no credentials, no deploy)
npm run dev             # local Worker with a local SQLite Durable Object
```

`cron:offline` runs the whole fixture pipeline from a clean `.shurik-local/board-offline.json` every
time, so it is repeatable and never consumes the live run's backoff window; `cron:local` keeps
`.shurik-local/board.json` and honours the same six-hour vendor schedule as the deployed cron, with
`npm run cron:local -- --fresh` as the override for a manual live check.

`npm run probe:production` sends only public GETs to `/health`, `/api/status`, `/api/catalog` and a few
`/api/board` queries (including an old retired-product URL). It never authenticates, never deploys and
never sends a credential; it asserts the single-product scope and writes a JSON snapshot under
`.shurik-local/production/` (or to `--out <path>`), so production state can be re-checked and diffed
without re-inventing the probe. Pass `--url http://127.0.0.1:8789` to run the same checks against a local
Worker.

With `npm run dev` running on port 8789, the same commands used during development are:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8789/api/board?grams=500\&dest=tel-aviv
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8789/cdn-cgi/local/scheduled   # simulate the cron trigger (wrangler dev only)
npm run qa:browser                            # offline fixture-backed browser QA (no network)
npm run qa:browser -- http://127.0.0.1:8789   # live browser QA against the running Worker
```

The local scheduled trigger waits while the run executes. With the vendors' declared crawl delays a full
run takes about 40 s, so a client-side timeout on that call does not mean the refresh failed; check
`/api/status` for the persisted run, `lastRefreshAt` and the vendors' `nextAttemptAt`.

`npm run qa:browser` without an argument starts `scripts/qa-server.mjs` on an ephemeral port. That server
serves `public/` and the read-only board API computed from `tests/fixtures/` with the production quote
engine, so headless Chrome checks the real UI offline and the script compares the DOM against the API
response instead of hard-coded prices. The live form checks the same UI against a real local Worker.

- **Product `/product/<id>` — decision page.** Directly loadable and shareable; the path plus
  `?grams=&dest=` query restores quantity and locality (a retired-line or unknown id falls back to the
  tracked product with a written notice). There is no blend/variant control, menu entry or warning: every
  eligible tracked listing — including one that states no blend wording — is in the one comparison, and
  a listing's raw wording and any stated blend wording stay inside `Offer details and check history` as
  provenance. Default view: compact product identity and the quantity/locality controls, then the best
  eligible offer with vendor, stock, accurate pack/grams, the three money values and a one-line
  conditional warning. Everything else is progressively disclosed:
  `Delivery options and conditions` and `Offer details and check history` per offer, one
  `Compare other offers (n)` disclosure for the rest of the ranking, one collapsed
  `Self-pickup options (n)` disclosure, and an `Offers with missing information (n)` disclosure that is
  only rendered when something is actually missing.

## Layout and components

- A single centered column (max 1240 px) with a responsive control grid that reflows on mobile; on
  small screens the quantity group and the locality group each take the full row, so the selected
  locality text is not clipped inside a half-width native `<select>` (verified at 390 px). No
  horizontal page scrolling at 1440 px or 390 px.
- **Offer cards** replace the former wide comparison table. The best known delivered offer carries a
  blue rule, the written tag "Best known delivered total" and its selection context; other ranked
  offers state their difference (`+₪x vs best delivered total`).
- Each card keeps the decision values together in one `.totals` row: **item subtotal**, **shipping
  charge, named delivery method and written certainty label** and the **delivered total** plus
  per-kilogram normalization. The method (`Home delivery`, `Pickup-point delivery`,
  `Distribution-center delivery`, `Self-pickup`, or `Delivery method not stated`) is rendered separately
  from the certainty label, so a shopper can tell what the charge buys. When a published quantity
  promotion reduced the subtotal, the item-subtotal cell adds one muted line (`10% promotion applied —
  was ₪264.00`); the vendor's own wording and the evidence stay inside the offer details. On mobile the
  three cells stack but remain in the same card, inside the first viewport.
- Conditions are one short list per offer (free-shipping threshold, minimum order, delivery area,
  alternative services, self-pickup, delivery time, cart-size limit) inside that offer's
  `Delivery options and conditions` disclosure. A coverage caveat is written once inside the same
  disclosure; the card face keeps only a one-line amber qualification. A free condition that comes
  from an anonymous-cart observation is written as observed and conditional. CoffeeMan's free
  observations are exact cart conditions, not a threshold: when the current cart matches one, the
  shipping cell reads `Free (observed for this cart)`, the certainty line adds
  `free condition cart-observed`, and the qualifier names the exact observed cart and says it must be
  confirmed at checkout; when the cart does not match (for example 3 kg of singles), the published base
  rate is shown and, if the subtotal is at or above an observed free subtotal, the qualifier says free
  delivery was observed only on specific carts. A published threshold (Pucks' free above ₪100) keeps
  the `Free (threshold met)` wording. An observed free condition is never merged into the published
  rate label. Pickup-only offers live in their
  own collapsed disclosure and never compete in the delivered ranking; each is one compact row (vendor,
  pack/quantity, item subtotal, pickup fee and the written "Self-pickup, not delivery"), with the
  repeated pickup terms behind a `Pickup terms` disclosure.
- Debug/provenance metadata (previous checks, failed attempts, the applied shipping-policy version, the
  applied promotion's vendor wording and evidence, the adapter's shipping terms, shipping evidence, FX,
  per-vendor refresh state, next source check) lives behind `Offer details and check history` /
  `Refresh diagnostics` disclosures instead of the first screen. A cart-observed alternative (for
  example CoffeeMan's distribution-center delivery) carries its cart condition in the short label and
  its full observation in the disclosure.
- Unknown shipping says **"Shipping not published"** with the exact reason and is never shown as zero;
  a published rate with unconfirmed destination coverage is labelled as such, not as a guaranteed
  checkout total.

# Deployment notes and owner handoffs

Current state (2026-10-12): handoff 1 (OpenCode key plus loop control) is complete, and the owner
reports the Cloudflare side connected and serving **https://attention-shoppers.igormaka.workers.dev**
with the production Worker name `attention-shoppers`. On 2026-10-12 15:51-15:54 UTC the coding loop
independently verified that URL from the runner with read-only public GETs (no Cloudflare credentials,
admin API or deploy): HTTP 200, exactly one catalog product, five persisted observations, and a
request-triggered initial refresh that completed at 15:52:12.546Z and advanced `lastRefreshAt`; evidence
in docs/evidence/production-verification-20261012T1554Z.json. The loop still does not administer
Cloudflare. The outstanding production checks are listed at the end of this file and in docs/STATUS.md.

## 1. OpenCode key

Add OPENCODE_API_KEY under repository Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret. Paste it only in GitHub's secret form, never into chat, a prompt, a dispatch input or a commit.

The repository variable SHURIK_ENABLED starts false, so scheduled recovery and manual dispatch cannot start a model loop before setup is finished. The owner has added the key and authorized DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on OpenCode Go. After the key is present, the maintainer sets SHURIK_ENABLED true and dispatches:

```sh
gh workflow run shurik.yml --repo igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting --ref main \
  -f command=start -f loop_id=main -f seconds=1800
```

Provider, model and reasoning are fixed in the workflow's control action to opencode-go / deepseek-v4.1-flash / max. Further model changes require an owner instruction and a workflow update. The initial loop writes directly to main. Unless a deadline is supplied it continues until stopped, including after ordinary agent answers. Provider availability and the owner's OpenCode Go allowance apply.

To stop, dispatch command=stop and loop_id=main. Record the durable stop before turning SHURIK_ENABLED false. To resume, use command=resume, loop_id=main; the workflow supplies max reasoning again and updates the saved model to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Control/session history and Actions logs are public; do not add private material to this task.

## 2. Cloudflare Git integration

Expected as configured by the owner; the coding loop does not administer Cloudflare. The owner connects the repo from the Cloudflare dashboard, not through Shurik.

- Workers & Pages → Create application → Import a repository.
- Select igor-makarov/attention-shoppers-happy-hunting.
- Worker name: `attention-shoppers` (must match `name` in wrangler.jsonc).
- Production branch: main. Root directory: repository root.
- Build command: `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run verify`. The verify script runs the node:test suite and `wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir dist`, which builds the Worker bundle locally without any Cloudflare credential. Confirm Node 24.14.0 where supported.
- Deploy command: `npx --no-install wrangler deploy`.
- Disable builds and previews for non-production branches, especially `shurik-control/*`.
- Keep CF credentials inside Cloudflare. No CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or CF account secret belongs in GitHub.
- Minimum token scope for Workers Builds: Workers Scripts:Edit for this Worker only (the deploy command creates/updates the script and applies the Durable Object migration). No account-wide or unrelated permissions are needed. The runtime needs no administrative credential at all.

## Required bindings and provisioning

`wrangler.jsonc` declares everything; the owner needs no manual dashboard resource creation:

| Binding | Type | Provisioning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env.BOARD` | Durable Object, class `BoardStore`, SQLite-backed | Created by migration tag `v1` (`new_sqlite_classes: ["BoardStore"]`) during `wrangler deploy` |
| `env.ASSETS` | Static assets from `public/` | Packaged from the repository |

Nothing else is required: the Worker persists observations, vendor refresh state, FX rates and run history in the Durable Object's SQLite tables (`observations`, `vendor_state`, `meta`, `runs`; refresh leases live under `meta` as `lease:*` keys) and reads vendor pages over plain outbound HTTPS.

Alternative storage was considered and rejected: KV or R2 would add a separate consistency problem and still need a migration path for the lease/last-known-good semantics; the SQLite-backed Durable Object is created by the deployment itself with no extra credential.

## Cron behavior

- `wrangler.jsonc` triggers the scheduled handler on `17 */6 * * *` (UTC), about every six hours.
- A successful vendor is stored as due at `run time + 6 h`. Because the cron fires on fixed clock times, a successful vendor also counts as due up to 15 minutes early (`EARLY_DUE_TOLERANCE_MS` in `src/refresh.js`). Without that tolerance a tick landing seconds before the due time skips every vendor, the board drifts to a twelve-hour cadence and reports stale for hours between runs; vendors inside a failure backoff keep their strict due time, so backoff is not weakened.
- The first tick after an off-phase initial refresh can legitimately record a run that saves nothing because every vendor is still inside its six-hour window. That run appears in the run history but does not advance `lastRefreshAt` (no offer was re-observed); the following tick refreshes normally.
- The first `GET /health` or `GET /api/board` after a deployment starts one initial refresh in the background so the board is not empty until the first cron tick. It is lease- and throttle-protected (10 minutes) and can never be triggered repeatedly by public traffic.
- Each run fetches at most one URL per tracked offer plus the Bank of Israel rate file, capped at two vendors concurrently, 12 s per request and 1.5 MB per response, with hosts restricted to each adapter's allowlist. Five Crema e Gusto offers from three independent vendors (CoffeeMan, Pucks, Coffee4U) are tracked today; the product and offers are visible in `/api/catalog`.

# Attention shoppers. Happy hunting.

## Latest owner correction — remove the coffee-variant feature (2026-10-12)

The owner explicitly asks: "Get rid of the coffee variant. There's only two variants and it's the same coffee." Treat the tracked Crema e Gusto listings as **one coffee comparison**, not separate shopper-selectable blends. This latest instruction supersedes every older variant-separation/selector requirement in this prompt, AGENTS.md and the design/architecture/status documentation. Implement it first in the next fresh iteration, then continue the product index, progressive disclosure and shipping-policy work below.

- Remove the blend/variant selector, unobserved-variant menu entries, variant warnings, "other variant" counts/links and variant-as-a-shopping-configuration from the home and product page. Do not replace it with another blend toggle or add variant-specific product cards.
- Compare all eligible tracked Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground offers together for the selected quantity, locality and delivery method. Include the currently "Variant not stated" Coffee4U listing in that same comparison instead of hiding it behind a selector or withholding it as another blend. Offers can still be unavailable/unrankable for genuine stock, freshness, shipping or cart-scope reasons.
- Keep single packs, four-packs and eight-packs as distinct offers with correct whole-pack rounding, purchased grams, item prices, shipping conditions and totals. Removing the variant feature does not merge or duplicate SKUs, pack sizes, cart discounts or service-specific policies.
- Retain original vendor product wording and any raw listing identity metadata in evidence/optional offer details if useful. Do not invent a manufacturer blend or relabel an unstated listing as Classico to make it eligible. Raw wording is provenance, not a default ranking filter or repeated variant badge.
- Remove implicit variant filtering from the default API/quote flow, not just its visible widget. Old shared URLs containing variant=classico/unspecified/etc must still preserve product/quantity/locality but resolve to this unified comparison; discard or ignore the obsolete variant parameter without creating a second view.
- Update AGENTS.md, catalog/public API where appropriate, docs and browser QA so they no longer instruct variant separation. Verify that the single product comparison can include Coffee4U alongside the other Crema e Gusto listings, still names vendors correctly, calculates packs/shipping honestly and has no residual blend control/warning. Existing stock, policy-scope, unknown-shipping and retired-product safeguards remain mandatory.

The active catalog remains Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee only; Oro, Rossa, Suerte and other product lines stay excluded. The home is still the product index with one real card. Keep the Canton Zürich design system, Inter and established semantic palette. Shurik writes the code/tests; the overseer only steers and reviews.

## Overseer acceptance findings — finish the matcher and measure the real viewport (2026-10-13 04:05 UTC)

Address these two remaining defects before more unchanged evidence reruns. The 3-85 scope/readability work and 3-87/3-88 contrast/capture checks are useful, but passing QA counts do not establish these acceptance points.

- **Match the discount and paid subtotal too.** The current `freeCartConditionMatches()` ignores `condition.discountPercent` and `condition.paidItemTotalIls`. The actual function still matches `singles-8` when the promotion ends (8 × ₪33 = ₪264 paid, no discount) or changes to 5% (₪250.80 paid), although the recorded cart was 10% / ₪237.60 paid. Enforce all required observed cart fields, including the paid amount and discount state, and do not treat missing required SKU/method values as matching confirmed ones. The changed/ended-promotion carts must keep the published ₪25 base rate unless new scoped browser evidence supports free delivery. Preserve the recorded carts, the separate eight-pack quote, expiry/conflict handling and honest read-time migration; Shurik writes the code and meaningful regression checks.
- **Measure a real 390×844 content viewport and require complete critical warnings.** Setting the WebDriver outer window to 390×844 currently produces `innerHeight: 701`. The live 2 kg failed-check warning starts at y=673 and ends at y=724; requiring only `failureRect.top <= innerHeight` lets a cut-off sentence pass. Set/verify the requested content viewport, use its actual `window.innerHeight` as the limit (no `Math.max(innerHeight, 844)` fallback), and require the full decision values, named delivery method, failure sentence and necessary concise conditional/coverage warning to end inside it. Keep secondary terms behind disclosure; do not hide the failure or coverage uncertainty to make a check pass.
- The saved live "cropped card" is 343×416 — exactly the visible intersection of the card with the 701 px viewport — and also cuts off the failure sentence. Save a genuinely complete readable affected-card view plus the correctly sized first-screen view. A crop or a warning's top edge is not evidence that its full text is visible. Inspect readable desktop/mobile home and product captures; accurately retain the pinned image-reader limitation rather than claiming pixel maps are native image review.
- Continue the shared-URL normalization already checkpointed in 3-89 and its appropriate checks. Preserve the concise one-card home, full-width readable locality, one unified Crema e Gusto comparison, separate packs, named method records, Canton Zürich/Inter palette and all existing safety/provenance requirements. Do not spend another iteration merely repeating unchanged totals or adding source-level guards while these two implementation defects remain.

## Overseer review follow-up — bind cart evidence to its actual scope, then finish shopping readability (2026-10-13)

This is review feedback under the existing owner shipping/UX brief, not a change to the one-product/no-blend correction above. Address the evidence-scope defect first in the next fresh iteration. Shurik implements the changes and tests; the overseer edits only this brief.

- **Do not infer a monotone CoffeeMan threshold from sampled carts.** The 3-82 policy makes every eligible single/4-pack cart at or above ₪231 free, with no cart-size cap. The vendor publishes no such threshold. Observing free courier for 7 singles (₪231), 8 singles (₪264 before the 10% promotion / ₪237.60 after it), and two 4-packs (₪248) does not establish free delivery for every larger or otherwise unobserved cart. Calling this inference "conservative" does not prove it. Preserve the correct, explicitly conditional results for those observed cart configurations, and the separate one-eight-pack ₪20 quote; represent the free observations with validated SKU/pack count, whole-pack quantity, item-subtotal/discount, named-method, destination-evidence and review scope. Outside the verified scope, retain the published base fee or explicit unresolved condition instead of inventing zero shipping. A general threshold is acceptable only with a new published rule or browser evidence that actually supports the stated range and limits. Do not add unrelated products or infer a universal CoffeeMan rule.
- Verify that the saved cart examples still reproduce their recorded fees, while an unobserved larger cart (for example 3 kg of singles or three 4-packs) cannot inherit free delivery merely because its subtotal exceeds ₪231. Check expired/conflicting evidence and price/promotion changes too. Keep read-time enrichment honest: no price/stock/observedAt/lastRefreshAt advance, no stretching the eight-pack quote, and no merging distinct packs/SKUs.
- The Coffee4U extractor now correctly records ₪76 + ₪30 = ₪106 for Jerusalem, Haifa and Be’er Sheva. Keep that fix. However, those common evidence records still carry `service: null` despite a successful step selecting door-to-door delivery. Record the actual confirmed method in the reusable evidence schema and preserve method/quantity/destination restrictions through policy interpretation and public quote output. Retain exact public-flow blockers when a required field or quote genuinely cannot be obtained; an extractor failure is not a vendor restriction.
- After the scope fix, finish the outstanding shopping readability work: the home card still repeats a long explanation of how comparison works, and the mobile locality label is clipped. Make the one-card index concise and the selected locality readable. Preserve the dedicated/shareable product route, quantity/locality state, all eligible Crema e Gusto listings, native keyboard disclosures and necessary stock/failure/conditional/stale warnings.
- Inspect and save readable views of the affected offer, not just the page top. Cover both 500 g and the 2 kg CoffeeMan winner on mobile (including the real last-check-failed state), with the actual vendor, accurate purchased packs/grams, item subtotal, named shipping method/charge and delivered total visible in the first 390×844 viewport. Save desktop/home views too. If the pinned PNG reader still rejects images, say so; DOM geometry and pixel maps are not native image inspection. Do not relaunch identical quote probes as a substitute for the scope/UI implementation.

Keep last-known-good observations and visible failure warnings; do not bypass vendor controls or administer Cloudflare. The next scheduled production retry is 06:17 UTC, so work on the scoped evidence and shopping UI rather than claiming a separate retry at the backoff-due timestamp.

## Current owner priorities — product index, reusable shipping knowledge, progressive disclosure (2026-10-12)

The owner has reviewed the updated website and still finds it very cluttered. The home page must become an overview index of products, with the comparison workflow on a dedicated product page. The owner also expects obvious browser-visible shipping rules, such as Pucks free shipping above ₪100, to be found systematically and actually used by the site. These priorities replace the earlier instruction to repeat the initial shipping investigation first in every fresh iteration. The first Pucks/CoffeeMan/Coffee4U browser investigation is already evidenced in iterations 3-67 through 3-72. Use that evidence; fresh browser work should address a specific missing, contradictory or stale condition. Do not spend whole iterations reproducing unchanged amounts while the requested product/UI work waits.

Shurik implements all code, assets, tests and documentation. The overseer only changes this brief and reviews results. Keep the Canton Zürich design direction, Inter, palette and Crema e Gusto-only active scope below.

### 1. Make the home page a product overview index

- The canonical home route must show a clean product index, not the full vendor comparison board. Render its cards from the active catalog. Today that means **one real card: Lavazza Crema e Gusto vacuum-packed ground coffee**. Design the structure to support additional products later, but do not add or reactivate Oro, Rossa, Suerte, other product lines, fabricated offerings or placeholder cards. Crema e Gusto offers share one comparison; pack sizes and multipacks remain distinct.
- Each product card links to a real, directly loadable product-detail URL. The home page needs only product identity, a concise useful summary and a clear way to open the comparison. If a summary price is shown, its quantity, destination, freshness and conditional nature must be understandable; do not mix different cart sizes into a misleading "from" price.
- The product page identifies the coffee and provides the quantity/locality/delivery controls and offers. Provide a clear "All products" way back. Preserve shareable selection state and handle existing product/query links, including retired-line fallbacks, without losing quantity or locality; obsolete variant parameters are ignored. - The home title is "Attention shoppers" without a period. The product-detail heading should name the product, e.g. "Lavazza Crema e Gusto", with compact site branding. Do not reproduce a giant branding hero or comparison explanation on both pages.

controls, so it could not evidence the first screen after loading the product URL. The card capture itself

  to 390×844 it scrolls back to that exact position. A later capture can no longer silently become a
  scrolled card view.

  viewport enlargement**: it resets scroll explicitly (`window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'instant' })`),

  DOM state to be exactly the requested 390×844 with `scrollY === 0` (`exact: true`). Every first-screen
